---
_**A Special Message from our Sponsor**_ _Please note that views expressed in this message do not necessarily reflect those of_ _Free Speech Daily_ _and do not constitute an endorsement or recommendation by Free Speech Daily_ _._
---
| BRAVE For Good We don’t have the millions behind us like the giant taxpayer-funded ALA. | | | | | Friend, If you haven’t heard about “See You at the Library Day” on Fox News or Newsmax or your other favorite news sources, **[please let me tell you why it’s so critical.](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5OTV9AAwAAAAAAuCwn2AMaR8zjLHNJUdIIA4DJ-UstwcdIKcKyspcZMyckizdTfWDQrfVUDNig7fLMEtCIdRSCCTdKSF-lg41IIT7Z9xxp3qYgEeFMH2mjg)** Back when you were growing up, you may remember lazy Saturdays at the library with a kind but stern librarian. She would fill your mind with classics like _Pat the Bunny_ and _The Little Engine That Could_. And eventually you got old enough to roam by yourself and discover adventures like the _Three Musketeers_ , _Treasure Island_ and _Charlotte’s Web_. **But today, all that has changed.** Instead of filling children with wholesome stories, the president of the American Library Association (ALA) says libraries should be used to address ‘systemic racism’ and elevate ‘BIPOC and GLBTQR+ writers and voices.’ Radical librarians call _Adventures of Huckleberry Finn_ and _To Kill a Mockingbird_ “racist.” They’ve stripped Laura Ingalls Wilder’s name from a prestigious book award because of her “problematic’ _Little House_ series. And they bring in men wearing full makeup, dresses, and high heels for “Drag Queen Story Hours” where books like these are read to children of all ages... _A is for Activist._ An ABC board book for “families who want their kids to grow up in a space that is unapologetic about activism, environmental justice, civil rights, LGBTQ rights, and everything else that activists believe in and fight for.” _Woke Baby._ “For all the littlest progressives, waking up to seize a new day of justice and activism. Woke babies raise their fists in the air. Woke babies cry out for justice. Woke babies grow up to change the world.” _Prince and Knight._ The “premier queer-friendly fairy tale” about a prince who marries a knight instead of a princess. And _The Hips on the Drag Queens Go Swish, Swish, Swish._ A “family-friendly celebration of drag” that encourages children to “work it.” I wish I could tell you this was only happening in places like New York City and San Francisco...but that’s just not true.
---
[](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5OTV9AAwAAAAAAuCwn2AN5HRSeC1h5g8oZTcFpUuqaavUtT7sYROkp2YCiDWpNnPY2bABzrru8-eCRwsJMenXrDOVtHdNDoeD0s6ZV5cOIK9q23ggPbmUBQ)
---
THIS IS A MAN leading “Drag Queen Story Hour”
---
**[That’s why parents and grandparents across the country are rising up through See You At The Library Day.](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5OTV9AAwAAAAAAuCwn2AO0-WEwYA6XfNyO86fv3s25QWEYTdyqQ-5etPCnmp8osQ9howQJbPmsL9nubsa6ofW3pi_de5b2W9RVUBCpceGK0Y7tQjKuC-qJg)** For decades, the ultra-liberal Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation and George Soros’ Open Society have spent millions radicalizing the ALA.**And as a result, a new generation of pink-haired, activist librarians have made it their mission to fill library shelves with anti-American, LGBTQ-friendly, and explicitly sexual content.** Maybe you’ve noticed all the displays at your own library celebrating Pride Month or elevating ‘the environment’ to a type of religion. Or maybe you’ve noticed the “Teen Zone” which is really meant to be a “parent-free” zone. The “Teen Zone” is filled with books like: _Rick_ about a cross-dressing Grandpa, _Melissa_ filled with graphic nudity, and _Darkstalker_ featuring gory violence and domestic abuse. **But here’s what’s really alarming.** We can’t just sit back and say, “Well, I’ll just make sure my family doesn’t go to “Drag Queen Story Hour” and we won’t check out those inappropriate books.” That may be good for your family -- for now. **But meanwhile, the ALA uses our taxpayer-funded libraries to lure in millions of _other_ children who grow up to be the very activists who are destroying our country and conservative values!** _**[I hope you see why I need your help today.](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5OTV9AAwAAAAAAuCwn2APgfuu6H-EmEqiFwc_lwFaYbhmjWvAVGda52aGjoKGhHVMoay7jSoo83jTPEC3jyZQzqoR4wbSikHgngeaycas6YLcKNEU0xB1rg) **_ My name is Kirk Cameron. Maybe you recognize me from the 1980’s family sitcom “Growing Pains” or from my work in inspirational movies like “Fireproof” and “Left Behind.” I know firsthand how dangerous it is to be indoctrinated by leftist values. Pride almost took me down as a young actor in Hollywood. But the gospel saved me. I love being an actor, but what’s far more important is being a husband, dad, grandad, and a Christian. When I saw what book publishers and libraries were doing to indoctrinate children with anti-God, anti-family, anti-America messages, I knew I had a duty to take action. So, I wrote a little book called “As You Grow” to teach children how to grow in wisdom through the fruit of the spirit. **Then I decided to go one step further and counter those awful “Drag Queen Story Hours” with _conservative Story Hours_ filled with the classic books you and I grew up with, plus new wholesome books like mine that captivate children with lessons in bravery, honesty, kindness, and patriotism.**And boy, the ALA and radical librarians didn’t like that one bit.
---
* Over 50 libraries rejected my request to host our Story Hour.

---
* The ALA helped local libraries scheme ways to keep me out including booking all the event rooms for themselves.

---
* Social media blew up with attacks: I was compared to a Nazi (that’s original), my publisher was accused of trying to “confuse and demoralize children,” supporters were described as “bored moms/busybodies who need something to feel good about,” and on and on.

---
I can’t even print most things these radicals said because it’s so vile. In the end I got two libraries to reverse course by reminding them that their censorship violated the Constitution of the United States. **And thousands of parents and grandparents brought their little ones to those “Story Hours” where we pledged allegiance to the flag, sang “God Bless America”, and read wholesome and Godly books.** It was incredible. But here’s the greatest part... From there, parents and grandparents started asking how they could host “Story Hours” of their own. And that’s how the nationwide “See You at the Library” movement was born. Last year, committed conservatives just like you booked event rooms at 201 libraries in 46 states. On the same day, across America hundreds of “Story Hours” filled children’s hearts with goodness, gratitude, and God. Conservative parents, grandparents, and patriots stood together for a very simple mission -- to reject the Left’s radical ideas and reclaim childhood innocence in America’s libraries. **[And this year, honoring America’s 250th birthday, my ambitious goal is to expand “See You at the Library Day” to reach 250,000 children.](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5OTV9AAwAAAAAAuCwn2AQrYqMWdR79BwVaUTFly7MO0S2zll1KZscont3yUX3aFNiS-V4cz_VJ8lZuflFm7PaNhaIg-0Ut04MFBwK8mu8781WFFt5T4K2kw)** The exact date will soon be announced. And before then, I need you! The response from parents, grandparents, and patriots who want to host “Story Hours” has been overwhelming. That’s a very good thing. | | | **_The war that began on September 11th never ended. It relocated. It moved onto the American college quad, and a Gulf monarchy has been helping pay the rent while the media encouraged "tolerance". That money is blurring our memories and weakening the resolve of young generations.

_**Friday marks twenty-five years since the towers came down. You remember the morning: where you were standing, who you called, the strange silence in the sky once they grounded every plane. We were told, again and again, that we would never forget. But many of us did.

**_One poll found, "Millennials are more likely than other generations to associate the 9/11 period with mistreatment of Muslims and minority groups."

_**Start with what happened on our own soil last year. By the FBI's own 2024 hate-crime data, there were **1,938 anti-Jewish hate crimes** , the most since the Bureau began keeping count in 1991.

**_Jews are 2% of America, but victims of 70% of religiously motivated hate crimes.

_**Counting more broadly, the Anti-Defamation League counted its highest tally since it started counting in 1979. That is **more than twenty-five a day** , every day, in the USA. Now follow the money. Qatar has poured **$7.7 billion** into American universities since 1986, more than any other foreign government on earth. Last year alone, Doha sent over a billion dollars, ** _one of every five foreign dollars that landed on American campuses.

_**You'll notice that antisemitic incidents on those same campuses jumped **84%****in a single year.** The money and the hatred are not on separate pages.**_

_**A 2023 poll asked whether "the Hamas killing of 1200 Israeli civilians and the kidnapping of another 250 civilians can be justified by the grievances of Palestinians." Among 18-to-24-year-olds,**60% said it can be justified

****_Six in ten 18-to-24-year-olds thought October 7th could be justified.

_** None of this required a foreign army. It required **foreign money, a willing faculty lounge, and a country too polite to say out loud what it knows to be true**.

Twenty-five years ago we swore we would remember. Remembering is not a moment of silence. It is refusing to let anyone, in a cave, a lecture hall, or a donor's checkbook in Doha, teach our grandchildren to call September 11th a two-sided story. We defined American resilience on 9/12. That is the state of play. It's time to call it out.

**_What can a rugged individual do about it?
_**

subject: Can we change human nature?
body:
Is human nature fixed, or can it be changed? That question lies at the heart of some of the most consequential ideas in history.

This sponsored message from Inside Scoop Politics is on behalf of Hillsdale College
| | | [](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckUuK3DAQQE8j72z082_hxRBPw0B6QtKLZGcqUrVdoB-WNHP90KRzgWzfK15B1c_rdgVyFPZ38LhQzpuNdjMQPtEcEHY8qocQoNQTN8nl0PK5FXwDU-gDNw2NXXoppvvU4CLGaeZaTFo3xyLV3GtrQN1RSA7ItZy5NP04mkmK-d7Q8ujxWXAhueays7Pq57EHIcQMw_CbaV6ThYIdhUwWs4kxpeiokMldPPfGLUcpKTP1wuSFyUtGU0_sDnIuW3DYoa1MXmwMUPDha0rxLG05sCVHYJm6ZNw9hvIlWmRq5YoL9c6lll9f1_Xb-vp6Y3KoxW851tM8RtIZc0JTKOxP5dFS9Uyt6IHcExrwCWgPTK1_Vz1xDAVDYWq9vvz49Xa7bt_H9u12a_8dozkXmz7JOcrDyDTfH83ORN-U__rPxyL_BAAA__8m5Z5k)

| | Dear Fellow American, **Is human nature fixed, or can it be changed?** That question lies at the heart of some of the most consequential ideas in history. Karl Marx believed that if society could be upended, mankind itself could be remade. That promise inspired revolutionary movements throughout the twentieth century—with catastrophic consequences, as communist regimes claimed the lives of more than 100 million people. **Sadly, we’re seeing a resurgence of this destructive ideology right here in the United States.** But anyone who’s read Homer understands something far different. Nearly **3,000 years ago** , _The Iliad_ portrayed men and women with the same hopes, fears, loves, jealousies, ambitions, courage, and grief that we recognize today. Open its pages, and you discover something remarkable: **Human nature has not changed.** Near the end of the poem, King Priam of Troy enters the camp of Achilles, the warrior who killed his beloved son Hector. The old king kneels before his enemy and begs for his son’s body. Achilles thinks of his own aging father, and both men weep together. Every parent understands that scene. Every son can understand it. Across three millennia, Homer reminds us that what is deepest in human nature remains the same. That is why _The Iliad_ has endured as one of the foundational works of Western civilization. And it is one reason Hillsdale College created our free online course, **“The Iliad.”** The course introduces students to truths about courage, honor, sacrifice, friendship, justice, and duty—truths that every generation must rediscover if liberty is to endure. Those same truths also expose the false promise behind every utopian ideology: **that human nature can somehow be perfected simply by changing politics or economics.** **Will you make a tax-deductible gift today to help us introduce 100,000 Americans to these timeless lessons through Hillsdale’s free online course on _The Iliad_?** Will you help? Your gift of $25, $50, $100, or even $200 or more will go a long way toward this effort. **Please make your best, tax-deductible gift today using this secure link:** [**https://secure.hillsdale.edu/donate/support-the-iliad**](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckUuK3DAQQE8j72z082_hxRBPw0B6QtKLZGcqUrVdoB-WNHP90KRzgWzfK15B1c_rdgVyFPZ38LhQzpuNdjMQPtEcEHY8qocQoNQTN8nl0PK5FXwDU-gDNw2NXXoppvvU4CLGaeZaTFo3xyLV3GtrQN1RSA7ItZy5NP04mkmK-d7Q8ujxWXAhueays7Pq57EHIcQMw_CbaV6ThYIdhUwWs4kxpeiokMldPPfGLUcpKTP1wuSFyUtGU0_sDnIuW3DYoa1MXmwMUPDha0rxLG05sCVHYJm6ZNw9hvIlWmRq5YoL9c6lll9f1_Xb-vp6Y3KoxW851tM8RtIZc0JTKOxP5dFS9Uyt6IHcExrwCWgPTK1_Vz1xDAVDYWq9vvz49Xa7bt_H9u12a_8dozkXmz7JOcrDyDTfH83ORN-U__rPxyL_BAAA__8m5Z5k) Today, more young Americans express favorable views of socialism than at any time in recent decades. Too many have never encountered the great books that reveal why attempts to remake human nature have always failed. **Education is the answer.** Through more than **50 free online courses** , Hillsdale College is introducing millions of Americans to the principles of liberty and the enduring truths of Western civilization. Like everything we do, this course was created **without accepting a single penny of taxpayer funding—not even indirect funding through student grants and loans.** That independence allows Hillsdale to teach the truth without political interference. But it also means we rely entirely on friends like you to carry these lessons to the Americans who need them most. Thank you for standing with Hillsdale College as we pursue truth, defend liberty, and help another generation discover one of civilization’s greatest books. Warm regards, Bill Gray ’01

Institutional Advancement
Hillsdale College

disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY SENATE CONSERVATIVES ACTION AND NOT AUTHORIZED BY ANY CANDIDATE OR CANDIDATE'S COMMITTEE
body:
Our national debt just hit $40 TRILLION — with a T.

| | | |
#
---
---
|
---
Our national debt just hit **$40 TRILLION** — with a T.

The federal government now spends more than **$1 TRILLION A YEAR** just on interest. Not defense. Not the border. Not a single thing you'll ever see or use. Just for interest. And it's set to double again within the next decade. That's your tax dollars, gone, before Washington spends a cent on anything that matters.

Senator Rick Scott (R-FL) said what conservatives have been saying for decades: **Congress needs to STOP SPENDING and BALANCE THE BUDGET!** He's right, and he's one of the only people in Washington with the guts to say it out loud.

**Here's the part nobody wants to admit: the Fed didn't do this to us._Congress did._ Politicians want to pass the blame to someone else when it's their fault. You cannot print, borrow, and spend $40 trillion and then blame the guys who have to finance it. **

And don't buy the line that we'll "grow our way out of it." That's not a plan. That's Washington-speak to keep spending and hope for the best. It won't work because it can't. This is a spending problem, plain and simple, and they only get fixed one way — by tightening your belt.

Voting for anyone with an R next to their name won't get the job done. Most of these Senators never saw a spending bill they wouldn't vote for. The earmarks keep flowing. The omnibus bills keep passing at 2:00 a.m. What really matters is the kind of Republicans we send to Washington.

This is why **Senate Conservatives Action** exists — to change Washington by changing the people we send there.

We don't back candidates just because they wear a Republican jersey. We back real leaders with the backbone to make the hard decisions, to fight for the policies we desperately need to save this country. **We only back candidates who will say NO to out-of-control spending — NO on the earmarks, NO on the late-night omnibus bills, and NO on business as usual.**

Here are the conservative Senate candidates you should support in the 2026 midterm elections: ✅ **Ken Paxton** — Texas
✅ **Mike Collins** — Georgia
✅ **Roger Marshall** — Kansas
✅ **Ashley Moody** — Florida
✅ **Harriet Hageman** — Wyoming
✅ **Kevin Hern** — Oklahoma
✅ **Barry Moore** — Alabama
✅ **Bill Hagerty** — Tennessee Election day is just 2 months away! If you were planning to help conservative candidates this cycle, now is the time to do it. [**Chip in $25 or more right now and help us elect conservatives who will fight to end government fraud and cut spending.**](https://email.editor.goppresidential.com/c/eJyckEFuwyAQRU-Dd7GGMR7MgkWlyrt026U1MZOEygELaNrevrJ6g-6_nt5_7-flzHGL6fbGD_G3vO9LqYuBVuK2xZyKcM2ptnyN3-0uCwLSCdxJw8Jri09ZDHfBGyZDRJ14bScHBkew3d0jsRBdLBOC00bbizWjBS1oxLrJddEfQHAaNOoRxn7Scr2QhhAIheSqDEiILZf-cCtSY5DUIm_9mh_d5u-t7VUNLwpnhXOV9bNIXyVxk8Mvp2OncC4_bkgK56CGeVXD65Q4f4x1x7UrPuxfx9tKVhm4PTj-0dt_ezw9_gYAAP__8oZvQA) $40 trillion isn't just a talking point. It's a currency crisis with the fuse already lit — and time is running out. Please join us in this fight and send the big spenders in Washington a message they cannot ignore.

Today we honor his legacy

| | | | [ ](https://links.fryforsc.com/els/v4/gotglehiicnpmsli6wy1c/Y2dNXQv33Usijcz8nLgTbnJnoPLNadSGX063CZKK7n_gkGqtcqYYgEVFN4S9h6bUqy_k/MkrYcxYDcBS9pPrkKLspKbotHE-zDwxFpcZ1r_O8UH_HWaQPprYgrXtclA28l1ZD5CGiXWPHelhqvldn_hlMvKIuJGKY872JsIYBblvjtU6xkGd6bYtlx7h_z4XO1N9K6DVDEDqG5MAoQt5h01sJwdzMt6XYfVDMnFUiVk3kG9E-q93LsovD2UGZc5lhopyLUexxKmP1cK40xdvR)

| | Peter, One year ago today, on September 10, 2025, America lost one of its most courageous, inspiring, and tireless voices for freedom - **_Charlie Kirk_.** As we mark this solemn anniversary, our hearts remain with his family, his loved ones, and the millions of young Americans whose lives were forever changed by his leadership. **Charlie was more than an activist; he was a leader who believed deeply in the promise of the American Republic.** From a young age, he dedicated his life to equipping the next generation with the courage to stand up for conservative principles, constitutional liberties, and free speech. He showed a generation of young people that their voices matter and that America’s best days are worth fighting for. While his passing was a tragic moment in our nation’s history, Charlie’s mission did not end one year ago. **Today, his spirit of bold truth and unwavering faith lives on in millions of students across South Carolina and all 50 states who continue to stand up for faith, family, and freedom.** Today, we pause to honor his memory, reflect on his extraordinary legacy, and renew our commitment to the conservative principles he championed every single day. **Please join me today in keeping Charlie’s family in your thoughts and prayers.** -Russell Fry
---
---
---
|
* * *
---
| | **_Meet Russell:_** Born and raised in Surfside Beach, SC, Congressman Russell Fry is the proud and homegrown Representative for South Carolina’s 7th Congressional District. Growing up in a cinder block home with no heating or air conditioning, Russell learned at an early age that hard work and perseverance pave the only true path to the American Dream. He watched his parents work day in and day out to make ends meet. And the values they instilled in him during his upbringing led Russell to self-fund both his undergraduate education at the University of South Carolina, and later his law studies at the Charleston School of Law. At Charleston, Russell served as the President of the Student Bar Association and even helped the school achieve its American Bar Association accreditation. He went on to practice law in the Grand Strand area for over a decade before entering the political arena to serve in the South Carolina House of Representatives for State House District 106 (Horry County). During his seven-year tenure in the SC House, Russell fought to safeguard Constitutional liberties, lower taxes, and put the best interests of South Carolina families above all else. He climbed the ranks to become Chief Majority Whip, and also chaired the House Opioid Prevention Study Committee. Under Russell’s leadership, 18 policy initiatives to combat the opioid crisis were signed into law. Since the first day he stepped foot in Washington, Russell has strived to shake up the corrupt status quo and deliver real change for the American people. He believes adamantly that so long as the American people stand united, we can keep the American Dream alive for every citizen of our great nation. Russell is a dedicated husband to his wife, Bronwen, and a loving father to his son, James. The family lives in Murrells Inlet with their chocolate lab, Jasper.

subject: Read my latest on Substack: ONE YEAR SINCE CHARLIE HAS BEEN GONE
body:
| | |

| |

| | It’s hard to believe it’s been a year. A year since Charlie Kirk was assassinated in front of 3,000 people on a college campus. The horrific images and replays went viral around the world for weeks. A year since a husband and father was taken from his family. A year since I lost a friend. A year since online ghouls began mocking his death — and some still do.I first met Charlie seven years ago. This was before everything got as big as it did. name: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez
subject: Rev. Frederick Haynes
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez for Congress
body:
#
For far too long, our political system has been dominated by corporate power and special interests. The result is that what is seen as “possible” in Washington is more about what works for the wealthy and powerful, and not what’s best for the working class who built this country.
We have the power to change this — but it is going to take electing fighters to Congress who are actually a part of the communities they represent and who run campaigns that are not funded by corporate PAC donations.
**That’s why I am proud to announce I’m endorsing Rev. Frederick D. Haynes III to represent TX-30.**
Rev. Frederick D. Haynes III has been a pastor in his community for 40 years. He is running on a platform of Medicare for All and economic justice. He refuses corporate PAC money — so we know that he won’t be beholden to special interests.
**Can we all come together to throw Frederick Haynes our support?**
[ Please split a donation of any amount between our campaigns today, so Frederick can reach voters all throughout Dallas before November 3rd.](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-20260910-haynes.PRYXTp&refcode=em20260910-12264-P_FND_SPL_END&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=3&akid=12264%2E2526796%2E2uyCm3)
Rev. Haynes knows that our government can and must serve working people — whether in New York, Texas, or elsewhere — to bring about a better future for all.
We both believe it is a moral failure that anyone in the richest country on earth fears the financial cost of getting sick or needing an operation and we will fight together for Medicare for All.
And we both believe that ICE must be abolished and that our immigration system must be rooted in principles of humanity.
I know Rev. Haynes will bring his spirit of service to his community to the halls of Congress. But first we need to help his campaign reach voters all throughout Texas’ 30th district.
[ With just 54 days until Election Day, will you split a $5 donation between our campaigns so we can get Frederick to Congress where we will fight for a better future together?](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-20260910-haynes.PRYXTp&refcode=em20260910-12264-P_FND_SPL_END&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=4&akid=12264%2E2526796%2E2uyCm3)

# Dr. Stephen Skoly Issues Statement on Rhode Island’s Second Congressional District Primary
“An election may end a campaign, but it does not end our responsibility to serve.”
**Cranston, R.I.** — Dr. Stephen Skoly released the following statement regarding the Rhode Island Second Congressional District primary: “Last night, Republican and unaffiliated voters in Rhode Island’s Second Congressional District made their choice. While this is not the outcome we worked for, I respect the voters’ decision at this time. “I entered this race for the same reason I have spent nearly four decades serving Rhode Islanders: I believe service requires showing up, telling the truth and standing firm when it matters. “We ran a campaign rooted in experience, accountability, constitutional freedom and a deep commitment to the people of Rhode Island. We did not compromise our principles, and I am proud of the campaign we ran. “To my wife, Carol, my family, friends and our volunteers, donors and every voter who placed their trust in me: thank you. Your faith, friendship and hard work will never be forgotten. “An election may end a campaign, but it does not end our responsibility to serve. I will continue standing up for patients, taxpayers, small businesses, working families, seniors, veterans and every Rhode Islander who believes government must answer to the people. “I leave this race with my head held high, my principles intact and my gratitude for Rhode Island deeper than ever. “The work continues. “Onward.” ###

clean_body: | | | | | Senate Republicans recently announced that they have no plans to spend party money to help conservative Ken Paxton win the U.S. Senate race in Texas. "We in the Senate don't have the money budgeted for Texas. We need help from the president," said Senator John Kennedy (R-LA). Republican Leader John Thune (R-SD) later confirmed the plan to abandon Paxton financially and deflected responsibility to the president. "I'm hoping the White House will become engaged; Texas is an incredibly expensive state," Thune said. What makes this so infuriating is that the Senate GOP spent over $100 million attacking Ken Paxton in the Republican primary. They had plenty of money to spend on Texas when they were trying to defeat a conservative, but when it comes to defeating a Marxist like James Talarico, they’ve got nothing. You would think that since they spent so much against the party's eventual nominee, they would feel some obligation to help him now. This race is competitive because they hurt Paxton in the primary. It should be on them, not President Trump, to clean up their mess. You break it, you own it. Sadly, that's not going to happen. You may hear party leaders say they "hope" Ken Paxton wins and they "hope" President Trump helps him, but they have closed their wallets and are quietly rooting for him to lose. They don't want another conservative in the Senate who will hold them accountable, and they would love to tell everyone that Ken Paxton was a bad candidate who cost them the majority, even though they're the ones who kneecapped and left him for dead. Friend,

As a grandfather, I find it deeply concerning to think that paper transgender dolls could be used to indoctrinate children in public elementary schools.

**I am calling for an immediate investigation into this “MyGender Dolls” project.**

We need leaders who will cut off federal funding for these kinds of projects, restore parental rights, and ensure that public schools focus on learning real topics, not this gender identity stuff.

Folks,
Throughout this campaign, I've kept you updated on where this race stands, how I'm feeling about it, and what it's going to take to win this U.S. Senate seat. Today, I wanted to take a different peek behind the curtain and show you exactly how Michael Whatley's campaign is trying to win.
Whatley knows that he can't win this race on policy (higher prices), his bio (lied about where he grew up), his record (as a Big Oil and utility company lobbyist), or his judgment (giving a big political job to a convicted child sex predator) so he's resorted to attacking Roy with blatant lies. Here's what's happening.
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/94bb7018-a61a-4134-b29b-57ee4abb540f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Whatley and his allies have launched a series of attack ads spreading false information about Roy and this campaign.
In August, the Senate Leadership Fund (SLF), the GOP super PAC dedicated to electing Republicans to the Senate, released two ads attacking Roy citing tragic murders. But both ads wrongfully associate them with Roy's record as Governor. **Independent fact checkers have determined both ads to be a lie -- one of the crimes didn't even take place in North Carolina.**
But these PACs that are bankrolling Whatley and trying to buy this U.S. Senate seat don't have to answer to voters and they don't have to tell the truth. And last week, the Supreme Court just made it a lot easier for Republicans to floor the airwaves with more misleading ads.
**Now, billionaires and the GOP will receive a massive TV ad discount, further eroding the power of everyday people.**
As the former RNC Chair, Whatley will be first in line to benefit from the RNC's $130 million war chest to bail out his flailing campaign. And this decision will make it a lot easier for him to continue running a campaign defined by so much manipulation and deceit that he doesn't even have time to focus on the issues that actually matter to North Carolinians.
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/94bb7018-a61a-4134-b29b-57ee4abb540f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
This November, we believe the choice in this race is very clear: a dedicated public servant with a record of fighting for North Carolinians or a Big Oil and utility company lobbyist who only cares about lining his own pockets and answering to Trump.
We know that we can't outspend Whatley and his DC GOP puppeteers. But we can out-organize them.
We have less than 54 days before early voting starts and less than 35 days until Election Day. And we are not wasting a single moment.
From now until polls close, we're knocking on every door, showing up in every community and making sure that every eligible voter in this state has a plan to cast their ballot.
And we need your help to do so.
Will you [chip in $5](https://substack.com/redirect/94bb7018-a61a-4134-b29b-57ee4abb540f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) today or [sign up](https://substack.com/redirect/112281f2-79a5-4fa5-a2d0-81da397f4b95?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for a canvassing shift? Every effort matters in this people-powered movement.
Thank you for standing with us in this fight.
Jeff

It's really simple, Peter. Mike Lawler votes with Donald Trump 100% of the time. Today he is on stage at Trump’s midterm convention in Dallas, to nationally stand up as one of the faces of the MAGA agenda. **And Trump is immediately rewarding him by deploying his super PAC to NY-17 this week.** [I need your help to fight back against the dark money flooding this race. This is a Clinton-Biden-Harris district.
NY-17 has never voted for Trump. But Lawler knows that Trump’s dark money is his best bet at winning reelection.
And it isn’t just Trump. Last week, Elon Musk officially jumped into our race and began hitting us with attack ads.
Over the last year, the Supreme Court has systematically peeled back protections against dark money in our politics, making it easier for campaigns to coordinate with super PACs.
**So we are in the fight of our lives. Republicans are going to outspend us.**
We will not match Lawler, Trump, and Elon Musk dollar-for-dollar. We don’t need to. What we need to do is run a smarter, more effective operation. So my team has been going over our budget with a fine tooth comb, looking for ways to stretch our dollar.
What we’ve been doing is working. But with less than 55 days until the Election, I’m counting on this grassroots team to help us keep our foot on the gas.
[Please, if you can, chip in $10 or even $17 to my campaign to flip NY-17. body:
Last week, we learned that the Department of the Interior plans to break ground on Trump’s “triumphal” arch just outside the gates of Arlington later this month.
#
Peter,
My name is Karen Meredith, and I am a Gold Star mother. My son is one of more than 400,000 buried at Arlington National Cemetery.
My only child, 1LT Ken Ballard, joined the Army after graduating high school in 1995. As an Army granddaughter, Army daughter, Army sister, and Army mom, I couldn't have been more proud of his decision.
My son deployed to Iraq in May of 2003, and 384 days later he was killed while fighting an Iranian-backed militia in Najaf. He had been scheduled to return home one month earlier, but his tour was extended.
For families like mine, Arlington is more than a cemetery. It is where Ken is at eternal peace. It is a place an entire country comes to express its gratitude for a debt that cannot be repaid.
Donald Trump wants to destroy that peace. Last week, we learned that the Department of the Interior plans to break ground on Trump’s “triumphal” arch just outside the gates of Arlington later this month.
Trump never served. He called my son and all who served alongside him “suckers” and “losers." He trampled the graves of the fallen in Section 60 for a campaign photo opportunity. That same man would use their graves as the backdrop for his own vanity project.
The indignity of this arch is difficult to put into words, but I am grateful to have an outlet for resisting it in my work with VoteVets. They are building a nationwide mobilization against this arch, and I’d be grateful if you could contribute to support them.

body:
Do you recognize the little girl in this photo?

[ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/15818?t=1001&akid=1855%2E181023%2EFYkUbw ]Jocelyn Benson as a child with her parents.

That’s me! Back then, growing up in a working-class family, I don’t think
anyone looked at me and thought, “that’s Michigan’s future Secretary of
State,” let alone that I would one day be running for governor.

While politics wasn’t a thought on that little girl’s mind, the values
that fuel my fight today were being instilled at an early age.

Ever since I was a student, I knew I wanted to fight for justice and make
a difference. I’m the daughter of two special education teachers — that’s
them in the photo — and at a very young age they taught me everyone
deserves a fair shot in life.

It’s why I started my career in Alabama investigating threats to democracy
and civil rights in the U.S. and abroad.

It’s why I became a law clerk in Detroit, fighting to protect and defend
people’s civil rights and freedoms.

It’s why, as Dean of Wayne State University Law School, I worked to ensure
all students could afford their education by freezing tuition, and
expanding scholarships.

And it’s why, as Secretary of State, I’ve fought to make everyday life
easier for all Michiganders, secure our elections, and expand voter
access.

But I know our work is far from finished.

I’m running for Governor to make sure Michigan is a place where everyone —
from our kids to our seniors — can stay and thrive.

Because I know — thanks to my mom and dad — we are all better when
everyone has a chance to thrive.

But here’s the truth: Michigan is one of the most competitive states in
the entire country, and my opponent is raking in millions from far-right
mega-donors like the DeVos family and special interests.

I’m not relying on the support of big billionaires and corporations,
because I’m not running to represent them — I’m running to fight for you.

I really hate reaching out and asking for money, but if we’re going to win
the kind of future we want, it’s going to take all hands on deck. So, I
have to ask: [ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/15819?t=1002&akid=1855%2E181023%2EFYkUbw ]will you please chip in $5 or whatever you can to power

* * *
**By Wendy M. Yurgo**
One year ago, Charlie Kirk was taken from this world. I have thought a great deal about what I wanted to say on this anniversary, and I keep returning to the same thing.
I do not want to remember Charlie by the way he died.
I want to remember the way he lived.
I want to remember the young man who walked onto college campuses carrying an enormous burden for the generation he found there. I want to remember the speed of his mind, the command of his facts, the confidence with which he defended what he believed, and the grace he showed the person standing across from him. I want to remember his faith, because without understanding his faith, it is impossible to understand Charlie.
For nearly seven years, Charlie and I moved in the same world. We shared many of the same friends and belonged to the same movement. As the founder of a Christian conservative company serving the faith and freedom community, I was often in the same rooms and at the same events as Charlie. We were among people who believed we had been called to defend something precious and who understood that doing so could come at a cost.
Charlie understood that better than most.
The world came to know him as one of the most formidable debaters in America. His mind was astonishingly quick. He did not simply know facts. He knew how ideas fit together. He could hear a question, find the assumption buried inside it, and answer what was really being asked. He could identify a contradiction almost instantly, but he did not use that ability to make the young person standing at the microphone feel small.
Charlie was direct. He was unapologetic. He would not soften the truth to make it easier to receive. But he listened. He let people finish their questions, even when they were angry or openly hostile. He looked at them when he answered. He took them seriously.
There was a reason for that.
Charlie loved young people.
His critics saw clips of arguments and decided he went onto college campuses to defeat people. They never understood what was happening in front of them. Charlie was not there because he wanted to conquer the young person standing across from him. He was there because he wanted to reach that person.

He saw what was happening to this generation. He saw young people who were isolated, anxious, medicated, confused, and searching desperately for somewhere to belong. He saw children being taught to distrust their parents, their country, their faith, and finally their own bodies. He saw them being told that their deepest discomfort proved God had made a mistake.
Charlie desperately wanted them to understand that this was not true.
You are not a mistake.
You were created in the image of God.
You are loved.
You are all right in the body God gave you.
That was not a political slogan to Charlie. It came from his faith, and it was personal. He understood that behind the anger and the rehearsed language was often a young person asking a much more painful question.
Is there something wrong with me?
Charlie wanted that young person to know that God does not make mistakes.
He never confused love with surrendering the truth. In fact, he believed love required the truth. But he also understood that the person arguing with him was still a human being created by God. He could reject an idea completely without treating the person expressing it as worthless.
That combination is rare. It is especially rare now.
We live in a culture where disagreement has become permission to hate. People no longer argue with an idea. They destroy the person who holds it. Charlie entered those spaces again and again, not because he hated the people inside them, but because he believed they were still worth reaching.
His critics mistook conviction for cruelty because they had come to believe that love requires agreement. Charlie knew better. He believed you could love someone enough to tell that person the truth and respect that person enough to remain at the table afterward.
Charlie did not go onto college campuses because he enjoyed defeating young people in debate.
He went because he loved them enough to tell them the truth.
One of my most treasured memories of Charlie did not happen before a crowd. It happened at a private Shabbat dinner with a small group of friends.
That evening, a visiting rabbi from Israel described Shabbat as the heartbeat of the Ten Commandments. His words stayed with me. Of all the commands God gave us, the command to stop, remember, worship, and rest sits at the center. It calls us out of the noise of the world and back into right relationship with God.

Charlie spoke about what the Sabbath had come to mean in his own life. From Friday evening until Saturday evening, he turned off his phone completely.
Think about that for a moment. Charlie carried a national movement. Millions of people listened to him. His days moved at a pace few of us could imagine, yet every week he deliberately became still. He put down the phone, stepped away from the demands, and made room for God and his family.
That evening, Charlie told me he was writing a book about the Sabbath. He wanted Christians to understand what he had discovered, that rest was not weakness or time stolen from the work. It was obedience. It was restoration. It was a gift from God.
Charlie completed that book shortly before he died. _Stop, in the Name of God: Why Honoring the Sabbath Will Transform Your Life_ was published three months after his death.
When it was released, I thought about that dinner and Charlie sitting at the table, telling me about the book he was writing. He should have been here to place it into the world himself. He should have been here to speak about it, teach from it, and watch others discover the gift that had changed his own life.
But the book came anyway.
And there was Charlie again, still reaching people, still teaching, still calling us away from the noise of the world and back to God.
The world remembers Charlie with a microphone in his hand.
I remember that he knew when to put it down.
That evening helped me understand where his public courage came from. Charlie was not drawing his strength from the crowd. He was drawing it from God. Before he was a political force or the founder of one of the most consequential youth movements in American history, he was a husband, a father, and a child of God.
The Charlie who stood fearlessly before thousands of people and the Charlie who turned off his phone for the Sabbath were not two different men. The stillness made the courage possible. His surrender to God allowed him to stand before a hostile world without surrendering the truth.
Charlie began Turning Point USA when he was eighteen years old. By 31, he had awakened a generation.
That is what I believe his greatest achievement was. It was not the size of the organization or the number of people who came to hear him, although both were extraordinary. It was the young person who heard Charlie and stopped being afraid. It was the student who realized loving America was not something to hide. It was the young man who learned that strength could be honorable and the young woman who learned she did not have to reject faith, femininity, marriage, or motherhood to have value.

[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..Cndn_7QIIaf84BxEqD8pJB2-nx8BpaBJ0NMvRnyHKc0?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=214896850)
Charlie gave young people permission to stand when almost every institution around them was demanding that they kneel.
A year later, what he planted is still growing. Turning Point now reports more than 5,000 chapters across the country. Students who once stood in Charlie's audience are stepping forward to lead. Young people are walking onto campuses Charlie will never again visit and carrying the message he spent his life building.
There is love in that legacy. There is hope in seeing that the work continues and that so many young people refuse to let what Charlie taught them disappear.
But there is also terrible loss.
A movement cannot take the place of a husband at the table. Thousands of chapters cannot replace a father in the lives of his children. No memorial, headline, or measure of influence can give Erika and their children back the man they loved.
Charlie should be here.
He should be walking onto another campus and inviting another young person to the microphone. He should be going home to Erika and their children. He should be turning off his phone on Friday evening. He should be watching the movement he built grow beyond anything even he imagined.
The calendar tells us a year has passed. Grief does not move so neatly. It is possible to be grateful for everything Charlie left behind and still feel the terrible wrongness of a world continuing without him in it.
I miss my friend. Our movement misses him. America misses him.
But I also see him everywhere.
I see him in the young person who refuses to be ashamed of faith. I see him in the student who finds the courage to stand at the microphone and speak. I see him in the young man or woman who finally understands that identity does not come from a screen, a diagnosis, a political movement, or the approval of strangers.
It comes from God.
The world will remember Charlie Kirk for the movement he built. Those of us who knew him will remember why he built it.
He loved God. He loved his family. He loved America.
And he loved a generation enough to tell them the truth.

We were among people who believed we had been called to defend something precious and who understood that doing so could come at a cost. Charlie understood that better than most. The world came to know him as one of the most formidable debaters in America. His mind was astonishingly quick. He did not simply know facts. He knew how ideas fit together. He could hear a question, find the assumption buried inside it, and answer what was really being asked. He could identify a contradiction almost instantly, but he did not use that ability to make the young person standing at the microphone feel small. Charlie was direct. He was unapologetic. He would not soften the truth to make it easier to receive. But he listened. He let people finish their questions, even when they were angry or openly hostile. He looked at them when he answered. He took them seriously. There was a reason for that. Charlie loved young people. His critics saw clips of arguments and decided he went onto college campuses to defeat people. They never understood what was happening in front of them. Charlie was not there because he wanted to conquer the young person standing across from him. He was there because he wanted to reach that person. (Piece continues below) PolitiBrawl will never back down With 1.4 million daily readers, PolitiBrawl is now the largest conservative publication on Substack! We didn't get that way by pulling our punches! on information. If we are going to take back our country, we must win the media wars. It is not an option. President Trump agrees. | | ---|---|--- will be used to FAIRLY cover President Trump's administration and aggressively hold the Democrats accountable because God knows CNN and the New York Times won't do it! This is why the mainstream media hates us, because we are waking up more American's every day to their lies. Thank you for your support and for joining the fight alongside us. \- The PolitiBrawl Editors (piece continues) He saw what was happening to this generation. He saw young people who were isolated, anxious, medicated, confused, and searching desperately for somewhere to belong. He saw children being taught to distrust their parents, their country, their faith, and finally their own bodies. He saw them being told that their deepest discomfort proved God had made a mistake. Charlie desperately wanted them to understand that this was not true. You are not a mistake. You were created in the image of God. You are loved. You are all right in the body God gave you. That was not a political slogan to Charlie. It came from his faith, and it was personal. He understood that behind the anger and the rehearsed language was often a young person asking a much more painful question. Is there something wrong with me? Charlie wanted that young person to know that God does not make mistakes. He never confused love with surrendering the truth. In fact, he believed love required the truth. But he also understood that the person arguing with him was still a human being created by God. He could reject an idea completely without treating the person expressing it as worthless. That combination is rare. It is especially rare now. We live in a culture where disagreement has become permission to hate. People no longer argue with an idea. They destroy the person who holds it. Charlie entered those spaces again and again, not because he hated the people inside them, but because he believed they were still worth reaching. His critics mistook conviction for cruelty because they had come to believe that love requires agreement. Charlie knew better. He believed you could love someone enough to tell that person the truth and respect that person enough to remain at the table afterward. Charlie did not go onto college campuses because he enjoyed defeating young people in debate. He went because he loved them enough to tell them the truth. One of my most treasured memories of Charlie did not happen before a crowd. It happened at a private Shabbat dinner with a small group of friends. That evening, a visiting rabbi from Israel described Shabbat as the heartbeat of the Ten Commandments. His words stayed with me. Of all the commands God gave us, the command to stop, remember, worship, and rest sits at the center. It calls us out of the noise of the world and back into right relationship with God. PolitiBrawl is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support our work, please consider becoming a paid subscriber. Charlie spoke about what the Sabbath had come to mean in his own life. From Friday evening until Saturday evening, he turned off his phone completely. Think about that for a moment. Charlie carried a national movement. Millions of people listened to him. His days moved at a pace few of us could imagine, yet every week he deliberately became still. He put down the phone, stepped away from the demands, and made room for God and his family. That evening, Charlie told me he was writing a book about the Sabbath. He wanted Christians to understand what he had discovered, that rest was not weakness or time stolen from the work. It was obedience. It was restoration. It was a gift from God. Charlie completed that book shortly before he died. Stop, in the Name of God: Why Honoring the Sabbath Will Transform Your Life was published three months after his death. When it was released, I thought about that dinner and Charlie sitting at the table, telling me about the book he was writing. He should have been here to place it into the world himself. He should have been here to speak about it, teach from it, and watch others discover the gift that had changed his own life. But the book came anyway. And there was Charlie again, still reaching people, still teaching, still calling us away from the noise of the world and back to God. The world remembers Charlie with a microphone in his hand. I remember that he knew when to put it down. That evening helped me understand where his public courage came from. Charlie was not drawing his strength from the crowd. He was drawing it from God. Before he was a political force or the founder of one of the most consequential youth movements in American history, he was a husband, a father, and a child of God. The Charlie who stood fearlessly before thousands of people and the Charlie who turned off his phone for the Sabbath were not two different men. The stillness made the courage possible. His surrender to God allowed him to stand before a hostile world without surrendering the truth. Charlie began Turning Point USA when he was eighteen years old. By 31, he had awakened a generation. That is what I believe his greatest achievement was. It was not the size of the organization or the number of people who came to hear him, although both were extraordinary. It was the young person who heard Charlie and stopped being afraid. It was the student who realized loving America was not something to hide. It was the young man who learned that strength could be honorable and the young woman who learned she did not have to reject faith, femininity, marriage, or motherhood to have value. PolitiBrawl is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support our work, please consider becoming a paid subscriber. Charlie gave young people permission to stand when almost every institution around them was demanding that they kneel. A year later, what he planted is still growing. Turning Point now reports more than 5,000 chapters across the country. Students who once stood in Charlie's audience are stepping forward to lead. Young people are walking onto campuses Charlie will never again visit and carrying the message he spent his life building. There is love in that legacy. There is hope in seeing that the work continues and that so many young people refuse to let what Charlie taught them disappear. But there is also terrible loss. A movement cannot take the place of a husband at the table. Thousands of chapters cannot replace a father in the lives of his children. No memorial, headline, or measure of influence can give Erika and their children back the man they loved. Charlie should be here. He should be walking onto another campus and inviting another young person to the microphone. He should be going home to Erika and their children. He should be turning off his phone on Friday evening. He should be watching the movement he built grow beyond anything even he imagined. The calendar tells us a year has passed. Grief does not move so neatly. It is possible to be grateful for everything Charlie left behind and still feel the terrible wrongness of a world continuing without him in it. I miss my friend. Our movement misses him. America misses him. But I also see him everywhere. I see him in the young person who refuses to be ashamed of faith. I see him in the student who finds the courage to stand at the microphone and speak. I see him in the young man or woman who finally understands that identity does not come from a screen, a diagnosis, a political movement, or the approval of strangers. It comes from God. The world will remember Charlie Kirk for the movement he built. Those of us who knew him will remember why he built it. He loved God. He loved his family. He loved America. And he loved a generation enough to tell them the truth. About the Author Wendy M. She writes about where faith collides with the systems shaping our culture, bringing a legal and executive lens to the most urgent issues of our time. | | | | | | Peter,
One year ago today, Charlie Kirk was assassinated.
The United States lost a man who devoted his life to his faith, his country, and the principles he believed in.
Charlie understood something important about our nation: our freedom depends on people having the courage to use it.
He spent his life encouraging a generation of young Americans to think for themselves, to speak boldly, and to never allow fear or intimidation to silence what they believe. His voice reached millions, but his legacy may be the countless people who found their own voices because of him.
His assassination was an act of unspeakable evil. But violence cannot erase an idea, and it most certainly cannot extinguish a legacy.
Charlie's voice isn't gone. It lives on in the courage he inspired in millions of young people in all 50 states.
But for those who share Charlie's faith, remembrance is accompanied by something greater than grief:
Hope.
Today, we remember Charlie Kirk. We pray for his family and everyone who continues to carry the weight of his loss.
We honor his memory not only with our words, but by living with the same courage of our convictions.
May God bless Charlie's family, and may his memory never be forgotten.
\- Stacy

**" The people are the only safe depositories of their own liberty."**
-- Thomas Jefferson, Letter to Littleton W. Tazewell, January 5, 1805
### **Compatriot,**
Jefferson understood that liberty survives only when citizens possess the facts and the courage to act upon them. Government is not the guardian of our rights; that duty belongs to the citizenry.
Our time on the campaign trail reaffirmed a fundamental truth: the work of securing our Republic cannot end at the ballot box. While a seat in Congress is a powerful lever for the preservation of liberty and the empowerment of the people, informed citizens and permanent vigilance are required on the home front. The mission does not depend on a title; it depends on the courage of citizens to act exactly where they are planted.
The grassroots investigative work that fueled our campaign--the council chambers, the doorsteps, and the testimony of our community--now serves as the foundation for our citizen journalism. We do this because the "Iron Triangle"--the collusion of bureaucracy, establishment, and special interests--persists.
### **Welcome to the enduring mission of the American Kitchen Table.**
This is journalism from the ground up, built on the Sunshine Mandate. Our work is delivered through [three distinct columns](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/f6e2d717-3d43-4b0c-a66f-6fc60b02e1c0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg):
**Receipts (Thursdays):** Weekly investigative dispatches exposing the mechanics of power. Evidence. Transparency. Accountability.

**Sweet Ground (Daily):** Rooted stories of resilience and gratitude. A reminder of why we protect the American Kitchen Table.

You haven't just cheered me on from the sidelines; you've put on your boots and walked right alongside me.

Dear Peter, I am writing this note not just as your Senator, but as a girl from Caribou who is continuously awed by the heart of this state. Thank you for opening your doors to me, for sharing your stories, and for pouring your time, energy, and hope into this work.You haven't just cheered me on from the sidelines, you've put on your boots and walked right alongside me. You've handed out signs, knocked on doors, and reminded me every single day why we fight so hard to find common ground. When people ask me where I find the strength to navigate the tough votes and the long days, the answer is simple: I look to you, Peter. I think of the Maine spirit: resilient, practical, deeply kind, and fiercely independent. Everything we have built, every policy we have crafted to protect our families, our lobstermen, our seniors, and our future, bears your fingerprints.**Thank you for believing in the power of conversation over conflict. Thank you for trusting me with your voices. And above all, thank you for giving me the greatest privilege of my life: bringing the character of Maine to the floor of the United States Senate.** We still have more trails to clear and more work to do, but today, I just want to pause and say how deeply, profoundly grateful I am to have you in my corner.

**Thursday, September 10, 2026 -**_**** Ansarallah seizes strategic Red Sea port of Mocha, advances toward Bab al-Mandab. Saudi launches more than 50 strikes across Yemen on Wednesday. Ansarallah targets three Saudi cities with ballistic missiles and drones. Pakistan says no military response to Ansarallah attacks on Saudi Arabia under discussion. Seafarer killed, another missing in attack on tanker. Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claims attack on U.S. aircraft carrier. Report: Iranian strike damages multiple U.S. warplanes at Jordan airbase. President Donald Trump warns Iran "not to get cute," threatens "very hard" strike on suspected nuclear site. Iran, China, and Russia reject International Atomic Energy Agency resolution. Wall Street Journal: Trump advisers privately warn Iran war could last beyond his presidency. Four Palestinians, including two children, killed in Israeli strike on Beit Lahia home. Israeli strikes hit homes across northern, central and southern Gaza on Wednesday. Israeli forces carry out raids, arrests and demolitions across occupied West Bank. Two Palestinian detainees injured during Israeli prison raid. Palestinian factions reject reconstitution process, warn of exclusion and Palestinian Authority control. Former U.S. Secretary of State Antony Blinken calls report he rejected early Hamas hostage release offer "complete fiction." Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to sue Haaretz over report he was warned of Oct. 7 attack. Israel destroys homes, wells, and agricultural sites across southern Lebanon despite "ceasefire." Lebanese army says Israel committed 7,700 violations of U.S.-brokered agreement. Trump administration proposes excluding undocumented immigrants, race questions from 2030 census. Trump to keep El Salvador TPS holders' protections until "appropriate time." Trump pledges $5,000 "Trump Dividend" to every American if Republicans keep Congress. Democratic Senator John Fetterman makes video appearance at Trump's midterm convention. Treasury announces $6 billion bond buyback amid soaring yields, market reacts negatively. U.S. strike in Caribbean kills three. Secretary of State Marco Rubio pledges $45 million in security funding for Ecuador. Eighty-seven missing after ferry fire near Philippine tourist destination. Algeria cuts diplomatic relations with UAE over "provocative or hostile" actions. Thousands protest as Slovenia opens Israeli embassy. British man charged with assisting Russian military intelligence. Cameroon separatists kidnap five teachers, kill police officer in raid. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's flight delayed after Russian drone crashes near Moldovan airport. Russian strikes hit Kyiv petrol station and agribusiness facility in Dnipro._
**This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday**

# Yemen
* **Ansarallah seizes strategic Red Sea port of Mocha, advances toward Bab al-Mandab:** Ansarallah forces seized the strategic Red Sea port city of Mocha and are advancing south toward the Bab al-Mandab Strait, Reuters reported Thursday. Witnesses separately told AFP they saw Ansarallah forces entering the city, while Saudi-backed troops reportedly withdrew. Yemen's Saudi-backed government has not officially confirmed Mocha's fall.
* Ansarallah forces are also nearing control of other coastal areas along the strait as they push to capture all of Yemen's Red Sea coastline. A military source told AFP that Ansarallah had seized Zuqar Island following rocket attacks and an amphibious assault.
* Bab al-Mandab Strait is a crucial waterway and one of the world's busiest global shipping lanes that links the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden and the Indian Ocean. It was being increasingly used as the U.S. and Iran to exchange attacks in the Strait of Hormuz.
* Fighting in Yemen since last week has killed at least 500 people, mostly combatants, according to AFP. Nearly 20,000 have fled their homes, according to the International Organization for Migration.
* **Saudi launches more than 50 strikes across Yemen on Wednesday:** Saudi warplanes [carried out](https://substack.com/redirect/f9b935e3-4beb-4d6f-8821-595c14e7eb7e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) 54 airstrikes across six Yemeni governorates within 12 hours on Wednesday, according to Ansarallah military spokesperson Yahya Saree.
* **North:** Saada, Ansarallah's main stronghold, and Al-Jawf, both bordering Saudi Arabia.
* **Center and east:** Marib, an oil and gas region east of Sana'a, and Al-Bayda, a strategic crossroads in central Yemen.
* **West and southwest:** Hodeidah, Yemen's main Red Sea port region, and Taiz, a major front between Sana'a and the Gulf of Aden.
* Saree warned the attacks "will not go unpunished." Saudi Arabia has not confirmed the strikes.
* **Ansarallah targets three Saudi cities with ballistic missiles and drones:** Saudi-led coalition spokesperson Turki Al-Maliki [said](https://substack.com/redirect/ccf07c00-6ac1-4539-ab80-bdcaaea6d354?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Ansarallah forces launched ballistic missiles and drones toward the Saudi cities of Khamis Mushait, Abha, and Jazan on Wednesday, accusing the group of targeting civilians and infrastructure, the Saudi Press Agency reported.
* Saudi Civil Defense separately [issued](https://substack.com/redirect/447414de-2a79-4bc7-b108-d28955a35f38?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) an alert Thursday in Khamis Mushait warning of a potential threat, the fourth such warning within 24 hours, before later announcing that the threat had passed.
* **Pakistan says no military response to Ansarallah attacks on Saudi Arabia under discussion:** Pakistan [said](https://substack.com/redirect/4a743397-4f47-4df1-9791-076fad1a516a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Thursday that it is not currently discussing a military response under the Mecca joint defense agreement following Ansarallah attacks on Saudi Arabia, Reuters reported.
* "There is no such thing under discussion right now," Foreign Ministry spokesperson Sajjad Haider Khan said. "When time comes, [we] will act under the agreement."
* The agreement, signed last month by Pakistan, Turkey and Saudi Arabia, stipulates that an armed attack on any one of the three countries will be considered an attack on all. Khan also said there were no plans to expand the alliance.

# Iran
* **Seafarer killed, another missing in attack on tanker:** One seafarer was [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/a837cff5-7ce0-4c36-984c-7a1fff0a3eaf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and another is missing after an incident Wednesday aboard the Gibraltar-flagged oil-products tanker Hercules Star while it was anchored off Dubai, the vessel's charterer told Reuters.
* Maritime security sources said the tanker may have been struck by a drone, but the weapon has not been confirmed. UKMTO separately reported a ship in the area listing and possibly taking on water after being hit by an unknown projectile. ([link](https://substack.com/redirect/a837cff5-7ce0-4c36-984c-7a1fff0a3eaf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))
* **Iran 's IRGC claims attack on U.S. aircraft carrier: **Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps [said](https://substack.com/redirect/023a1eb4-e896-4db0-8a86-d014a4d27971?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) it targeted a U.S. aircraft carrier roughly 500 kilometers (~310 miles) away on Wednesday, according to Mehr News.
* The U.S. has not confirmed that a carrier was hit and previously said Iranian missile attacks caused no damage or casualties.
* **Report: Iranian strike damages multiple U.S. warplanes at Jordan airbase:** Multiple U.S. military aircraft were [damaged](https://substack.com/redirect/f8caed64-d9f7-4310-9442-20b1e4ac621b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in an Iranian strike on Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in Al Azraq, Jordan, early Wednesday, CBS News reported.
* Around eight F-15 fighter jets sustained light damage and were returned to service, while an A-10 Thunderbolt was hit and lost a wing. U.S. forces reportedly fired more than 30 Patriot missiles to intercept incoming Iranian projectiles.
* The strike was part of Iranian retaliation after the U.S. attacked five Iranian oil tankers on Tuesday.
* **Trump warns Iran "not to get cute," threatens "very hard" strike on suspected nuclear site:** President Donald Trump threatened further attacks on Iran over alleged renewed activity at Pickaxe Mountain, a suspected nuclear site near the heavily damaged Natanz uranium enrichment facility.
* "We notice there's a little activity at Pickaxe. I would advise Iran not to get cute because we will have to hit them very hard," Trump said Wednesday.
* Trump also predicted the U.S.-Iran war would continue until after November's midterm elections, claiming, "the war will end immediately after the election because they can't hold out any longer."
* He argued that short-term economic pain for Americans was worth preventing Iran from developing nuclear weapons. No intelligence assessment has concluded that Iran was close to developing a nuclear weapon.
* **Iran, China, and Russia reject IAEA resolution:** Iran, China, and Russia [jointly rejected](https://substack.com/redirect/bf20e8d1-1226-4169-908f-36b3e86e042f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a draft resolution introduced by the U.S., Britain, France, and Germany at the IAEA Board of Governors, the U.N. nuclear watchdog's policymaking body, calling for Iran's nuclear file to be referred to the U.N. Security Council.
* The three governments said the draft "fails even to make explicit reference to the attacks," which they described as "the root cause and principal factor underlying the current situation." They said continuing U.S. attacks have made normal IAEA inspections and safeguards work in Iran effectively impossible.
* The statement noted that Iran nevertheless agreed to provide the agency access to the Bushehr nuclear power plant in mid-September, but said further cooperation requires guarantees that attacks on Iranian nuclear facilities will not recur.
* China, Iran, and Russia also called the IAEA's June 2025 finding of Iranian noncompliance "politically motivated and far-fetched," arguing that it paved the way for attacks on safeguarded nuclear facilities.
* Iran's representative to international organizations in Vienna, Reza Najafi, said the IAEA had never verified any diversion of Iranian nuclear material and accused the resolution's sponsors of "rewarding the aggressor and punishing the victim."
* **WSJ: Trump advisers privately warn Iran war could last beyond his presidency:** Top White House advisers privately [warned](https://substack.com/redirect/68f0c152-ff9f-446b-b430-1896872c10d8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Trump that the war with Iran could continue beyond his term in January 2029, despite his public predictions of a swift victory, the Wall Street Journal reported, citing U.S. officials.
* Vice President JD Vance, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, and others have discussed the possibility that Tehran could withstand the U.S. naval blockade and other military pressure for years. Trump, however, said Wednesday that the war would end "immediately" after November's midterm elections because Iran "can't hold out any longer."
* Vance publicly declined last week to provide an "artificial timeline," saying, "It would be irresponsible for us to write out our strategy and our timeline."
* The Pentagon is meanwhile preparing for a prolonged U.S. presence, with some deployments extended into 2027 and air-defense units potentially remaining without a firm end date.

# Palestine
* **Killed and wounded in Gaza:** Over the past 24 hours, one Palestinian was killed and 30 injured in attacks across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health.
* The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023 has risen to 73,670 killed, with 174,682 injured. Since October 11, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,359 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 4,571, while 831 bodies have been recovered from under the rubble.
* **Four Palestinians, including two children, killed in Israeli strike on Beit Lahia home:** Four Palestinians from the same family were killed, including two children aged 8 and 12, and several others wounded on Thursday when Israeli forces [struck](https://substack.com/redirect/d7b19a2b-de42-4276-a327-eee066a07e92?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a home in the Beit Lahia area of northern Gaza, WAFA reported. The four bodies were taken to al-Shifa Hospital in Gaza City, while others were reported missing under the rubble.
* Earlier, several Palestinians were wounded after Israeli military vehicles and a drone opened fire toward displacement tents in Jabalia refugee camp.
* **Israeli strikes hit homes across northern, central and southern Gaza on Wednesday:** An Israeli strike hit a house belonging to the Al-Masri family in Al-Shati refugee camp, west of Gaza City, after the family was ordered to evacuate.
* "They called and ordered us to evacuate. But we're not resistance fighters or anything. We're civilians. We have children," Mahmoud Al-Masri, 37, told Drop Site's Mohamed Ahmed.
* Ibrahim Al-Shaarawi, 45, whose home was also destroyed, said around 10 families had been living there. "Who told you that the war had stopped? ... Every day there's bombing. Every day there are strikes," Al-Shaarawi said.
* In central Gaza, a house in Nuseirat refugee camp was struck after an Israeli displacement order, wounding several Palestinians. An order was also issued for another house in western Khan Younis, south of Gaza, before it was struck.
* **Watch the dispatch from Mohamed Ahmed[ here](https://substack.com/redirect/ae54386a-8536-4bcc-80b1-d9845c42e4c4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).**
* **Israeli forces carry out raids, arrests and demolitions across occupied West Bank:** Israeli forces carried out raids across the occupied West Bank on Thursday, as Palestinian prisoners' groups [said](https://substack.com/redirect/0d75f3c9-ff45-44c6-8a27-375f3e50fe8b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) more than 100 Palestinians, including children, women, former prisoners and journalists, had been detained across the territory over the past week.
* **Tulkarm:** Israeli forces [raided](https://substack.com/redirect/d38d86ed-b17e-4360-8f18-2efb7840d37b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Eco Park, north of Tulkarm, and seized several wild animals from the park on Thursday, WAFA reported. They also detained a park employee.
* **Bethlehem:** Israeli forces [demolished](https://substack.com/redirect/3d95b00f-30ec-460d-a5c3-5c26c79b2e64?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a 170-square-meter home in Battir, west of Bethlehem. Elsewhere in the governorate, Israeli forces detained seven Palestinians, including journalists Sabri Jibril and Muath Amarna, during raids in Tuqu, Dheisheh refugee camp and several areas of Bethlehem.
* **Nablus:** Two Palestinians were [hospitalized](https://substack.com/redirect/3d4a763b-611a-405c-9b23-748783655d18?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) after Israeli forces beat them during a raid on Awarta, south of Nablus, on Wednesday evening. Israeli forces also fired live ammunition, tear gas and stun grenades during the raid.
* **Two Palestinian detainees injured during Israeli prison raid:** Two Palestinian prisoners were [injured](https://substack.com/redirect/23ef03d3-7e84-4ae5-9f0e-3edccf710b83?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) after Israeli Prison Service units raided several sections of Ganot Prison, according to the Palestinian Commission of Detainees' Affairs. The commission said the units used stun grenades and rubber-coated bullets during the raid.
* Around 9,400 Palestinian Palestinians are currently held in Israeli prisons, with 3,244 held under administrative detention without charge or trial.
* **Palestinian factions reject reconstitution process, warn of exclusion and PA control:** Hamas, Palestinian Islamic Jihad, the PFLP, Fatah's Democratic Reform Current, the PFLP-GC, the Palestinian National Initiative, and the Popular Resistance Committees [rejected](https://substack.com/redirect/b825343e-a3eb-45ab-ae38-ee4e971c4059?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and expressed "deep concern" over the procedures being used by the Palestinian Authority to reconstitute the Palestinian National Council (PNC), warning that the practices "contradict the principles of national partnership and democracy."
* The PNC is the PLO's legislature, intended to represent Palestinians in Palestine and abroad. The factions said members are being appointed through assemblies in several Arab countries that do not represent Palestinians as a whole.
* They condemned "appointment instead of election, exclusion instead of partnership, and unilateralism instead of national consensus." They accused a powerful faction within the Palestinian Authority of engineering the council to control its decisions, disenfranchise Palestinians abroad, and exclude resistance factions, opposition forces, and independent figures.
* The signatories demanded the process be replaced by national dialogue and a unified election law providing free and transparent voting and proportional representation.

* **One year after Doha assassination attempt, Hamas 's Basem Naim tells Drop Site that Israel has not changed course: **One year after Israel tried to assassinate Hamas's negotiating delegation in Doha, senior Hamas official Bassem Naim [shared](https://substack.com/redirect/a71d917c-814b-47cd-954d-6e4f75ec20dc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a statement with Drop Site reflecting on the attack.

* Naim said the U.S. was "beyond any doubt, complicit in the crime," and that the failed assassination attempt and the international outrage that followed pushed Washington toward the Sharm el-Sheikh agreement.
* Naim stated that Hamas has adhered to all of the agreement provisions, while Israel continues "the crime of genocide and the project of forced displacement, albeit in a less brutal form" since the agreement. He also criticized the "Board of Peace" for allowing Israel to "continue spreading death, destruction, and hunger everywhere."
* "There can be no successful wager on breaking the Palestinian will, nor on exhausting the patience of our people," Naim said. He added that killing individual Palestinian leaders "will not alter the course toward freedom and independence."

* **Blinken calls report he rejected early Hamas hostage release offer "complete fiction": **Former U.S. Secretary of State Antony Blinken [denied](https://substack.com/redirect/ab8d3b4a-0ef2-4ee3-939e-5acc630b72e7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a Haaretz report that he urged Qatar to wait after it offered to mediate the release of civilian hostages held by Hamas on October 7, 2023.

* **Netanyahu to sue Haaretz over report he was warned of Oct. 7 attack:** Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu [said](https://substack.com/redirect/73b70600-8151-4188-8a1a-dda82aabfb34?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Wednesday he will sue Haaretz and reporters Shlomi Eldar and Ruth Yaval over a report claiming UAE President Mohammed bin Zayed warned him of a Hamas attack 10 days before October 7, 2023, calling the report "fabricated" and "politically motivated."
