* **Trump administration proposes excluding undocumented immigrants, race questions from 2030 census:** The Census Bureau [proposed](https://substack.com/redirect/d1c92c82-d59e-4ec3-919d-899d1c2c1649?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a sweeping overhaul of the 2030 census Wednesday that would exclude undocumented immigrants and some legally present immigrants lacking permanent resident status from population counts used to apportion House seats, while also prohibiting race, ethnicity, and sexual orientation questions on the count.
* Census results determine congressional apportionment, redistricting, federal funding, and enforcement of civil rights laws like the Voting Rights Act.
* The proposal would redefine "usual residence" to argue undocumented immigrants lack "a sufficient tie and allegiance" to the country, marking an expanded version of a similar effort Trump's first administration pursued for the 2020 census, one abandoned by the Biden administration after it was challenged legally.

* DHS said "an announcement on El Salvador's TPS will be made at the appropriate time" and that Salvadoran TPS holders "retain protection" until then, without specifying when a final decision would come.
* The National TPS Alliance advocacy group estimates about 170,000 Salvadoran TPS holders live in the U.S.
* **Trump pledges $5,000 "Trump Dividend" to every American if Republicans keep Congress: **President Donald Trump pledged Wednesday at the GOP's midterm convention in Dallas to send every American adult $5,000 if Republicans retain control of the House and Senate, calling it "the Trump Dividend" and comparing it to corporate shareholder distributions, citing the U.S.'s "tremendous strength and success economically."
* The promise would likely cost more than $1 trillion and require congressional approval.
* Vice President **JD Vance** appeared to partially walk back the proposal within the hour, suggesting the wealthy wouldn't receive payments and that it could be funded by tariff revenue, though such revenue falls far short of the pledged sum.
* **Fetterman makes video appearance at Trump 's midterm convention:** Sen. **John Fetterman**(D-Penn.)****[ appeared](https://substack.com/redirect/85b66553-6d69-4718-bb93-f60adf43d0ee?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in a video Wednesday at the opening night of President Trump's midterm convention in Dallas, describing himself as a "common-sense Democrat" who rejects "the extremes in socialism" and introducing Republican Sen. David McCormick, with whom he pledged to "work together... and defend the steel way of life."
* The appearance came amid speculation about a possible party switch, which Fetterman has repeatedly denied, telling the Times in July he would "never" leave the Democratic Party, though he recently announced an unusual joint fundraising committee with McCormick.
* The pro-Israel stalwart has noted, however, that a change in Democratic party policy towards against would be a "red line" for him.
* About 69% of likely Democratic voters in Pennsylvania view Fetterman negatively, according to an August Times/Philadelphia Inquirer/Siena poll.
* **Treasury announces $6 billion bond buyback amid soaring yields, market reacts negatively** : The Treasury Department [said](https://substack.com/redirect/a256ebcd-db91-4580-a394-86ca0c0b5b25?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Wednesday it will buy back up to $6 billion of government debt in an effort to reduce the costs of borrowing.
* The Department's repurchases reduce the available supply of longer-dated bonds, increasing their price and lowering their yields, which would then theoretically reduce interest rates across the board.
* The market's immediate reaction to the buyback was negative, however, with the 10-year yield rising 0.05 percentage points on Thursday afternoon, a 3-year-high, and the 20-year yield rising by a similar amount.

* **Zelenskyy 's flight delayed after Russian drone crashes near Moldovan airport:** A flight carrying Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy from Moldova to Norway was [delayed](https://substack.com/redirect/aa107c52-9bc7-4e1f-8a37-7a39aef810ff?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) this week after authorities closed Moldova's airspace due to a drone incursion, with Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre claiming that the plane "was nearly hit by a drone as it took off from Moldova."
* Moldovan police said a Russian drone crashed and exploded Tuesday in a sunflower field about 100 miles from Chișinău International Airport, sparking four fires but no injuries.
* The drone had also crossed into the airspace of Romania, a NATO member, prompting Spanish Air and Space Forces to send two F-18 jets to track it before it reentered Moldovan airspace.
* Zelenskyy's flight, one of three delayed by the airspace closure, ultimately departed later than scheduled, allowing him to arrive in Oslo Tuesday to meet with Støre to discuss Ukraine's air defense needs before attending King Harald V's funeral.
* **Russian strikes hit Kyiv petrol station and agribusiness facility in Dnipro:** A Russian drone [struck](https://substack.com/redirect/b6755a11-96ad-42c2-adad-19a3f21754d1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a petrol station in Kyiv injuring four people in what appeared to be the first attack of its kind on a fuel station in the capital.
* In Dnipro, a separate Russian strike hit a sunflower-oil facility operated by the global agribusiness Bunge, killing two people and wounding five. The plant is one of Ukraine's five largest food-processing facilities.
* Russia also struck a shopping center in Sumy and intensified attacks on Ukraine's southern ports, killing four people and injuring 19 in Mykolaiv overnight. The attacks come amid escalating Russian and Ukrainian strikes on logistics, fuel infrastructure and other economic targets intended to undermine each side's war effort.

Photo by Mohammed Huwais / AFP via Getty Images. Thursday, September 10, 2026 -** Ansarallah seizes strategic Red Sea port of Mocha, advances toward Bab al-Mandab. Saudi launches more than 50 strikes across Yemen on Wednesday. Ansarallah targets three Saudi cities with ballistic missiles and drones. Pakistan says no military response to Ansarallah attacks on Saudi Arabia under discussion. Seafarer killed, another missing in attack on tanker. Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claims attack on U.S. aircraft carrier. Report: Iranian strike damages multiple U.S. warplanes at Jordan airbase. President Donald Trump warns Iran "not to get cute," threatens "very hard" strike on suspected nuclear site. Iran, China, and Russia reject International Atomic Energy Agency resolution. Wall Street Journal: Trump advisers privately warn Iran war could last beyond his presidency. Four Palestinians, including two children, killed in Israeli strike on Beit Lahia home. Israeli strikes hit homes across northern, central and southern Gaza on Wednesday. Israeli forces carry out raids, arrests and demolitions across occupied West Bank. Two Palestinian detainees injured during Israeli prison raid. Palestinian factions reject reconstitution process, warn of exclusion and Palestinian Authority control. Former U.S. Secretary of State Antony Blinken calls report he rejected early Hamas hostage release offer "complete fiction." Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to sue Haaretz over report he was warned of Oct. 7 attack. Israel destroys homes, wells, and agricultural sites across southern Lebanon despite "ceasefire." Lebanese army says Israel committed 7,700 violations of U.S.-brokered agreement. Trump administration proposes excluding undocumented immigrants, race questions from 2030 census. Trump to keep El Salvador TPS holders' protections until "appropriate time." Trump pledges $5,000 "Trump Dividend" to every American if Republicans keep Congress. Democratic Senator John Fetterman makes video appearance at Trump's midterm convention. Treasury announces $6 billion bond buyback amid soaring yields, market reacts negatively. U.S. strike in Caribbean kills three. Secretary of State Marco Rubio pledges $45 million in security funding for Ecuador. Eighty-seven missing after ferry fire near Philippine tourist destination. Algeria cuts diplomatic relations with UAE over "provocative or hostile" actions. Thousands protest as Slovenia opens Israeli embassy. British man charged with assisting Russian military intelligence. Cameroon separatists kidnap five teachers, kill police officer in raid. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's flight delayed after Russian drone crashes near Moldovan airport. Russian strikes hit Kyiv petrol station and agribusiness facility in Dnipro. This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday Yemen Ansarallah seizes strategic Red Sea port of Mocha, advances toward Bab al-Mandab: Ansarallah forces seized the strategic Red Sea port city of Mocha and are advancing south toward the Bab al-Mandab Strait, Reuters reported Thursday. Witnesses separately told AFP they saw Ansarallah forces entering the city, while Saudi-backed troops reportedly withdrew. Yemen's Saudi-backed government has not officially confirmed Mocha's fall. Ansarallah forces are also nearing control of other coastal areas along the strait as they push to capture all of Yemen's Red Sea coastline. A military source told AFP that Ansarallah had seized Zuqar Island following rocket attacks and an amphibious assault. Bab al-Mandab Strait is a crucial waterway and one of the world's busiest global shipping lanes that links the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden and the Indian Ocean. It was being increasingly used as the U.S. and Iran to exchange attacks in the Strait of Hormuz. Fighting in Yemen since last week has killed at least 500 people, mostly combatants, according to AFP. Nearly 20,000 have fled their homes, according to the International Organization for Migration. Saudi launches more than 50 strikes across Yemen on Wednesday: Saudi warplanes 54 airstrikes across six Yemeni governorates within 12 hours on Wednesday, according to Ansarallah military spokesperson Yahya Saree. North: Saada, Ansarallah's main stronghold, and Al-Jawf, both bordering Saudi Arabia. Center and east: Marib, an oil and gas region east of Sana'a, and Al-Bayda, a strategic crossroads in central Yemen. West and southwest: Hodeidah, Yemen's main Red Sea port region, and Taiz, a major front between Sana'a and the Gulf of Aden. Saree warned the attacks "will not go unpunished." Saudi Arabia has not confirmed the strikes. Ansarallah targets three Saudi cities with ballistic missiles and drones: Saudi-led coalition spokesperson Turki Al-Maliki Ansarallah forces launched ballistic missiles and drones toward the Saudi cities of Khamis Mushait, Abha, and Jazan on Wednesday, accusing the group of targeting civilians and infrastructure, the Saudi Press Agency reported. Saudi Civil Defense separately an alert Thursday in Khamis Mushait warning of a potential threat, the fourth such warning within 24 hours, before later announcing that the threat had passed. Pakistan says no military response to Ansarallah attacks on Saudi Arabia under discussion: Pakistan Thursday that it is not currently discussing a military response under the Mecca joint defense agreement following Ansarallah attacks on Saudi Arabia, Reuters reported. "There is no such thing under discussion right now," Foreign Ministry spokesperson Sajjad Haider Khan said. "When time comes, [we] will act under the agreement." The agreement, signed last month by Pakistan, Turkey and Saudi Arabia, stipulates that an armed attack on any one of the three countries will be considered an attack on all. Khan also said there were no plans to expand the alliance. Iran Seafarer killed, another missing in attack on tanker: One seafarer was and another is missing after an incident Wednesday aboard the Gibraltar-flagged oil-products tanker Hercules Star while it was anchored off Dubai, the vessel's charterer told Reuters. Maritime security sources said the tanker may have been struck by a drone, but the weapon has not been confirmed. UKMTO separately reported a ship in the area listing and possibly taking on water after being hit by an unknown projectile. () Iran 's IRGC claims attack on U.S. aircraft carrier: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps it targeted a U.S. aircraft carrier roughly 500 kilometers (~310 miles) away on Wednesday, according to Mehr News. The U.S. has not confirmed that a carrier was hit and previously said Iranian missile attacks caused no damage or casualties. Report: Iranian strike damages multiple U.S. warplanes at Jordan airbase: Multiple U.S. military aircraft were in an Iranian strike on Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in Al Azraq, Jordan, early Wednesday, CBS News reported. Around eight F-15 fighter jets sustained light damage and were returned to service, while an A-10 Thunderbolt was hit and lost a wing. U.S. forces reportedly fired more than 30 Patriot missiles to intercept incoming Iranian projectiles. The strike was part of Iranian retaliation after the U.S. attacked five Iranian oil tankers on Tuesday. Trump warns Iran "not to get cute," threatens "very hard" strike on suspected nuclear site: President Donald Trump threatened further attacks on Iran over alleged renewed activity at Pickaxe Mountain, a suspected nuclear site near the heavily damaged Natanz uranium enrichment facility. "We notice there's a little activity at Pickaxe. I would advise Iran not to get cute because we will have to hit them very hard," Trump said Wednesday. Trump also predicted the U.S.-Iran war would continue until after November's midterm elections, claiming, "the war will end immediately after the election because they can't hold out any longer." He argued that short-term economic pain for Americans was worth preventing Iran from developing nuclear weapons. No intelligence assessment has concluded that Iran was close to developing a nuclear weapon. Iran, China, and Russia reject IAEA resolution: Iran, China, and Russia a draft resolution introduced by the U.S., Britain, France, and Germany at the IAEA Board of Governors, the U.N. nuclear watchdog's policymaking body, calling for Iran's nuclear file to be referred to the U.N. Security Council. The three governments said the draft "fails even to make explicit reference to the attacks," which they described as "the root cause and principal factor underlying the current situation." They said continuing U.S. attacks have made normal IAEA inspections and safeguards work in Iran effectively impossible. The statement noted that Iran nevertheless agreed to provide the agency access to the Bushehr nuclear power plant in mid-September, but said further cooperation requires guarantees that attacks on Iranian nuclear facilities will not recur. China, Iran, and Russia also called the IAEA's June 2025 finding of Iranian noncompliance "politically motivated and far-fetched," arguing that it paved the way for attacks on safeguarded nuclear facilities. Iran's representative to international organizations in Vienna, Reza Najafi, said the IAEA had never verified any diversion of Iranian nuclear material and accused the resolution's sponsors of "rewarding the aggressor and punishing the victim." WSJ: Trump advisers privately warn Iran war could last beyond his presidency: Top White House advisers privately Trump that the war with Iran could continue beyond his term in January 2029, despite his public predictions of a swift victory, the Wall Street Journal reported, citing U.S. officials. Vice President JD Vance, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, and others have discussed the possibility that Tehran could withstand the U.S. naval blockade and other military pressure for years. Trump, however, said Wednesday that the war would end "immediately" after November's midterm elections because Iran "can't hold out any longer." Vance publicly declined last week to provide an "artificial timeline," saying, "It would be irresponsible for us to write out our strategy and our timeline." The Pentagon is meanwhile preparing for a prolonged U.S. presence, with some deployments extended into 2027 and air-defense units potentially remaining without a firm end date. Palestine Killed and wounded in Gaza: Over the past 24 hours, one Palestinian was killed and 30 injured in attacks across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health. The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023 has risen to 73,670 killed, with 174,682 injured. Since October 11, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,359 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 4,571, while 831 bodies have been recovered from under the rubble. Four Palestinians, including two children, killed in Israeli strike on Beit Lahia home: Four Palestinians from the same family were killed, including two children aged 8 and 12, and several others wounded on Thursday when Israeli forces a home in the Beit Lahia area of northern Gaza, WAFA reported. The four bodies were taken to al-Shifa Hospital in Gaza City, while others were reported missing under the rubble. Earlier, several Palestinians were wounded after Israeli military vehicles and a drone opened fire toward displacement tents in Jabalia refugee camp. Israeli strikes hit homes across northern, central and southern Gaza on Wednesday: An Israeli strike hit a house belonging to the Al-Masri family in Al-Shati refugee camp, west of Gaza City, after the family was ordered to evacuate. "They called and ordered us to evacuate. But we're not resistance fighters or anything. We're civilians. We have children," Mahmoud Al-Masri, 37, told Drop Site's Mohamed Ahmed. Ibrahim Al-Shaarawi, 45, whose home was also destroyed, said around 10 families had been living there. "Who told you that the war had stopped? ... Every day there's bombing. Every day there are strikes," Al-Shaarawi said. In central Gaza, a house in Nuseirat refugee camp was struck after an Israeli displacement order, wounding several Palestinians. An order was also issued for another house in western Khan Younis, south of Gaza, before it was struck. Watch the dispatch from Mohamed Ahmed. Israeli forces carry out raids, arrests and demolitions across occupied West Bank: Israeli forces carried out raids across the occupied West Bank on Thursday, as Palestinian prisoners' groups more than 100 Palestinians, including children, women, former prisoners and journalists, had been detained across the territory over the past week. Tulkarm: Israeli forces Eco Park, north of Tulkarm, and seized several wild animals from the park on Thursday, WAFA reported. They also detained a park employee. Bethlehem: Israeli forces a 170-square-meter home in Battir, west of Bethlehem. Elsewhere in the governorate, Israeli forces detained seven Palestinians, including journalists Sabri Jibril and Muath Amarna, during raids in Tuqu, Dheisheh refugee camp and several areas of Bethlehem. Nablus: Two Palestinians were after Israeli forces beat them during a raid on Awarta, south of Nablus, on Wednesday evening. Israeli forces also fired live ammunition, tear gas and stun grenades during the raid. Two Palestinian detainees injured during Israeli prison raid: Two Palestinian prisoners were after Israeli Prison Service units raided several sections of Ganot Prison, according to the Palestinian Commission of Detainees' Affairs. The commission said the units used stun grenades and rubber-coated bullets during the raid. Around 9,400 Palestinian Palestinians are currently held in Israeli prisons, with 3,244 held under administrative detention without charge or trial. Palestinian factions reject reconstitution process, warn of exclusion and PA control: Hamas, Palestinian Islamic Jihad, the PFLP, Fatah's Democratic Reform Current, the PFLP-GC, the Palestinian National Initiative, and the Popular Resistance Committees and expressed "deep concern" over the procedures being used by the Palestinian Authority to reconstitute the Palestinian National Council (PNC), warning that the practices "contradict the principles of national partnership and democracy." The PNC is the PLO's legislature, intended to represent Palestinians in Palestine and abroad. The factions said members are being appointed through assemblies in several Arab countries that do not represent Palestinians as a whole. They condemned "appointment instead of election, exclusion instead of partnership, and unilateralism instead of national consensus." They accused a powerful faction within the Palestinian Authority of engineering the council to control its decisions, disenfranchise Palestinians abroad, and exclude resistance factions, opposition forces, and independent figures. The signatories demanded the process be replaced by national dialogue and a unified election law providing free and transparent voting and proportional representation. One year after Doha assassination attempt, Hamas 's Basem Naim tells Drop Site that Israel has not changed course: One year after Israel tried to assassinate Hamas's negotiating delegation in Doha, senior Hamas official Bassem Naim a statement with Drop Site reflecting on the attack. Before the attack, Naim said Hamas received a proposal from Trump through Qatari mediators and was given 48 hours to respond. The delegation was meeting to discuss it when Israel attempted to assassinate its members "in the heart of the capital of a mediating state allied with the United States." Naim said the U.S. was "beyond any doubt, complicit in the crime," and that the failed assassination attempt and the international outrage that followed pushed Washington toward the Sharm el-Sheikh agreement. Naim stated that Hamas has adhered to all of the agreement provisions, while Israel continues "the crime of genocide and the project of forced displacement, albeit in a less brutal form" since the agreement. He also criticized the "Board of Peace" for allowing Israel to "continue spreading death, destruction, and hunger everywhere." "There can be no successful wager on breaking the Palestinian will, nor on exhausting the patience of our people," Naim said. He added that killing individual Palestinian leaders "will not alter the course toward freedom and independence." Blinken calls report he rejected early Hamas hostage release offer "complete fiction": Former U.S. Secretary of State Antony Blinken a Haaretz report that he urged Qatar to wait after it offered to mediate the release of civilian hostages held by Hamas on October 7, 2023. Drop Site co-founder Ryan Grim summarized the report as saying Hamas had conveyed through Qatar that it was prepared to return civilian hostages and that Israel refused to engage, after which Qatar approached Blinken. Grim wrote that Blinken "had the opportunity to free every single civilian hostage and de-escalate the situation. Instead he wanted war." Blinken quote-posted Grim's tweet Wednesday, writing: "For the record, this is false. Complete fiction." Netanyahu to sue Haaretz over report he was warned of Oct. 7 attack: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu Wednesday he will sue Haaretz and reporters Shlomi Eldar and Ruth Yaval over a report claiming UAE President Mohammed bin Zayed warned him of a Hamas attack 10 days before October 7, 2023, calling the report "fabricated" and "politically motivated." The Haaretz report claimed then-Hamas leader Yahya Sinwar relayed warnings through an intermediary that he was preparing a "huge surprise" and told contacts "to expect an earthquake." Bin Zayed's aides then reportedly passed this to Israel's Shin Bet, which dismissed the threat, before bin Zayed personally raised it with Netanyahu, who also brushed it aside. Netanyahu denied that the phone call with bin Zayed occurred, saying a review of his call log "found no trace of it whatsoever," and separately accused Palestinian political figure Muhammad Dahlan, who lives in the UAE, of being behind the report. Lebanon Israel destroys homes, wells, and agricultural sites across southern Lebanon despite "ceasefire": Nabatieh: Israeli warplanes a two-wave strike on Nabatieh Al-Fawqa on Thursday, Lebanon's National News Agency (NNA) reported. In Mais al-Jabal, Israeli forces carried out a large explosion in the Al-Dabsh area, west of the town, a waste-sorting facility as well as homes and industrial and agricultural structures. A separate Israeli strike on the Marj Harouf-Zebdine road wounded two people on Wednesday, according to Lebanon's Health Ministry. Tyre (Sour): Israeli forces continued demolishing homes and infrastructure in Mansouri, where more than 10 large explosions were since midnight, alongside airstrikes and artillery fire. Israeli drones dropped barrels packed with high explosives onto the roofs of homes before detonating them remotely, according to NNA. Israeli forces also blew up artesian wells in the town. Lebanese army says Israel committed 7,700 violations of U.S.-brokered agreement: The Lebanese army Wednesday Israel has committed approximately 7,700 violations of the framework agreement, including opening fire near army personnel and patrols, while escalating strikes and demolitions across southern Lebanon. The army said it had fulfilled its obligations by establishing operational control in designated areas and seizing 1,818 weapons and munitions. U.S. News Primary results: Rhode Island State Representative David Morales , a democratic socialist, incumbent Providence Mayor Brett Smiley in Tuesday's Democratic primary. It's a major win for , which has spent years working to reshape the state's politics. Morales campaigned on capping rent hikes, expanding affordable housing, and raising taxes on polluters and corporate landlords, and drew support from Sen. Bernie Sanders and former Mayor Jorge Elorza. Smiley, seeking a second term after winning in 2022, attacked Morales over past support for "defunding the police"--a characterization Morales rejected, saying Smiley was "clinging on to quotes and tweets from over five years ago" and stating he would "not defund the police, a position that I have been very consistent on." Morales is expected to win in November's general election in the heavily Democratic city. Former CVS executive Helena Foulkes easily incumbent Gov.Dan McKee in Rhode Island's Democratic gubernatorial primary. McKee, who has served as governor since 2021, faced intense scrutiny over his administration's handling of the 2023 closure and rebuilding of the Washington Bridge between Providence and East Providence. Foulkes, who lost to McKee in the 2022 primary, is now the favorite heading into November's general election. Trump administration proposes excluding undocumented immigrants, race questions from 2030 census: The Census Bureau a sweeping overhaul of the 2030 census Wednesday that would exclude undocumented immigrants and some legally present immigrants lacking permanent resident status from population counts used to apportion House seats, while also prohibiting race, ethnicity, and sexual orientation questions on the count. Census results determine congressional apportionment, redistricting, federal funding, and enforcement of civil rights laws like the Voting Rights Act. The proposal would redefine "usual residence" to argue undocumented immigrants lack "a sufficient tie and allegiance" to the country, marking an expanded version of a similar effort Trump's first administration pursued for the 2020 census, one abandoned by the Biden administration after it was challenged legally. Trump administration keeps El Salvador TPS holders ' protections until "appropriate time": The Trump administration tens of thousands of Salvadoran immigrants will keep their Temporary Protected Status for now, despite the protections having been scheduled to expire Wednesday, according to a statement from the Department of Homeland Security. DHS said "an announcement on El Salvador's TPS will be made at the appropriate time" and that Salvadoran TPS holders "retain protection" until then, without specifying when a final decision would come. The National TPS Alliance advocacy group estimates about 170,000 Salvadoran TPS holders live in the U.S. Trump pledges $5,000 "Trump Dividend" to every American if Republicans keep Congress: President Donald Trump pledged Wednesday at the GOP's midterm convention in Dallas to send every American adult $5,000 if Republicans retain control of the House and Senate, calling it "the Trump Dividend" and comparing it to corporate shareholder distributions, citing the U.S.'s "tremendous strength and success economically." The promise would likely cost more than $1 trillion and require congressional approval. Vice President JD Vance appeared to partially walk back the proposal within the hour, suggesting the wealthy wouldn't receive payments and that it could be funded by tariff revenue, though such revenue falls far short of the pledged sum. Fetterman makes video appearance at Trump 's midterm convention: Sen. John Fetterman(D-Penn.)** in a video Wednesday at the opening night of President Trump's midterm convention in Dallas, describing himself as a "common-sense Democrat" who rejects "the extremes in socialism" and introducing Republican Sen. David McCormick, with whom he pledged to "work together... and defend the steel way of life." The appearance came amid speculation about a possible party switch, which Fetterman has repeatedly denied, telling the Times in July he would "never" leave the Democratic Party, though he recently announced an unusual joint fundraising committee with McCormick. The pro-Israel stalwart has noted, however, that a change in Democratic party policy towards against would be a "red line" for him. About 69% of likely Democratic voters in Pennsylvania view Fetterman negatively, according to an August Times/Philadelphia Inquirer/Siena poll. Treasury announces $6 billion bond buyback amid soaring yields, market reacts negatively : The Treasury Department Wednesday it will buy back up to $6 billion of government debt in an effort to reduce the costs of borrowing. The Department's repurchases reduce the available supply of longer-dated bonds, increasing their price and lowering their yields, which would then theoretically reduce interest rates across the board. The market's immediate reaction to the buyback was negative, however, with the 10-year yield rising 0.05 percentage points on Thursday afternoon, a 3-year-high, and the 20-year yield rising by a similar amount. 📥 Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email DC Correspondent Julian Andreone at Julian@dropsitenews.com Other International News U.S. strike in Caribbean kills three: U.S. Southern Command on Wednesday that its "Joint Task Force Western Hemisphere" had struck a vessel it claimed belonged to narco-traffickers, killing three in the Caribbean. Wednesday's strike is the 69th acknowledged strike in the Pacific by U.S. forces, part of a campaign that has killed at least 230 people who the Trump administration has alleged were trafficking drugs in the region, though several of these incidents have involved civilians. Rubio pledges $45 million in security funding for Ecuador: Secretary of State Marco Rubio during a visit to Quito on Wednesday that the U.S. would seek $45 million in additional security funding and new equipment for Ecuador, including a 110-foot Coast Guard cutter and five interceptor vessels. Rubio also designated the Ecuador-based gang Los Tiguerones a foreign terrorist organization, following similar designations for two other Ecuadorian gangs last year, and announced sanctions on seven former Ecuadorian officials accused of bribery. He also claimed that the U.S. campaign against suspected drug trafficking boats has shifted to joint strikes with Ecuador, insisting that the strikes were not aimed at killing fishermen. Drop Site's Camila Lourdes Galarza reported on these strikes on fishermen in April. Her full report is available. Eighty-seven missing after ferry fire near Philippine tourist destination : At least five people have been and 87 remain missing after a fire broke out Wednesday evening aboard the ferry M/V June Aster. about 2.2 kilometers offshore of the Philippine's Palawan province, according to the Philippine coastguard. The coastguard said 42 people had been rescued so far out of the 134 passengers and crew listed on the ship's manifest. Algeria cuts diplomatic relations with UAE over "provocative or hostile" actions: Algeria Thursday it would be cutting diplomatic relations with the United Arab Emirates, saying the country had "exhausted all means of preserving bilateral relations" after a series of "provocative or hostile" actions by Abu Dhabi despite "repeated warnings," according to the country's foreign ministry. The ministry claimed it had summoned the Emirati ambassador and gave him 48 hours to comply with the decision, though the UAE has not immediately responded. The rupture follows years of strained ties over the UAE's normalization with Israel under the 2020 Abraham Accords, and the two countries' opposing positions on the Western Sahara dispute, in which the UAE backs Morocco's sovereignty claim while Algeria supports the Polisario Front seeking independence. Thousands protest as Slovenia opens Israeli embassy: Thousands in Ljubljana on Wednesday against the opening of Israel's first embassy in Slovenia, following Prime Minister Janez Jana's reversal of his predecessor Robert Golob's policy, which had characterized Israel's war in Gaza as a genocide. Protesters carried banners reading "We stand together for peace and Palestine" and "genocide is not self-defense." A June poll by newspaper Delo found 56% of Slovenians opposed closer ties with Israel, while 14% supported closer ties. The opposition Freedom Movement and the country's Left party jointly filed a parliamentary proposal Wednesday to impeach Jansa over the foreign policy shift. British man charged with assisting Russian military intelligence : Joshua Cammidge, 31, was on Wednesday with assisting a foreign intelligence service, the UK's Crown Prosecution Service announced, after he allegedly receiving instructions to commit an act of sabotage from a suspected representative of the GRU Volunteer Corps, a group controlled by Russia's military intelligence. Cameroon separatists kidnap five teachers, kill police officer in raid: Armed attackers a police officer and kidnapped five teachers during a raid on a teacher training center in Wum, in Cameroon's Northwest Region, on Tuesday, according to the region's governor. Anglophone groups have fought government forces in Cameroon's Northwest for roughly a decade, with the conflict emerging from a 2016 government crackdown on protests by English-speaking teachers and lawyers objecting to francophone authorities' growing control over education and legal systems in the area. At least 6,000 people have died in the fighting since 2016, according to the United Nations, and more than 330,000 people were displaced internally in Cameroon last year. Zelenskyy 's flight delayed after Russian drone crashes near Moldovan airport: A flight carrying Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy from Moldova to Norway was this week after authorities closed Moldova's airspace due to a drone incursion, with Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre claiming that the plane "was nearly hit by a drone as it took off from Moldova." Moldovan police said a Russian drone crashed and exploded Tuesday in a sunflower field about 100 miles from Chișinău International Airport, sparking four fires but no injuries. The drone had also crossed into the airspace of Romania, a NATO member, prompting Spanish Air and Space Forces to send two F-18 jets to track it before it reentered Moldovan airspace. Zelenskyy's flight, one of three delayed by the airspace closure, ultimately departed later than scheduled, allowing him to arrive in Oslo Tuesday to meet with Støre to discuss Ukraine's air defense needs before attending King Harald V's funeral. Russian strikes hit Kyiv petrol station and agribusiness facility in Dnipro: A Russian drone a petrol station in Kyiv injuring four people in what appeared to be the first attack of its kind on a fuel station in the capital. In Dnipro, a separate Russian strike hit a sunflower-oil facility operated by the global agribusiness Bunge, killing two people and wounding five. The plant is one of Ukraine's five largest food-processing facilities. Russia also struck a shopping center in Sumy and intensified attacks on Ukraine's southern ports, killing four people and injuring 19 in Mykolaiv overnight. | | Remembering Charlie Kirk
---
| | As we remember those who gave everything to protect our freedom, we also remember our great friend Charlie Kirk, who devoted his life to defending the principles that make America worth fighting for. Charlie understood that freedom must be cherished, protected, and passed to the next generation. He inspired countless young Americans to find their voice, stand boldly for truth, and never take the blessings of liberty for granted. As moms, we are grateful for his courage, his conviction, and his unwavering love for America. His work reminds us that every generation has a responsibility to protect the freedoms we inherited and ensure they remain for our children and grandchildren. We remember Charlie. We honor his legacy. And we carry the torch forward.
---

| | 25 Years Later, We Remember!
---
|

As moms, we have the privilege and responsibility of teaching our children what that day revealed about America: the courage to stand together, the compassion to care for one another, and the faith and love of freedom that carried our nation through its darkest hours. We remember so our children will never forget.We honor. We remember. We stand united. Every day Ilhan and our campaign receive racist messages, violent tirades, and direct death threats. And these threats spike every time Trump goes after Ilhan, which is quite often these days.
These threats culminated in an incident just a few months ago, when a mentally unwell man rushed Ilhan at a town hall and sprayed her with liquid from a syringe. **We can thank our lucky stars that Ilhan’s security team was there to take that man down before he could do much worse.**
Ilhan is fearless, and she brushed off that attack within seconds. But as we continue to fight to win reelection, stand up to Trump, and pass a transformative agenda for the working class, we absolutely have to make sure that Ilhan and everyone on this campaign team can do so safely.

#
Hi Peter, it's Tim.
My team texted me this photo from the RNC this morning.
[](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=stp-ms-em-20260910-1.LTfZ2V&amount=5&refcode=em20260910-1071&t=1&akid=1071%2E34582%2ELEagiI)
Right up on the main stage, on a giant screen next to President Biden and Vice President Harris, was a picture of me.
I’m retiring at the end of the year, and my name isn’t even on the ballot this November. But clearly, _I’m still living rent-free in their heads._
It tells you everything you need to know about the GOP’s priorities. They don't have a plan to solve real problems and improve people's lives; all they can do is invent boogeymen to scare their base.
**They want a distraction so no one notices who they’re actually fighting for: the tech bros, the modern-day robber barons, and the billionaires tripping over themselves to suck up to Trump and buy our elections.**
When Republicans put their MAGA megadonors and corporate interests first, working families in small towns pay the price.
I started Small Town PAC to fight back by supporting Democrats in tough races across the country who understand what our communities actually need — good schools, good jobs, affordable health care, and a real future for our kids.
Every one of our endorsed candidates is taking on Republicans backed by Trump’s MAGA machine. But winning these seats takes real resources.

body:
Floridians deserve a courageous leader fiercely committed to her values and her community — Angie Nixon is that fighter.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20260910-1&t=1&akid=3991%2E587540%2EjNE4SJ)
Exciting news, Peter:
**Leaders We Deserve is proud to announce we’re endorsing Angie Nixon for U.S. Senate in Florida!**
[](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260910_1_angie.g2PvJ7&refcode=em20260910-3991&t=2&akid=3991%2E587540%2EjNE4SJ)
I’ll tell you more, but first — Angie just won one of the biggest primary upsets of the entire cycle, and her momentum is undeniable. **Now she’s fighting to flip a critical U.S. Senate seat in Florida.[Will you split a $5 contribution between Angie Nixon and Leaders We Deserve today?](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260910_1_angie.g2PvJ7&refcode=em20260910-3991&amount=5&t=3&akid=3991%2E587540%2EjNE4SJ)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260910_1_angie.g2PvJ7&amount=5&refcode=em20260910-3991&t=4&akid=3991%2E587540%2EjNE4SJ)**
**Angie Nixon** learned the power of organizing and the meaning of solidarity from her mother, a union member who worked two jobs just to keep food on the table. That lived experience shaped Angie into the resilient advocate, fierce union organizer, and proven fighter for Floridians that she is today.
She grew up attending Jacksonville’s public schools, where she was bused across town because her predominantly Black neighborhood school didn’t have the resources it deserved. That’s exactly where her power as a leader comes from: she knows what it looks like when working families get the short end of the stick, because she was one of them.
Long before there was a seat to run for, Angie was doing the hard work of building power in her own community.
She co-founded Melanin Market to support local businesses, opened Natalie’s Nook with her daughter to fight food insecurity in her own neighborhood, and later opened Cafe Resistance, a bookstore and coffee shop in Jacksonville that offers tutoring, mental health workshops, a food pantry, and a safe space for teens to learn and thrive. **Angie’s history in her community proves she’s always had the instincts to take action. She doesn’t wait for permission — she sees a need, and meets it.**
As a State Representative, Angie has expanded childcare access for thousands of families, taken on a major grocery chain for price gouging Floridians at the register, introduced legislation to unmask the ICE agents terrorizing immigrant communities across the state, and led the fight against Ron DeSantis’ racist redistricting maps (even bringing out a megaphone on the House floor to speak up for Florida voters).
[](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260910_1_angie.g2PvJ7&refcode=em20260910-3991&t=5&akid=3991%2E587540%2EjNE4SJ)
Her opponent, Ashley Moody, was never even elected to this Senate seat. _She was hand-picked by Trump’s buddy Ron DeSantis to fill it._ Moody’s tenure as Attorney General was mired in misappropriated Medicaid funds to the tune of $10 million. And in the Senate, she voted to let ACA subsidies expire, a decision that’s already caused over 440,000 Floridians to lose their health coverage. She’s spent her entire career answering to power — _not the people of Florida._
**Angie is different. She’s fighting for a future shaped by teachers, nurses, parents, and workers.** In the Senate, she’ll join the progressive coalition fighting for Medicare for All, push for universal childcare, a national rent freeze and moratorium on evictions, stronger union protections, and a $25 federal minimum wage. She’ll rally hard to get corporate money out of politics and rein in the tech companies and data center giants driving up costs for working people.
If she wins in November, she’ll be the first Black person Florida has ever elected to the U.S. Senate.
And listen Peter, I said it before and I’ll say it again: _we’re not writing Florida off._ Nobody is pretending that this will be an easy fight. But Angie has already accomplished something enormous this cycle, upsetting the establishment-backed opponent who outraised her more than 16:1 — proof that the many really can beat the money. **She’s truly an exciting candidate with the power to shake up the state of this race. She just needs the resources and a strong grassroots movement behind her to win.**
That’s where you come in. Leaders We Deserve doesn’t take a single dollar from corporate PACs or special interests — and neither does Angie. Our ability to back candidates like her depends entirely on supporters like you showing up when it counts.
**[So Peter, will you split a $5 contribution between Angie and Leaders We Deserve today?](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260910_1_angie.g2PvJ7&refcode=em20260910-3991&amount=5&t=6&akid=3991%2E587540%2EjNE4SJ)**

Thank you,
David Hogg

That’s exactly where her power as a leader comes from: she knows what it looks like when working families get the short end of the stick, because she was one of them. Long before there was a seat to run for, Angie was doing the hard work of building power in her own community. She co-founded Melanin Market to support local businesses, opened Natalie’s Nook with her daughter to fight food insecurity in her own neighborhood, and later opened Cafe Resistance, a bookstore and coffee shop in Jacksonville that offers tutoring, mental health workshops, a food pantry, and a safe space for teens to learn and thrive. Angie’s history in her community proves she’s always had the instincts to take action. She doesn’t wait for permission — she sees a need, and meets it. As a State Representative, Angie has expanded childcare access for thousands of families, taken on a major grocery chain for price gouging Floridians at the register, introduced legislation to unmask the ICE agents terrorizing immigrant communities across the state, and led the fight against Ron DeSantis’ racist redistricting maps (even bringing out a megaphone on the House floor to speak up for Florida voters). Her opponent, Ashley Moody, was never even elected to this Senate seat. She was hand-picked by Trump’s buddy Ron DeSantis to fill it. Moody’s tenure as Attorney General was mired in misappropriated Medicaid funds to the tune of $10 million. And in the Senate, she voted to let ACA subsidies expire, a decision that’s already caused over 440,000 Floridians to lose their health coverage. She’s spent her entire career answering to power — not the people of Florida. Angie is different. She’s fighting for a future shaped by teachers, nurses, parents, and workers. In the Senate, she’ll join the progressive coalition fighting for Medicare for All, push for universal childcare, a national rent freeze and moratorium on evictions, stronger union protections, and a $25 federal minimum wage. She’ll rally hard to get corporate money out of politics and rein in the tech companies and data center giants driving up costs for working people. If she wins in November, she’ll be the first Black person Florida has ever elected to the U.S. Senate. And listen Peter, I said it before and I’ll say it again: we’re not writing Florida off. Nobody is pretending that this will be an easy fight. But Angie has already accomplished something enormous this cycle, upsetting the establishment-backed opponent who outraised her more than 16:1 — proof that the many really can beat the money. She’s truly an exciting candidate with the power to shake up the state of this race. She just needs the resources and a strong grassroots movement behind her to win. That’s where you come in. Leaders We Deserve doesn’t take a single dollar from corporate PACs or special interests — and neither does Angie. Our ability to back candidates like her depends entirely on supporters like you showing up when it counts. Thank you, David Hogg

name: Wes Moore
subject: Saying goodbye.
body:
# [](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/8?t=1&akid=1899%2E1086043%2E7pEXyz)
This is a longer email about saying goodbye, Peter, but if you don’t have time to read through, I would deeply appreciate **[a contribution to power our campaign.](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260910-1.CPMW_u&refcode=em-20260910-1&t=2&akid=1899%2E1086043%2E7pEXyz)**
After nearly a century of operation, Valley Forge Military Academy — the place where I went to school and grew from an angry, complicated child to a confident young man — has closed.
When my mother first sent me to the Forge, she saw military school as a last resort in response to a seemingly endless chain of misbehavior, both at home and at school. At age 11, I’d already felt handcuffs on my wrists. **I was not on a path to success.**
There was no overnight miracle when I started school there, but slowly, things changed. I learned about honor, code, and service. I started to take an interest in campus life, academics, and leadership positions — and I rose up the ranks and became a first captain in command of around 800 cadets.
After graduation, I went on to study at Johns Hopkins and Oxford, deployed to Afghanistan with the 82nd Airborne Division, ran one of the largest poverty-fighting organizations in the country, and now, I serve as the 63rd governor of Maryland _and the first Black governor in the history of my state._
What saddens me most isn’t losing a place I once called home. My memories will forever live on with me.
**It saddens me that other young men like me will have one fewer avenue to challenge themselves and build their own pathway to success.**
Peter, at a time where our young men and boys are falling behind and feeling isolated, we have to offer more paths for connection and engagement.
I know Valley Forge Military Academy did that for me, and I’m determined to find ways to do that for young Marylanders today.
That includes the **Maryland Corps and Service Year Option** — the first statewide program in the country to give high school graduates a year of paid, full-time community service on the path to college or a career.
We have to help young Marylanders find the thing that guides them on a pathway to success and that inspires them to serve. **[If you support that mission, I would appreciate a donation to keep me in the fight as Maryland's governor today.](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260910-1.CPMW_u&refcode=em-20260910-1&t=3&akid=1899%2E1086043%2E7pEXyz)**
Elevate,
Wes

Friend of Life, If someone asked you what $28 could accomplish today, you probably wouldn't think of it as a life-changing amount of money. At PreBorn!, however, a gift of $28 helps provide one life-saving ultrasound, and we've seen God use that simple moment to change the course of countless lives. When a woman walks into one of our Network Clinics, she is often carrying far more than the weight of an unexpected pregnancy. Many have been told there is only one answer to the crisis they're facing. Others arrive convinced they are completely alone. Some have never had anyone slow down long enough to ask how they're really doing. That's why the ultrasound matters so much. For the first time, she has the opportunity to see her baby. She hears the heartbeat. She begins asking questions she hadn't considered before. Instead of making a permanent decision in fear, she is surrounded by compassionate people who take time to listen, answer her questions, offer practical support, and share the hope of Jesus Christ. Those moments save babies. They also change mothers, strengthen families, and open doors for the gospel to be shared. In fact, more than 80% of abortion-vulnerable women choose life after seeing their baby on an ultrasound at a PreBorn! Network Clinic. That's the impact your generosity helps make possible. Today, because of a generous group of friends, every gift made before September 30 will be MATCHED dollar for dollar, up to $100,000. That means your gift can help twice as many women encounter a life-saving ultrasound, compassionate care, and the hope of Jesus Christ when they need it most. We know $28 may not seem like much. But to the next woman who walks through the doors of a PreBorn! Network Clinic searching for hope, it could become the moment that changes everything. Will you make your matched gift today and help provide the next life-saving ultrasound?
---

But if my campaign doesn’t have the funds to support our team, then we will be unable to compete. And right now, it looks like we are going to run out of funds.** We do not need to outraise my opponent, Troy Jackson. We can’t.But we need to raise enough to fight back.And that means raising $3M in September.That sounds like a huge amount of money, and it is. But if everyone could match their previous $10 donation, we’d make a huge dent in getting there. body:
A 45-million-acre corporate land grab

---](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/8Qxe7vLNqezaIVHwo3N6pw~~/AAUS1hA~/3CNEy7vjmjAR1IOCLIckGXtd3GEbAr4U7vE32-YVN8AACa0TZDxxFJrBn-DG_C5qNlGBTv-dAv1b5hmhKEhX7R1zcqPlyezOiEHQRL6gOiXanXv1B9QsCKdKt3vNjw0_)
| | | | Peter, How do you successfully execute a 45-million-acre corporate land grab? **Step one:** You take an executive who spent his career lobbying to chop down national forests. **Step two:** You appoint him as the Chief of the U.S. Forest Service. Step three: You wait for him to open the floodgates. **That is exactly what is happening right now in Washington.** Tom Schultz is the first-ever Forest Service Chief who didn't actually come from within the agency. Before this, he was the president of a timber trade association. Now, he is using his government authority to completely kill the 25-year-old "roadless rule," stripping protections from 45 million acres of untouched wilderness so his former employers can bulldoze roads and clear-cut the backcountry. The politicians rubber-stamping this heist are looking the American public in the eye and claiming they need to build logging roads into pristine habitats to "prevent wildfires." It is complete garbage. [**This is a 45-million-acre heist happening in broad daylight. Will you pitch in $10 today to our rapid-response war chest so we can expose this corruption?**](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/F-6ESfaJCDii_3Ii3EEmag~~/AAUS1hA~/AF-hAQHk-XK2LCkULnvTFOMKCnHu9HkZxGuNSYQerZQbyVpVapi70rA7nxgdyMTSyrhcNNPjQCHw0Q9JPd5f35kPL3DhDS3Lbqikhg-bmXVfmsEuQBCQ-G9s42JumQK7Xxz_sK0c5yNZmEXMlrd0BOz_KL65UZi_ZyUKNhbqhrn3NMabGty4oSiHT4gPAFem48MFKf8OKqzMw0WHWqaOve7dBY-L_0sDm_7YFBRkJ-ItACC4ntGP_pJGEv0Huh8c) The Forest Service's _own data_ shows that wildfires are nearly three times as likely to start near roads because they bring in human ignition sources. They aren't trying to stop forest fires—they are using the threat of fires as a human shield for the timber lobby. And the lumber executives know it. They are literally bragging on corporate earnings calls, telling their Wall Street investors, "We know the new Forest Service chief." Schultz and the politicians enabling him think they can quietly liquidate the last remaining old-growth forests in America without facing any consequences. They expect you to be too exhausted by the news cycle to put up a fight. We are going to ensure that every hunter, angler, hiker, and voter knows exactly who allowed a timber lobbyist to sell off our national heritage. ---

The "NDA playbook" trend -- a pre-written decision rubric spelling out preferred terms, fallback positions, and walk-away points for every clause of a non-disclosure agreement -- has moved from legal-department tool to a quiet force in two very public arenas: data center development and municipal government.
**Data centers:** secrecy as a site-selection weapon. When a hyperscaler scouts a region, everything is negotiated under NDA: power capacity, tax abatement terms, land prices, water rights, and utility rate structures. A playbook matters here because the stakes are asymmetric. Developers review hundreds of NDAs a year; a county reviews a handful. Without a rubric, local negotiators improvise, and improvisation favors the party that negotiates for a living. A playbook forces the landowner, utility, or local government to pre-decide the dangerous clauses: how long confidentiality lasts (data center deals routinely demand five to seven years -- long enough to outlast the elected officials who signed), whether the existence of the deal itself is secret, and what happens when a competing bidder asks why the parcel vanished from the market. Playbooks also standardize "residuals" and "similar development" language -- critical when two hyperscalers are courting the same utility district.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/340a4ce5-00d3-4d9a-afdb-03c4b06e3ca0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**City halls:** NDAs as governance friction. Municipalities increasingly sign NDAs with developers, vendors, and even other agencies, often before any public record exists. The playbook movement is teaching city attorneys and procurement staff to set institutional guardrails: define narrowly what is confidential, cap the term, carve out anything subject to open-records and sunshine laws, and require council notification before signing. This is educational in the best sense -- it converts an informal "the city attorney will handle it" culture into a written standard a new council member can read in ten minutes.
Records requests filed by the Gulf States Newsroom and Type Investigations turned up at least [54 NDAs signed by elected officials in Louisiana](https://substack.com/redirect/ce860785-4b56-43a3-b9e4-98cd541bfef3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) about various types of projects since Gov. Jeff Landry took office in early 2024. They include the ones for data centers.
The honest tension. Neither arena is purely commercial. Data center NDAs can delay public knowledge of water and power impacts for years; municipal NDAs can hollow out open-meeting principles if used reflexively. A good playbook doesn't eliminate secrecy -- legitimate negotiations need it -- but it forces the question how much secrecy, for how long, and who approved it to be answered in advance rather than under deadline pressure.
The NDA playbook is doing for data centers and city halls what budget rules did for finance departments: replacing improvisation with documented institutional judgment. For smaller governments facing billion-dollar counterparties, it may be the most cost-effective leverage available.

body:
This has to stop.
| | |
---
Friend, I recently visited the construction site of a proposed data center in Effingham County, Georgia. **Simply put, I’m alarmed.**
This would become one of the largest data centers in the country – right down the street from an elementary school. But the people who live in Effingham County haven’t had any say in the matter. The entire process has been cloaked in secrecy.
We’re seeing this happen all across Georgia and all across the country. Corporations come in and build these massive data centers with no input from the people who live in these communities. And in many cases, it’s driving up the cost of electricity, raising the price of water, and creating pollution.
**It has to stop. That’s why I’m calling for a moratorium on the construction of data centers.** This moratorium should only be lifted if corporations can ensure transparency and that the data centers won’t cause any spike in utility bills or pollution.

* * *
I'll be honest with you guys: I didn't watch most of the Republican convention last night. I assumed it would be a tremendous waste of my time, so I spent the evening with my family instead. and play Dungeons and Dragons with my son. My wife and I watched Ted Lasso. I caught a little bit of a nasty Cubs game against the Brewers. I regret none of it.
This morning I caught up on the so-called highlights, which is all anybody ever needs to do with these things. Tim Scott delivering an unhinged speech to a half-empty arena. A sitting U.S. cabinet official trying to slap the behind of a sitting female Republican congresswoman. You know, just weird, MAGA shit.
But I want to focus on maybe the only genuinely interesting thing that happened, which is Donald Trump's newest scheme to hoodwink the American people into voting Republican in the fall: a promise that if Republicans hold the House and the Senate, every American adult gets a $5,000 dividend check.
Let's call that what it is**:** a bribe. He is trying to buy your vote with your own money, out in the open, on a stage, in front of cameras, and nobody in that arena so much as blinked.
Trump talked for _an hour and forty-seven minutes_. From everything I've been told, it was the exact same speech he always gives -- the same grievances, the same riffs, the same sixty-minute detour through whatever's currently rotting in his head. And at some point in there, he dangled five grand in front of a country that is genuinely struggling to pay for groceries and boasted that he has brought the 'most tremendous economic success' in the history of our country.
You have to be a special kind of stupid at this point to believe he's actually going to send you that check. Because seriously, how many times has he run this play?
First, it was the $5,000 "DOGE dividend" from all those billions Elon Musk was supposedly going to save the federal government. Never happened.
Then it was a $2,000 "tariff dividend" from all the money his beautiful tariffs were supposedly going to rake in. Never happened.
Then came the promise of $1,000 checks from the "savings" created by letting ACA subsidies expire and gutting healthcare for millions of Americans through his Big Ugly Bill. Never happened.
And now, conveniently, less than two months before an election, there's another check. This time it's five thousand dollars. This time all you have to do is keep Republicans in power.
He has been lying about this exact thing, in this exact form, for years now, and he keeps doing it because it keeps working on somebody.
Politicians lying is not new. I've been in this business twenty years; I'm not naive about it. But the way Donald Trump lies is so far beyond the pale that it belongs in its own category. Politicians have tried to buy votes before. Nobody has ever done it this brazenly, this shamelessly, with this little effort at cover. On some level you almost have to stand in awe of it. He isn't even pretending anymore.
And then you've got JD Vance out on Fox News trying to defend it -- and even Fox News isn't buying it. Even they're skeptical this money ever materializes. **Good**. So Vance is sitting there explaining that we've paid down so much of the debt and the deficit that we can just hand the savings back to you.
That is not true. It isn't remotely true.
The debt and the deficit are exploding right now because of Donald Trump. This administration is spending enormous amounts of money on the war in Iran. It has single-handedly eroded trade agreements and relationships with some of our closest allies. It has pursued a dozen other stupid, expensive policies. And through all of this, the administration is helping itself to billions of dollars of the American people's money while it happens.
The outright lying isn't new. I'm still amazed by it every single time.
And I keep coming back to the promises that actually hurt. We all remember the big ones: everything was going to get cheaper. He wasn't going to start new wars.
But it's the seemingly forgotten promises that stick with me.

_Already a paid subscriber? Then like, share, and keep showing up in the comments. It matters more than you know._
* * *
During his 2024 campaign, Trump stood up and promised families dealing with infertility in this country that he was going to make IVF _free_ for _every_ American. Think about what a promise like that means to somebody desperate to start a family. Think about hearing the president of the United States tell you that the thing standing between you and having a child might finally be taken care of.
There are people who heard that promise and let themselves hope that something they desperately wanted might finally be within reach. But after the election ended, Trump moved on, and he has never thought about them again. He has done nothing. Not a damn thing.
He used them. That's what makes this shit so cruel.
And here's the part that should end this whole conversation:
**Republicans** _**control**_**the House. Republicans** _**control**_**the Senate. If they wanted to send every American a $5,000 check, they** _**could**_**do it right now** _**.**_**Today.** Trump could get his party in a room and it would be done by the weekend. They won't, because he doesn't have the votes -- he doesn't really control his own party anymore. So instead of governing, he's selling a check he can't write to voters he thinks won't notice.
And that's the part I don't want anybody to lose sight of. Donald Trump isn't asking you to judge Republicans on what they've done with the power they already have. He's asking you to ignore it. He's asking for more time. More power. More opportunities to enrich himself and the people around him at the expense of the American people. More opportunities to erode the already fragile foundations of our democracy and further corrupt the institutions that are supposed to protect it.
And he's doing it by exploiting something incredibly human: _hope_. Giving people false hope when they're struggling goes beyond being dishonest, it's fucking cruel.
It's absurd. And it makes me angry.
So I'm going to do what I always tell you to do, which is turn the rage into something useful. I'm writing this in my head walking to work this morning, the way I usually do -- record it into my phone, clean it up at the office, take out at least some of the f-bombs. I've got a couple of media hits today where I'm going to call this administration exactly what it is. I'm going to keep organizing people in my own community to make sure our democracy holds here, block by block. I'm going to keep telling people the truth. That's what I can do.
Here's what you can do: don't waste another minute of your life on that convention. Nothing new is coming out of it. Take the anger, take the rage, take the frustration, and put it somewhere it does damage. Don't let them sell you false hope. Channel that anger into building something real--for yourself, your family, for your country.
Let's give these guys exactly what they've earned this fall -- a massive, historic electoral defeat that ends this presidency in everything but name, turns Donald Trump into the lamest of lame ducks, and clears the way for a new generation of Democratic leadership. Leadership that can actually fix this broken economy, undo the damage, and -- most importantly -- deliver some accountability for the staggering corruption inside this administration.
I believe we can do all of it.
Hang tough.
With urgency,
--Mike

But after the election ended, Trump moved on, and he has never thought about them again. He has done nothing. Not a damn thing. He used them. That's what makes this shit so cruel. And here's the part that should end this whole conversation: Republicans controlthe House. Republicans controlthe Senate. If they wanted to send every American a $5,000 check, they coulddo it right now .Today.** Trump could get his party in a room and it would be done by the weekend. They won't, because he doesn't have the votes -- he doesn't really control his own party anymore. So instead of governing, he's selling a check he can't write to voters he thinks won't notice. And that's the part I don't want anybody to lose sight of. Donald Trump isn't asking you to judge Republicans on what they've done with the power they already have. He's asking you to ignore it. He's asking for more time. More power. More opportunities to enrich himself and the people around him at the expense of the American people. More opportunities to erode the already fragile foundations of our democracy and further corrupt the institutions that are supposed to protect it. And he's doing it by exploiting something incredibly human: hope. Giving people false hope when they're struggling goes beyond being dishonest, it's fucking cruel. It's absurd. And it makes me angry. So I'm going to do what I always tell you to do, which is turn the rage into something useful. I'm writing this in my head walking to work this morning, the way I usually do -- record it into my phone, clean it up at the office, take out at least some of the f-bombs. I've got a couple of media hits today where I'm going to call this administration exactly what it is. I'm going to keep organizing people in my own community to make sure our democracy holds here, block by block. I'm going to keep telling people the truth. That's what I can do. Here's what you can do: don't waste another minute of your life on that convention. Nothing new is coming out of it. Take the anger, take the rage, take the frustration, and put it somewhere it does damage. Don't let them sell you false hope. Channel that anger into building something real--for yourself, your family, for your country. Let's give these guys exactly what they've earned this fall -- a massive, historic electoral defeat that ends this presidency in everything but name, turns Donald Trump into the lamest of lame ducks, and clears the way for a new generation of Democratic leadership. Leadership that can actually fix this broken economy, undo the damage, and -- most importantly -- deliver some accountability for the staggering corruption inside this administration. I believe we can do all of it. Hang tough. With urgency, --Mike Mike Nellis is a Democratic strategist and entrepreneur who has raised over $1 billion for Democratic campaigns and causes. [1]Justice Democrats

Peter,

Recently, House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries was asked what the
Democratic Party’s agenda would be if it wins control of Congress in this
November’s midterm elections. And his response tells you everything you
need to know:

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260910.4vEIgq&refcode=em20260910-38248&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1002&akid=38248%2E1203867%2E6ylfKM ]Tweet from @sahilkapur: "What @RepJeffries told me the House agenda
will be next year if Democrats win control in the 2026 midterms: —Reverse
Trump's Medicaid cuts —Extend expired ACA tax credits —Restore Congress's
authority on tariffs —"Decisively" end the Iran war... Beyond that: "We've
established five working groups on affordability.""; attached is a still
from a C-SPAN broadcast of House Democratic Leader Jeffries holding news
conference on spending bill, with him standing at a podium

Reverse. Extend. Restore.

A bold strategy to turn back the clock 2-4 years every 4-6 years... how
ambitious.

Refusing to think big and go bold, Jeffries and establishment Party
leaders are perfectly content with simply returning to the pre-Trump
status quo.

But the pre-Trump status quo was never good enough for working families
across the country.

Instead of championing hugely popular and transformative policies like
Medicare for All, they’re proposing a few working groups and outdated
talking points. They have:

No plans to change our broken, profit-driven healthcare system.
No plans to get corporate money out of politics.
No plans to stop sending endless, unconditional military funding to
Israel.
No plans other than upholding a status quo that has failed the working
class for decades.

With less than eight weeks until the midterms, we’re ready to show Party
leaders that we’re tired of the Do-Nothing politics they refuse to let go
of.

We’ve already elected 7 Justice Democrats so far this year, and now we
have the chance to send 3 more to Congress to clean house and fight for
the people-first policies we desperately need and deserve.

But unlike our opponents, we don’t have billionaire donors, corporate PAC
checks, or AIPAC funding — we’re relying entirely on this grassroots team.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260910.4vEIgq&refcode=em20260910-38248&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1003&akid=38248%2E1203867%2E6ylfKM ]So Peter,
will you pitch in $5 now to help us unseat more Do-Nothing
Democratic incumbents this November?

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260910.4vEIgq&refcode=em20260910-38248&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1022&akid=38248%2E1203867%2E6ylfKM ]Contribute $5

In solidarity,

Justice Democrats

Friend, Tennessee has _always_ been the home of freedom fighters. Our state's history is written by _ordinary people_ who refused to accept the status quo and demanded a better, fairer future for _everyday Tennesseans._ From the Anderson County miners who broke the corrupt convict lease system during the Battle of Coal Creek, to the activists and mothers who secured women's suffrage during the War of the Roses, the Clinton 12 who courageously integrated their high school against mob violence, the students who dismantled Jim Crow during the Nashville Sit-Ins, and the Memphis sanitation workers and civil rights leaders who marched under _"I Am A Man"_ banners for economic justice _—_** _This is and has always been the true fighting spirit of Tennessee._** **The fight for justice, dignity, and opportunity didn't end with past generations, and _it's time for us to take up our rightful torch this November._** Jerri Green is _carrying that torch forward_ in her historic run for Governor. Jerri is fighting to _fully fund our K-12 public schools_ and _expand universal Pre-K_ instead of draining our communities with voucher schemes. | | Dear Fellow American, Classic children's literature is being ignored and eliminated from our nation's classrooms at an alarming rate. Beloved classics like _The Wind in the Willows_ , _Treasure Island_ , and _The Adventures of Huckleberry Finn_ are just a few of the foundational books that are rarely being taught to our nation's children today. Not only does this rob young people of classic tales of adventure and friendship, but they also rob children of fundamental lessons about the world and how best to live.
