name: Kristan Hawkins, Students for Life
subject: “watch your back”
body:
A crazed pro-abort came barreling out of the house and chased her down the driveway.
---
[View in Web Browser](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e5985531/VaHR0cHM6Ly93cm8ubnVjbGV1c2VtYWlsLmNvbS9hbXBsaWZ5L3YvcHB2ZVpQdmh3Zg/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjA5MTA/LbmNsQUJsRlF6bQ/qP2hpZHM9bmNXR0tDTXlkdUc1NFdscw/gaqLZMw/sbv98f628c1)
| | | | | |
---
| |
---
| | |

[](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)

Dear Friend,

_“I rang the doorbell, and a lady answered.”_

That’s how Grace’s story starts.
[](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
She introduced herself. Told the woman she was volunteering to protect preborn babies. Asked politely if she could count on her vote.

The woman said “no, thank you.” Grace said have a good day and turned to leave.

**That’s when someone screamed from inside the house. A second woman ran out the door – she chased Grace down the driveway, shoved her, and hit her in the head with both fists.**

As Grace tried to run away and reached the end of the driveway, the woman threw a dinner roll that hit her in the face – **and kept following her down the street, screaming that she hoped Grace would be run over by a car.**

Grace filed a police report. The woman was arrested and charged.

My name is Kristan Hawkins, and I’m the President of Students for Life Action. You can think of us as the grassroots arm of the Pro-Life Movement.

Friend, this is just one story from one of Students for Life Action’s door-to-door canvassers during the last midterm election.

I’ve told every one of our canvassers to prepare for anything over the next two months.

I wish I could tell you Grace’s story was a one-off. It isn’t. Doors get slammed. Voices get raised. Sometimes it gets violent.

And yet our canvassers keep walking up the next driveway because they know if the Abortion Lobby seizes power in November, it will be a death sentence to millions more innocent preborn babies.

**_[Friend, will you please prayerfully consider sending a Care Package to one of our door-to-door canvassers heading into the field this fall](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)_**?

These young women and men will be walking for hours in scorching heat. Knowing pro-lifers like you have their backs will help keep them going.

Of course, I could tell our door-knockers to go home.

I could focus on running expensive TV ads instead.

But studies show that face-to-face conversations move voters more than any TV ad, mailer, or text ever could – and the effect doesn’t disappear after one election.

**Voters who talk to one of our students in person are more likely to show up and vote pro-life again in the _next_ election cycle, too.**

_And, it only costs us about $3 for every door we knock._

Not only that, but we’ll be deploying teams of pro-life activists to blanket church parking lots with flyers exposing the records of pro-abortion politicians in key districts every Sunday in September and October.

This is the on-the-ground grassroots campaigning that’s needed to turn out every pro-life voter.

Last cycle, this approach worked.
***** In Oklahoma,** our student canvassers knocked 633 doors, made 26,931 phone calls, and sent 26,078 texts exposing two pro-abortion senators who killed our Chemical Abortion Pill Trafficking Bill – and voters threw them out.

***** In South Carolina,** we knocked 2,572 doors and made 51,371 calls exposing three pro-abortion Republican senators who protected the _Life at Conception Act’s_ enemies – and they lost too.

***** In North Carolina,** 1,052 doors and 52,554 texts helped four pro-life candidates win their primaries outright.
That’s just a small sample of what our door-to-door canvassing team has done over the years. The Abortion Lobby would love nothing more than for our students to stay home this fall.

Right now, we’re already deployed and expanding over the next two months, where this election gets decided door by door. Our target map for the 2026 Midterms is the most ambitious we’ve run:
**> >> Idaho and Missouri** – ballot referendum battles where the Abortion Lobby is trying to buy a win at the ballot box.

**> >> Georgia, Iowa, Michigan, North Carolina, Ohio, Texas** – U.S. Senate races that could decide who controls the chamber.

**> >> Georgia, Iowa, Michigan, Ohio, North Carolina, Pennsylvania** – Gubernatorial and state legislative races that will shape abortion law for years.

**> >> California’s 13th, Iowa’s 3rd, Michigan’s 10th, Pennsylvania’s 10th, North Carolina’s 1st, Ohio’s 9th, and Texas’s 34th** – U.S. House battlegrounds where a few thousand doors could flip a seat and determine control of Congress.
We’ll be active in at least ten states in races up and down the ballots. And every single one of them needs boots on the ground before Tuesday, November 3rd.

Friend, the Abortion Lobby has the money, the media, and the institutions. What they don’t have is thousands of young pro-lifers willing to knock on a stranger’s door, get yelled at, sometimes get hit with worse than words – and go knock on the next door anyway.

That grit and determination is what wins elections.

**_[So, will you please prayerfully consider making your most generous contribution to fund our canvassers as they head into the two most important months of this election](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)_**?
**> >> $1,200** fully funds FIVE pro-life canvassers for an entire day in the field – roughly 400 doors knocked, one voter conversation at a time.

**> >> $240** fully funds a canvasser’s entire day in the field – roughly 80 doors knocked, one voter conversation at a time.

**> >> $70** covers a canvasser’s gas for a full weekend of door-knocking.

**> >> $50** puts a canvassing team through a full Church Parking Lot Blitz weekend – flyers, printing, and all.

**> >> $25** pays for a canvasser’s meals for a day in the field.
Grace didn’t quit after that driveway. And this fall, our students won’t quit either.

But they need to know you’re behind them.

Kristan Hawkins
President, Students for Life Action
P.S. – Our door-to-door pro-life canvassers will be active in at least ten states this fall, targeting races up and down the ballot. Knowing pro-lifers like you have their back will help them keep going. **_[Will you please chip in $250, $100, $50, $25, or $10 right now to keep our canvassers moving – and protected – all the way through Election Day](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)_**?

Contributions or gifts to Students for Life Action are not tax deductible for IRS purposes; they do, however, avoid recognition of gain on appreciated assets. Any donations raised above or short of the goal will be used in the next area of greatest need towards our mission, as determined by the organization._

108 S Washington St. Suite 200
Alexandria, VA 22314

name: Ken Burns
subject: Coming to you with a heartfelt request...

body:
Eugene Vindman deserves your support.
#

[](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/evfc-em-aug26?refcode=em260910-4-ken-burns&refcode2=1105_3892029_22gF1K&akid=1105%2E3892029%2E22gF1K)
---
Hi, it’s Ken Burns. I am coming to you with a heartfelt request:
[**If you, like me, are deeply concerned about the future of our democracy and the rising tide of extremism, I urge you to join me in supporting Eugene Vindman’s reelection campaign for Congress today.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/evfc-em-aug26?refcode=em260910-4-ken-burns&refcode2=1105_3892029_22gF1K&akid=1105%2E3892029%2E22gF1K)
As a filmmaker, my life’s work has been dedicated to capturing pivotal moments in American history — moments that have shaped our nation’s identity and spirit. I’ve documented our country navigating through its darkest hours and emerging stronger and understanding the profound consequences of these moments.
Throughout my career, I’ve seen our nation evolve in countless ways, but one constant remains: our democracy, the cornerstone of our republic, and the essence of what it means to be American.
Yet, at this very moment, our democracy faces an unprecedented challenge — a critical inflection point. We are at a juncture where our very rights and freedoms are threatened.
The stakes have never been higher. Our democracy stands at a crossroads — and this moment requires leaders who will unify our country in defense of the very fabric of our nation — no matter political party or affiliation. Eugene Vindman is one of those leaders.
I first met Eugene and Alex nearly 40 years ago, when I interviewed the Vindman twins and their grandmother for a documentary about the meaning of the Statue of Liberty. It was shortly after they fled Soviet Ukraine and sought refuge in the United States as children.
[](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/evfc-em-aug26?refcode=em260910-4-ken-burns&refcode2=1105_3892029_22gF1K&akid=1105%2E3892029%2E22gF1K)
Their father came to the U.S. with $759 in his pocket, three children, and a dream of giving them a better life. And through hard work and perseverance, they achieved just that.
Eugene’s story is the embodiment of the American dream. He is a Ukrainian immigrant, an Army Veteran, and a lifelong defender of our democracy. He’s a good man — one who has devoted himself to defending our country with courage, selflessness, and resilience, even at his own expense.
Eugene has never failed to hold our leaders accountable — no matter their party. But right now, not only is our government baselessly retaliating against him through an investigation aimed at removing him from Congress, but he is being attacked relentlessly by the far right, all because he has never failed to hold our leaders accountable.
We need to keep people like Eugene in Congress — leaders who continue to stand up for our democracy and represent the true spirit of America.
So it would mean a lot to me if you could support his reelection campaign today to help keep him fighting for us in the People’s House.
[**Can you please contribute $25 or whatever you can afford to Eugene Vindman’s campaign for Congress today? I am asking because it is critical.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/evfc-em-aug26?refcode=em260910-4-ken-burns&refcode2=1105_3892029_22gF1K&akid=1105%2E3892029%2E22gF1K)

It worked - but it emptied our account. Winning a runoff doesn't put a dollar back in the bank. Annie Andrews has $4.1 million. I promised South Carolina I'd carry the conservative agenda to the Senate for six more years. President Trump stood with me and told you why he trusts me, too. I'm not letting her bank account break that promise. The general is November 3 - less than 65 days out. Every week from now until then, she's on TV, in your mailbox, on your phone. name: Elizabeth Warren
subject: I wrote a new book called The New Middle Class — and I’d love to tell you all about it:
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Warren for Senate
body:
| | | [ ](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/216?t=3&akid=3016%2E4032634%2EdZvmaO)
---
I wanted to share some news with you directly: I teamed up with my daughter Amelia to write a book called [_**The New Middle Class**_](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/3792?t=8&akid=3016%2E4032634%2EdZvmaO) — and I’d love to tell you all about it. | [](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/3792?t=9&akid=3016%2E4032634%2EdZvmaO)
---

This is a guide for anyone who is trying to figure out how to not just survive — but really thrive — in our rigged economy. That’s right: rigged.
Look, the rules we’ve been told to follow — work hard, buy a home, save a little each month to build a secure middle-class life — are not working. Over the last few decades, the rich and powerful have twisted our economy to work for them and our government has been more than happy to enable it.
Housing, college, and health care costs have all exploded. Jobs are less predictable. And retirement feels further away than ever. **The old rules of living and budgeting no longer apply.**
Through writing _The New Middle Class_ , we wanted to offer an easy-to-understand guide with tools and strategies for readers to build an actually sustainable American dream. Think of it like a modern day follow-up to our books _The Two-Income Trap_ and _All Your Worth: The Ultimate Lifetime Money Plan_.
[**This book is for anyone who wants to know more about how our economic system REALLY works so you can take control of your money and build financial stability in the world as it is. If you’d like to preorder my new book The New Middle Class, click here to learn more.**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/3792?t=10&akid=3016%2E4032634%2EdZvmaO)
Before ever becoming a senator, I spent my career studying why families go broke and fighting to rebuild the middle class.
After Wall Street crashed our economy in 2008, I fought to create the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau to protect people from getting scammed by big banks and corporations.
After Senate Republicans vowed to block my nomination to serve as the CFPB’s first director, I went back home to Massachusetts and launched a campaign to make our economy fairer for working families — and we won.
_The New Middle Class_ draws on those decades of research, public service, and real-world experience.
If you want to learn how to build a safety net to protect you in a precarious economy, stay ahead of a shifting world of work, be more strategic on housing, avoid dangerous scams, and plan for whatever comes next, this book is for you.
[**I’m excited for this to be out in the world, and I hope you are too. Click here to learn more and to pre-order my new book The New Middle Class.**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/3792?t=11&akid=3016%2E4032634%2EdZvmaO)
Elizabeth

Sixty-three thousand students, 261 campuses, and one inescapable conclusion: free expression on campus is in its worst shape yet -- and the year's defining act of political violence made it measurably worse.
On September 9, 2026, the Foundation for Individual Rights and Expression (FIRE) released its seventh annual College Free Speech Rankings, the largest survey of campus expression in the country. This year's edition covers 261 colleges and universities, built from nearly 63,000 undergraduate responses, and its headline finding is sobering: the assassination of Charlie Kirk on September 10, 2025, generated what FIRE describes as "a wave of censorship at America's colleges over the past year," deepening a climate in which far too many students already feared saying what they think.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/1be83cef-f135-4f23-a9de-786f81cf9ad3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**Kirk 's murder becomes the question students can't discuss**
The most striking new data point: 44% of students nationally now identify Charlie Kirk -- his assassination, or defending or criticizing him -- as one of the most difficult topics to discuss on campus. At Utah Valley University, where Kirk was shot while tabling on campus, the number is 62%, making it the single most difficult topic there.
That a specific political murder has, within one year, risen to sit alongside the Israeli-Palestinian conflict in the pantheon of unspeakable subjects tells you everything about the moment. The full list of hardest topics nationally includes:
\- The Israeli-Palestinian conflict -- still the most difficult topic overall (~50%)
\- Charlie Kirk's assassination (44%)
\- Donald Trump
\- Abortion
\- Immigration
\- Transgender rights
It's a portrait of a generation navigating its campuses not as marketplaces of ideas, but as minefields.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/e7e53496-60d4-42bf-8cca-472681f55789?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**Comfort down, self-censorship up**
Beyond the headline, the underlying trend lines are all moving the wrong way. FIRE's report finds:
\- Comfort expressing views is down across the survey;
\- Self-censorship is up -- more students report holding their tongues at least sometimes;
\- The trajectory continues what FIRE documented just days before Kirk's murder last year: a record and steadily rising share of students who say that shouting down speakers, blocking events, or even using violence to stop speech is acceptable "to some extent."
**Who rose, who sank**
The rankings themselves deliver the usual mix of vindication and humiliation:
The top of the class: Coverage of the release reports Claremont McKenna College taking the No. 1 spot for the second time, with Purdue University and the University of Chicago rounding out the top three (Chicago and Purdue have both been perennial fixtures near the top since the rankings began). Other strong performers include Michigan Technological University and the University of Colorado Boulder. Purdue placed No. 3 among public universities and No. 7 overall, and the university has leaned into the badge proudly.
The bottom of the barrel: Texas State University, the University of Washington, and New York University anchor the bottom of the list. Barnard College finished last overall, with Columbia and Indiana University close behind -- a familiar neighborhood for Columbia, which has become a recurring case study in administrative capitulation under pressure.
Bright spots: Schools that revised policies and made good-faith fixes -- Dartmouth, Vanderbilt, and Yale -- saw meaningful jumps in the rankings, which is FIRE's implicit thesis: campus speech climates respond to leadership, not fate. In Florida, Florida State (No. 21) and USF (No. 22) led the state, while FAU earned a D-, with coverage noting the Kirk-reaction fallout as a factor.
**Why this year 's rankings matter more than the last**
Every year's rankings come with a "worst ever" pronouncement, and there's a temptation to tune it out as a broken record. What's different in 2027 is the cause FIRE identifies. This isn't merely the accumulation of speech codes and shaky administrators -- it's the aftershock of an act of political assassination committed on a college campus, followed by a nationwide purge-let of firings, suspensions, and investigations targeting people who celebrated or even too-coldly commented on Kirk's death.
The result is a campus environment where a majority of students can't discuss the hardest topic of the day at all, where self-censorship is the norm rather than the exception, and where, per FIRE's earlier surveying, roughly one in three students now express at least some support for using violence against speech.
FIRE's own framing puts it bluntly: the Kirk murder added "another difficult topic to a dismal climate for student expression."
**The takeaway for readers choosing a school**
For parents and students using these rankings as intended -- a consumer guide -- the lesson of 2027 is double-edged. There are still campuses where students can speak, argue, and be wrong out loud: Claremont McKenna, Purdue, Chicago, and their peers prove it's possible. But the broader picture is that the median American campus is now a place where nearly half of students are afraid to touch the single most-discussed event of the year.
A university that can't host a conversation about a murder that happened on another university's lawn isn't performing education. It's managing risk.

SCOTUS Takes Up Citizenship Verification

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/grantdemocracy/grant-report-july-16-12774991?e=c16f400a56)
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/5L5GRJWkoMo?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a)
| | **The Supreme Court Takes Up Citizenship Verification**
**By Justin Riemer, President, USGI, and Marshal Trigg, Counsel, USGI**
The Supreme Court will hear _Republican National Committee v. Mi Familia Vota_ on December 8, the latest round of litigation over Arizona’s 2022 election laws addressing citizenship verification and removal.
The RNC sought review of two issues. The first is whether the National Voter Registration Act (NVRA), or a 2018 federal consent decree the state entered into, prevent Arizona from requiring documentary proof of citizenship from applicants who register using the state’s own voter-registration form. Under that decree, Arizona cannot reject a state-form application submitted without such proof, but must instead register the applicant for federal elections only—as a so-called “federal-only” voter. The Ninth Circuit held that both do. The RNC [argues](https://us.list-manage.com/aocV4QnWPn0?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) that the ruling improperly applies restrictions governing the federal registration form to a separate form created by the State.
The second issue concerns the NVRA’s 90-day pre-election restriction on systematic voter-list maintenance. Arizona law requires election officials to cancel a registration, irrespective of timing, when information obtained through periodic list reviews confirms that the registrant is not a U.S. citizen. The Ninth Circuit held that the NVRA bars Arizona from carrying out those removals during the 90 days before a federal election. The RNC argues that the provision does not require states to retain registrations of people who were never eligible to register.
Although this case remains a blockbuster, the RNC did not seek review of every issue decided below. For example, the Ninth Circuit struck down state provisions that prohibited individuals who did not provide proof of citizenship from voting by mail or for President. The presidential voting restriction in particular would have presented the Supreme Court with a significant opportunity to clarify the breadth of Congress’s authority under the U.S. Constitution to regulate presidential electors. The vote-by-mail restriction involving an obscure provision of the NVRA was less significant from a constitutional law perspective but had considerable policy implications.
Arizona legislative leaders [separately petitioned](https://us.list-manage.com/x8VZ3bIYydM?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) the Court after losing in the Ninth Circuit on the State’s proof-of-residence requirement for the state registration form, the vote-by-mail restriction, and whether the law was enacted with discriminatory intent. The State of [Arizona](https://us.list-manage.com/14RP6cPizn0?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) petitioned the Court solely on the Ninth Circuit’s discriminatory intent ruling and on organizational standing. Both petitions technically remain pending.
Restoring Integrity and Trust in Elections (RITE), together with the Center for Election Confidence and the Honest Elections Project, filed an [amicus brief](https://us.list-manage.com/1n9PUKqnUDQ?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) on the merits last week supporting the RNC. A number of other organizations and public officials, including Secretaries of State, also [filed briefs](https://us.list-manage.com/16xESimDGzJ?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) supporting the RNC.
On balance, the odds slightly favor Supreme Court reversal of the Ninth Circuit on both issues. In 2024, the Supreme Court granted the RNC a [stay](https://us.list-manage.com/my5H3BjC5Jg?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) of a lower court ruling enjoining enforcement of the state registration form proof of citizenship requirement. Also in 2024, the Court issued a [stay ](https://us.list-manage.com/G7EYiOxTz9z?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a)of a Virginia federal district court ruling preventing Virginia from removing noncitizen voters within the 90-day pre-election period. However, given the Court’s recent ruling in the _Watson_ case rejecting the claim that mail ballots must be returned by Election Day, the ultimate result of _Mi Familia Vota_ is far less certain than some of the Court’s critics may assume.
---
| | | | |
---
| | **Arizona** At least 149,776 voters, nearly all in Maricopa County, [received](https://us.list-manage.com/ZbTVW4NAIpl?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) letters asking whether they had moved after comparisons between voter registration and driver’s license records flagged address discrepancies. A 2022 law requires monthly comparisons to help maintain the state’s voter rolls. **California** On August 31, a Marina del Rey petition circulator [was sentenced](https://us.list-manage.com/18rrB33Jkd4?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) to 18 months of probation and 120 hours of community service after she pleaded guilty to paying individuals, including homeless people on Los Angeles’s Skid Row, to register to vote. Prosecutors said she solicited petition signatures in exchange for money and, on several occasions, supplied her own address to homeless registrants.**Colorado** The Secretary of State’s office [announced](https://us.list-manage.com/21RTGn1gpj9?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) that Initiative 256, a proposed constitutional amendment limiting mid-decade congressional redistricting, qualified for the November ballot. Beginning with the 2028 election, the measure would prohibit changes to an approved congressional map without approval from the state’s Congressional Redistricting Commission and Supreme Court. Initiative 256 requires a 55% majority vote to become law.**Georgia** A state audit of roughly 8 million voter registrations [determined](https://us.list-manage.com/o6Rxaj6yM3S?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) that Georgia’s system generally prevents noncitizens from registering and found no evidence of widespread fraud. Auditors identified about 2,570 potential noncitizens who were placed in active or inactive status because of administrative failures, including 407 registrations with voting histories. They attributed the problems largely to driver’s license processing errors and county verification failures.**Iowa** Linn County [removed](https://us.list-manage.com/17276zYNWW6?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) 422 voters, roughly 85 percent of the registrations challenged, after a record 495 eligibility challenges this year. State law holds the bulk of the removals until after the November election.Johnson County election officials [completed](https://us.list-manage.com/t3UxGCTqARn?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) an initial review of 921 voter registration challenges. Eighteen voters requested cancellation or had already canceled their registrations, while officials resolved nine challenges without removal. Officials will review the remaining 894 registrations after the November election. **Michigan** The Michigan Auditor General [reported](https://us.list-manage.com/jFclWrkV_RC?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) that the state’s list-maintenance program canceled more than 300 noncitizen registrations and removed close to a million defunct records over the review period. The program found roughly 2,500 ballots cast in the names of voters who had since died over the prior four years, about a hundredth of a percent of votes cast. The audit findings are available [here](https://us.list-manage.com/XHm2rVroIlt?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a).**Montana** The State Administration and Veterans Affairs Committee [voted](https://us.list-manage.com/xccGuTWkstV?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) to subpoena Secretary of State Jacobsen for details on the voter data her office turned over to the Department of Justice in 2025, which included partial Social Security numbers and dates of birth.**Nevada** Secretary of State Cisco Aguilar’s office [confirmed](https://us.list-manage.com/tpEUSr95bh8?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) receiving seven DOJ subpoenas seeking Nevada voter data, an escalation after a federal court dismissed the DOJ’s civil suit for the state’s unredacted voter file.**New Jersey** House Republicans [are escalating](https://us.list-manage.com/hlQlmAXPu2V?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) their inquiry into New Jersey’s noncitizen voter registration error after Governor Sherrill responded to lawmakers’ questions by stating that affected residents had been notified and disputing that the SAVE America Act would have prevented the problem. U.S. Representative Jeff Van Drew, chair of the U.S. House Judiciary Committee’s Oversight Subcommittee, said he plans to hold a hearing, seek additional records from state election officials, and consider subpoenas if officials do not cooperate.**North Carolina** The 100 county boards of elections [have begun](https://us.list-manage.com/M87z6Qd8eO2?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) mailing absentee ballots, making North Carolina the first state to begin voting in the 2026 midterm general election. In-person early voting will run from October 15 through October 31, and Election Day and the absentee ballot return deadline are November 3.**Vermont** State officials [removed](https://us.list-manage.com/q9qUR2D6DiM?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) around 900 people from Vermont’s voter rolls after an audit found that the DMV had transmitted voter registration information for about 20,000 residents who had declined to register. Most remained on the rolls because they had separately indicated an intent to register, while officials removed those who had never voted or otherwise interacted with the election system. The errors appear to derive from the state’s transition to automatic voter registration and a later DMV data migration.**Wisconsin** The Wisconsin Elections Commission [voted](https://us.list-manage.com/FEPYnaXnPUC?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) to request voting-equipment audit logs from Milwaukee over a wrong-file error that delayed reporting of the August primary results, and to move toward a final determination on whether Green Bay violated state law by mailing duplicate absentee ballots.
---
|
---
| | **Colorado** Amendments to the Colorado Department of State Election RulesHearing: September 14, 2026The Secretary of State [noticed](https://us.list-manage.com/bcq2J0JZy65?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) proposed amendments to the office’s Election Rules, revising voter-registration matching criteria and mail-ballot envelope signature-capture requirements, among other changes, and implementing HB 26-1113. Written comments may be submitted through the September 14 hearing.**North Carolina** On September 4, the North Carolina Board of Elections [approved](https://us.list-manage.com/mPS3NW_Lnub?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) new guidelines for mail-in ballots in a split vote, hours before those ballots were sent to voters. The guidance changes how county officials handle certain ballot defects, including improperly sealed inner envelopes. Similar proposed rules were blocked from taking effect in the 2026 election.
---
|
---
| | **Federal Agencies** _**National Republican Congressional Committee v. Brown,**_**No. 26A274** _****_**(U.S.)** On September 4, the Supreme Court [granted](https://us.list-manage.com/D6V8Nw6d3oP?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) the National Republican Congressional and Senatorial Committees a stay of the Fourth Circuit’s decision setting aside Federal Communications Commission (FCC) guidance that extended discounted broadcast-advertising rates to political parties making coordinated ad buys and for certain joint fundraising ads. The Court held that the Fourth Circuit likely lacked statutory jurisdiction because the challengers sought judicial review while their application for review remained pending before the full Commission, and that the committees would suffer irreparable harm from losing favorable advertising rates before the midterms. **Arizona** _**Republican National Committee v. Mi Familia Vota**_**, No. 25-1017 (U.S.)** On September 5, the Center for Election Confidence, Restoring Integrity and Trust in Elections, and the Honest Elections Project [filed](https://us.list-manage.com/10Vpq7E_WFK?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) an amicus brief [urging the U.S. Supreme Court](https://us.list-manage.com/1BG5cabEEgV?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) to uphold two Arizona voter-registration laws—a documentary proof-of-citizenship requirement and a mandate to remove noncitizen registrants within 90 days of a federal election—that the Ninth Circuit held violated the National Voter Registration Act. Several other amicus briefs were also [filed](https://us.list-manage.com/155EWUl5Okw?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) in support of the state and RNC. The Court granted review in July and set argument for December 8, 2026.**Delaware** _**Hocker v. Albence**_**, No. 2026-1021 (Del. Ch.)** On September 4, a state court [upheld](https://us.list-manage.com/OPNfWU1lxsb?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) Delaware’s permanent absentee voting law against a state constitutional challenge, holding that the statute (which permits qualifying voters to keep receiving absentee ballots without reapplying each election) does not expand who may vote absentee, since a voter’s status is canceled once the qualifying condition ends.**District of Columbia** _**Trujillo v. U.S. Department of Homeland Security**_ , **No. 1:26-cv-03072 (D.D.C.)** On September 2, the Coalition for Humane Immigrant Rights and a naturalized citizen [filed suit](https://us.list-manage.com/zFD0Tula9JE?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) in federal court to stop the Department of Homeland Security from pressing California to match its voter rolls against federal databases and to force rescission of a letter demanding the state’s voter file, arguing the database comparisons wrongly flag naturalized citizens as noncitizens._**League of Women Voters v. U.S. Department of Homeland Security**_**,**_****_**No. 26-5243** _****_**(D.C. Cir.)** On September 4, the D.C. Circuit [denied](https://us.list-manage.com/xu1hV9RyjkJ?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) the government’s request to stay a district court order setting aside the "modified SAVE" changes that let the citizenship-verification system run searches on full or partial Social Security numbers, holding the government had not made a strong showing of likely success on its Social Security Act claim. The court expedited the consolidated appeals.**Hawaii** _**Public Interest Legal Foundation v. Nago**_**, No. 1:23-cv-00389 (D. Haw.)**_****_ The Center for Election Confidence [announced](https://us.list-manage.com/OcS7UPekCnP?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) that former U.S. Solicitor General Paul Clement filed an amicus brief urging the U.S. Supreme Court to review the Ninth Circuit’s decision exempting the statewide voter file from the NVRA’s public transparency provisions. The Honest Elections Project also [filed](https://us.list-manage.com/8yNODS39mj8?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) an amicus brief urging the U.S. Supreme Court to take up the Ninth Circuit appeal.**Indiana** _**Deery v. Copenhaver**_ , **No. 26A-EX-2271 (Ind.)** On September 3, the Indiana Supreme Court [stayed](https://us.list-manage.com/VbpAKF8Qna4?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) the issuance and distribution of general-election ballots for state Senate District 23 across six counties while it weighs an appeal of the recount that left the original winner of the state senate race three votes behind his opponent. Argument is scheduled for September 10.**Maryland** _**Wheatley v. Maryland State Board of Elections**_**, No. C-09-CV-26-000285 (Md. Cir. Ct., Dorchester Cnty.)** On August 28, a state trial court [held](https://us.list-manage.com/H1f9aFv3zyt?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) that the General Assembly violated the state constitution, the Declaration of Rights, and state election laws by approving a proposed constitutional amendment on congressional redistricting. The court found that the legislature passed misleading ballot language and failed to comply with applicable deadlines. The court enjoined the question from appearing on the November ballot but [stayed]() the order pending appeal to the state Supreme Court.On September 3, the Supreme Court of Maryland [kept](https://us.list-manage.com/11UUkqRDemj?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) the proposed amendment on the November ballot but ordered its ballot summary rewritten, holding the language voters would have seen was misleading and violated due process.**Massachusetts** _**State of California v. United States Postal Service**_**, No. 1:26-cv-13917 (D. Mass.)** On August 28, the federal government [petitioned](https://us.list-manage.com/mF_8EQzmXin?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) the First Circuit to stay an August 27 temporary restraining order preventing the U.S. Postal Service (USPS) from enforcing new mail-in ballot regulations. On September 8, the government [filed](https://us.list-manage.com/16MThPcIw8d?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) a reply supporting a separate stay request arguing that the U.S. Postal Service’s rulemaking authority encompasses envelope design and reporting requirements for federal ballot mail._**League of Women Voters of Massachusetts v. Trump**_**, No. 1:26-cv-11549 (D. Mass.)** On September 4, a federal district court [dissolved](https://us.list-manage.com/w_5yCi5rK7V?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) the August 27 temporary restraining order and granted a preliminary injunction enjoining enforcement of the challenged USPS regulations._**United States Postal Service v. State of California | Trump v. League of Women Voters of Massachusetts**_**,**_****_**No. 26A305 (U.S.)** On September 6, the federal government [filed](https://us.list-manage.com/sXPmf_mpdrP?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) a new application to the U.S. Supreme Court seeking to stay the preliminary injunction issued September 4 and [withdrew](https://us.list-manage.com/7AapDL_O3a2?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) its earlier application concerning the TRO. The state challengers [opposed](https://us.list-manage.com/Q6eyFRfp9aC?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) the application on September 9.**Michigan** _**Americans for Citizen Voting v. Michigan Board of State Canvassers**_**, No. 26A275 (U.S.)** On August 31, proponents of a proposed constitutional amendment requiring proof of citizenship to vote [asked](https://us.list-manage.com/TjQ34G8qeqv?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) the U.S. Supreme Court for an emergency injunction ordering Michigan officials to place the measure on the November ballot. The application states that the Board of State Canvassers voted to keep the petition off the ballot after a five-and-a-half-month review and that the Michigan Supreme Court had not acted on the proponents’ request for relief. On September 3, Justice Kavanaugh [declined](https://us.list-manage.com/XxwNImdyjBY?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) the emergency application. Later that day, the Michigan Supreme Court also declined expedited review, holding that petitioners were not entitled to mandamus relief compelling the board to approve the petition.**Minnesota** _**Public Interest Legal Foundation v. Simon**_ , **No. 0:24-cv-01561 (D. Minn.)** On August 28, the Eighth Circuit Court of Appeals [vacated](https://us.list-manage.com/e4yV0JqYTyS?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) a lower court’s merits ruling against the Public Interest Legal Foundation and remanded with instructions to dismiss its challenge to Minnesota’s exemption from the National Voter Registration Act’s records-disclosure requirement, holding the Foundation alleged only an informational injury and lacked standing.**Missouri** _**von Glahn v. Hoskins**_**, No. 26AC-CC00440 (Mo. Cir. Ct., Cole Cnty.);**_**Onder v. Missouri**_**, No. 4:26-cv-01424** __**(E.D. Mo.)** On September 3, the state Supreme Court unanimously [held](https://us.list-manage.com/_IP8JgidgzL?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) that Secretary of State Hoskins had incorrectly deemed a referendum petition insufficient. The petition sought a statewide vote on the congressional map enacted by state legislators in 2025. The court ordered the map to be submitted to voters in November, holding that the state’s 2022 districts will govern the general election unless voters approve the 2025 map, even though the August primaries were conducted under the newer districts. On September 8, Justice Kavanaugh [denied](https://us.list-manage.com/11ClLxksBXM?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) Missouri’s emergency appeal to the U.S. Supreme Court seeking a stay of the state Supreme Court ruling. Shortly after the state Supreme Court ruling, U.S. Representative Bob Onder filed a federal district court action seeking a temporary restraining order that would require the state to use the 2025 map. The court [granted](https://us.list-manage.com/sOrKXg9dC1v?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) the motion. Intervenor-defendants then sought a stay with the Eighth Circuit Court of Appeals which it denied, and then to the U.S. Supreme Court which the court [granted](https://us.list-manage.com/oGx2UplsV8V?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) this morning. This leaves the 2022 maps in effect for the upcoming election. After Secretary Hoskins instructed election officials to use the new map following the federal district court ruling, the Missouri Supreme Court [ordered](https://us.list-manage.com/P26pQ4ap46N?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) him to show cause why that did not violate its injunction and set a contempt hearing for today which just concluded.

| | The Democratic National Committee [is expanding](https://us.list-manage.com/NRBrFbKNtIp?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) its nationwide “voter protection infrastructure” ahead of the November midterms, including creating its first internal litigation department and deploying tens of thousands of election observers across the country. The Republican National Committee is pursuing its own strategies ahead of November, including currently litigating nearly 180 active election integrity cases across 37 states.The rate of mail ballots rejected for late arrival [increased](https://us.list-manage.com/78YmNbauOr8?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) during recent primary and general elections in roughly a dozen states, including states with competitive congressional and statewide races. The DOJ alleges that four noncitizens voted illegally in the 2022 or 2024 elections. A U.S. citizen was also charged with allegedly participating in his wife’s illegal voting. Pennsylvania Department of State officials said they cooperated with the investigation.General Dan Caine, Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, [stated](https://us.list-manage.com/gQ8rB3c52rB?e=c16f400a56&c2id=fe0a341e6e6069e01834adfd2665567a) in a letter to U.S. Senator Elissa Slotkin that the U.S. Armed Forces have no plans to deploy federal troops or federalized National Guard personnel to polling places during the November elections. He also said there are no plans to use those personnel to seize ballots, voting machines, or other election materials.

body:
Reflecting on the legacy of a true champion for America’s youth and conservative values| | |
---
One year ago today, our nation lost a fearless fighter, a devoted husband and father, and a deeply cherished friend to so many of us in the conservative movement: Charlie Kirk. It’s still difficult to process that a full year has passed since Charlie was taken from us. **In the days and months following that terrible day, we felt the profound weight of his absence – not just on college campuses or in political debates, but in the heart of our conservative family.** Charlie possessed a rare, generational courage. At a time when so many were content to stay silent, Charlie stepped directly into the fire. **He poured his life into empowering young Americans, defending our constitutional liberties, and unapologetically proclaiming his faith in God.** He believed with every fiber of his being that America’s best days were still ahead if we simply had the fortitude to stand up for the truth. As I reflect on his life today, I am reminded that Charlie didn’t fight out of anger – he fought out of love. Love for his family, love for our country, and love for the principles that make America the greatest nation on earth. While he is no longer with us, the torch he lit in the hearts of millions of young patriots burns brighter than ever. **His voice may be silent, but his life’s work continues to echo across high school and college campuses in every corner of our country.** Today, I ask you to join my family in honoring Charlie’s memory. Please keep his wife, Erika, their sweet children, and the entire Kirk family in your prayers as they navigate this painful anniversary. **May we honor Charlie’s legacy not just with our words, but by carrying forward his unwavering commitment to faith, family, and freedom.** God bless you, and God bless the memory of Charlie Kirk. _Rep. Eric Burlison_

Charlie possessed a rare, generational courage. At a time when so many were content to stay silent, Charlie stepped directly into the fire. He poured his life into empowering young Americans, defending our constitutional liberties, and unapologetically proclaiming his faith in God. He believed with every fiber of his being that America’s best days were still ahead if we simply had the fortitude to stand up for the truth. As I reflect on his life today, I am reminded that Charlie didn’t fight out of anger – he fought out of love. Love for his family, love for our country, and love for the principles that make America the greatest nation on earth. While he is no longer with us, the torch he lit in the hearts of millions of young patriots burns brighter than ever. His voice may be silent, but his life’s work continues to echo across high school and college campuses in every corner of our country. Today, I ask you to join my family in honoring Charlie’s memory. Please keep his wife, Erika, their sweet children, and the entire Kirk family in your prayers as they navigate this painful anniversary. May we honor Charlie’s legacy not just with our words, but by carrying forward his unwavering commitment to faith, family, and freedom. God bless you, and God bless the memory of Charlie Kirk. Rep. **I never imagined that I would become one of Donald Trump’s most outspoken opponents.**

I grew up in a working-class, conservative Catholic family in El Paso, Texas. My mother was a Mexican immigrant who became an American citizen. My father was a lifelong truck driver. The Fourth of July was practically sacred in our home.

I was raised to believe in hard work, personal responsibility, service and love of country.

After September 11th, I felt called to serve. I went to work at the Pentagon, spent a year in Iraq and served our country in national-security and counterterrorism positions under both Republican and Democratic presidents.

Eventually, I was asked to serve as Vice President Mike Pence’s homeland security and counterterrorism adviser.

I sat in the Situation Room. I staffed the White House Coronavirus Task Force. I entered those rooms believing that, no matter our political differences, everyone entrusted with the security of the American people would understand that the country came first.

Then I saw what was really happening behind closed doors.

**I watched Donald Trump treat a deadly pandemic like a political and public-relations problem. I watched expertise get dismissed, the truth get bent and dedicated public servants get pushed aside because they would not place loyalty to one man above their oath to the country.**

Decisions that affected millions of American families were repeatedly reduced to one question: What was best for Donald Trump?

For a long time, I told myself that staying meant I could help. That perhaps I could prevent something worse from happening.

But eventually, I had to ask myself a much harder question:

Was I helping protect the country -- or was my presence helping legitimize something I knew was dangerous?

In 2020, I resigned from the Trump administration. Then I went public.

I was terrified.

I knew speaking out could cost me my career, my livelihood and my family’s safety. The attacks came quickly. There were threats, smears and attempts to intimidate me into silence.

But silence costs more.

So I spoke out. I supported Joe Biden. I stood on the stage at the Democratic National Convention and supported Kamala Harris. And after spending most of my life as a Republican, I eventually became a Democrat.

Not because every belief I held changed overnight. Not because I suddenly agreed with every Democrat on every issue.

I became a Democrat because there comes a moment when party loyalty becomes complicity -- and country must come first.

Now, Trump is back in the White House, the guardrails are weaker, and Republicans in Congress have repeatedly chosen obedience over oversight. MAGA is no longer merely threatening to abuse power. We are living with the consequences.

**That is why I am writing to you today on behalf of Resist Reclaim Rebuild.**

Resist Reclaim Rebuild is a group of Democratic activists working to defeat MAGA candidates in the battleground races that will determine whether Donald Trump continues to enjoy virtually unchecked power -- or whether we elect a Congress capable of standing up to him.

They understand that resistance cannot exist only in speeches, television interviews, or social media posts.

It MUST reach the ballot box.

It MUST be organized.

And it MUST be focused on the races where a relatively small number of votes could mean the difference between a MAGA rubber stamp and a real check on Donald Trump’s power.

[**So, I'm asking personally: Will you donate $10, $25 or whatever you can afford today to help Resist Reclaim Rebuild defeat MAGA in the battleground races that matter most?**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138944195/645717547/-323302678?refcode=260910_rrr_troye&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMjAwMzEiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMTFjZDA5NzMtM2NhZC1mMTExLTliMzMtMDAyMjQ4MmE5MzNiIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=5xtjibp0BtY-MwB_jSyJFXHfN00Jfy1lrijfh1ssRrw=)[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138944196/645717548/949025562?refcode=260910_rrr_troye&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMjAwMzEiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMTFjZDA5NzMtM2NhZC1mMTExLTliMzMtMDAyMjQ4MmE5MzNiIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=5xtjibp0BtY-MwB_jSyJFXHfN00Jfy1lrijfh1ssRrw=)

Eventually, I was asked to serve as Vice President Mike Pence’s homeland security and counterterrorism adviser. I sat in the Situation Room. I staffed the White House Coronavirus Task Force. I entered those rooms believing that, no matter our political differences, everyone entrusted with the security of the American people would understand that the country came first. Then I saw what was really happening behind closed doors. I watched Donald Trump treat a deadly pandemic like a political and public-relations problem. I watched expertise get dismissed, the truth get bent and dedicated public servants get pushed aside because they would not place loyalty to one man above their oath to the country. Decisions that affected millions of American families were repeatedly reduced to one question: What was best for Donald Trump? For a long time, I told myself that staying meant I could help. That perhaps I could prevent something worse from happening. But eventually, I had to ask myself a much harder question: Was I helping protect the country -- or was my presence helping legitimize something I knew was dangerous? In 2020, I resigned from the Trump administration. Then I went public. I was terrified. I knew speaking out could cost me my career, my livelihood and my family’s safety. The attacks came quickly. There were threats, smears and attempts to intimidate me into silence. But silence costs more. So I spoke out. I supported Joe Biden. I stood on the stage at the Democratic National Convention and supported Kamala Harris. And after spending most of my life as a Republican, I eventually became a Democrat. Not because every belief I held changed overnight. Not because I suddenly agreed with every Democrat on every issue. I became a Democrat because there comes a moment when party loyalty becomes complicity -- and country must come first. Now, Trump is back in the White House, the guardrails are weaker, and Republicans in Congress have repeatedly chosen obedience over oversight. MAGA is no longer merely threatening to abuse power. We are living with the consequences. That is why I am writing to you today on behalf of Resist Reclaim Rebuild. Resist Reclaim Rebuild is a group of Democratic activists working to defeat MAGA candidates in the battleground races that will determine whether Donald Trump continues to enjoy virtually unchecked power -- or whether we elect a Congress capable of standing up to him. They understand that resistance cannot exist only in speeches, television interviews, or social media posts. It MUST reach the ballot box. It MUST be organized. And it MUST be focused on the races where a relatively small number of votes could mean the difference between a MAGA rubber stamp and a real check on Donald Trump’s power. = | | | = MAGA wants us exhausted. They want every new outrage to make us feel a little more powerless. They want us to believe that one person speaking out, casting a ballot or making a contribution cannot possibly change anything. I learned the opposite. I learned that courage is contagious. Control of Congress could come down to only a handful of seats. Your contribution can help elect Democrats who will defend our Constitution, demand accountability and finally place a meaningful check on Trump’s unfettered power. Please help Resist Reclaim Rebuild fight for those victories today. = Stay informed. Stay compassionate. Stay hopeful. But above all, refuse to be silent. Olivia Troye | | | | Resist Reclaim Rebuild is an organization committed to helping Democrats win up and down the ballot, nationwide. # [Goldman's Hatzius just called time on the AI spend binge](https://substack.com/redirect/3b41ab0d-8fd8-4617-9f34-7bbc25911c99?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Goldman Sachs chief economist Jan Hatzius told the firm's Communacopia conference the AI spending surge **[will not go on forever,](https://substack.com/redirect/12eed9b3-49e1-4220-bdde-81d96619a211?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** even if the buildout proves productive.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/3b41ab0d-8fd8-4617-9f34-7bbc25911c99?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Two-phase cycle:** Hatzius said a new technology brings an investment phase when capex rises sharply, then an exploitation phase when the technology is used and investment volume falls.
* **Downside not excluded:** He said it is also possible many of the investments are not productive, a downside scenario that cannot be ruled out.
* **Baseline still constructive:** His working assumption is that AI spending is sustainable and productive and will contribute to stronger productivity growth later.
* **Political risk flagged:** A Citadel Securities note **[wrapped by ZeroHedge](https://substack.com/redirect/bc01acd4-90f9-46c2-89be-b59ae9f6f932?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** argues the more immediate threat to AI optimism is political, not a collapse in compute demand.

# [Nasdaq puts $100M into Kraken for stocks that never sleep](https://substack.com/redirect/3b41ab0d-8fd8-4617-9f34-7bbc25911c99?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Nasdaq Ventures is investing $100 million in Kraken parent Payward **[to launch tokenized equities in the second quarter of 2027,](https://substack.com/redirect/ab649f87-94bc-4c53-ae77-f1a60531852a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** lifting the crypto firm's valuation to $21 billion.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/3b41ab0d-8fd8-4617-9f34-7bbc25911c99?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Tokens are not shares:** Nasdaq said tokenized stocks are digital representations of public securities or other assets on a blockchain, and holders do not have outright ownership of the assets themselves.
* **Surveillance comes with it:** Payward will adopt Nasdaq's market-surveillance technology across its venues, including crypto and tokenized equities, as Kraken pushes beyond digital assets.
* **Cohen frames plumbing:** President Tal Cohen said the next market era will be defined by how efficiently capital and assets move, and that the Payward tie-up advances Nasdaq Equity Tokens.
* **Rights fight nearby:** The same report notes Robinhood's tokenized AMC products, which AMC calls a synthetic market without shareholder rights; Robinhood says firms cannot control how their stock is tokenized.

* * *
* * *
# [Goldman: Gold's $5,589 peak was a pause, not the top](https://substack.com/redirect/3b41ab0d-8fd8-4617-9f34-7bbc25911c99?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Goldman's metals desk said gold's bull market is not dead after an elongated pause, arguing new record highs are still coming as traders waited on U.S. inflation data.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/3b41ab0d-8fd8-4617-9f34-7bbc25911c99?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Twenty percent off peak:**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/083b106b-1728-4c9e-9b9e-1b3b633c4ca6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ZeroHedge said](https://substack.com/redirect/083b106b-1728-4c9e-9b9e-1b3b633c4ca6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** gold peaked in January, had a decent August, and is still sitting about 20% off that high.
* **Spot held overnight:** **[WSJ said](https://substack.com/redirect/143c41d4-e9f2-4604-bcf9-07a7b6c19b9c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** spot gold was flat at $4,399.41 an ounce in early Asian trade as investors awaited U.S. PPI and CPI.
* **Fed path in focus:** Zaner Metals' Peter A. Grant said the prints could clarify the Fed's rate path before next week's meeting.
* **Hot data would weigh:** Grant said hot inflation readings could fuel hawkish Fed bets, lift the dollar, and weigh on gold, which pays no interest.

* * *
* * *
# [Goldman: Rice, sugar, cocoa could jump 50-100%](https://substack.com/redirect/3b41ab0d-8fd8-4617-9f34-7bbc25911c99?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Goldman Sachs researchers Lina Thomas and Daan Struyven say crop inventories remain comfortable, but[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/11881351-adcf-4eeb-b186-bb6abfd0b488?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[they see upside risks to agriculture prices](https://substack.com/redirect/11881351-adcf-4eeb-b186-bb6abfd0b488?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** building from several shocks at once.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/3b41ab0d-8fd8-4617-9f34-7bbc25911c99?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Hormuz still listed:** GS GIR points to Hormuz disruptions as one of the supply shocks arriving even while inventories look comfortable.
* **Black Sea added:** Renewed Black Sea tensions are part of the same stack of upside risks to agriculture prices, the researchers say.
* **Super El Ni ño arriving:** A potentially historic Super El Niño is hitting at the same time as the shipping shocks, according to the Goldman note.
* **Protectionism can amplify:** Increasingly protectionist trade policies could amplify any supply shock, Thomas and Struyven warn.

Together, We Can Revive American Manufacturing and Jobs!
| | | | | [](https://a6x6czhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001LU3gsBG4Ma7dip3Yx9ycum86kgq3oQVGHP8Cg399DwMNC-lu9N9vov2o2lMNG0cKRkjJv9dextNPPPE-jKf4IkIy7qBK1WWfPQx5_TNb_DpryD9Z6awZ0f2ZogOknL9FW7lVZS-QWP93RXA8RIHBXSwGJPjtknUt&c=e-ZRek0-fBBukR1bA5GyV62Jcfj4u0LvSQTVLyI_mh4rKN-Q0YFElg==&ch=SlZTcXtYJd5lMMRM7d2kYb-CC7YanH-x2DKJjHMJFzzjLxqP29L1vg==)

| Friends,
Tonight, I had the honor of taking the stage at the Republican Convention to share Northwest Ohio's story with the country.
I talked about Toledo: a city built by American manufacturing, once home to a booming economy, growing population, and high-paying jobs. But for 43 years, Marcy Kaptur has been in Congress while too many factories closed, jobs disappeared, and American manufacturing moved overseas.
I shared my vision for a stronger Northwest Ohio: bring manufacturing jobs home, lower costs for working families, secure our border, support law enforcement, protect our elections, and put American workers first.
Most importantly, I delivered a message to Americans watching across the country:
Don't give up on the American Dream.

We live in the greatest country in the history of the world. I believe our best days are still ahead if we have the courage to fight for them.
It was an honor to represent Northwest Ohio on the national stage.
God Bless Ohio, and God Bless America!
In Service, Derek Merrin

**YOU WRITE THE BILL 2026 - Sept. 22** Ever thought about something that could be made better with appropriate legislation? Want more transparency in our government? Do you want to be heard? Join us Tuesday, September 22, at 5:30 pm at the Melrose Branch Library for our annual "You Write the Bill Workshop." You'll be able to learn about how a bill becomes law here in the Commonwealth, as well as work with others that share your passion to draft bills.
---
**LABOR DAY WEEKEND 2026** Another SWVA Labor Day Weekend in the books! We kicked off the long weekend marching in the Roanoke City Labor Day parade on Saturday, then celebrated on Sunday at dinner with our friends in Harrisonburg and Rockingham County, and finally wrapped up in Buena Vista on Labor Day. Thank you to all of the workers who keep this country moving forward.

name: The Texas Flyover
subject: Why Are So Many Drivers Suddenly Shopping Their Car Insurance?
body:
Your car insurance renews, you glance at the number, and somehow it's jumped again.
****

---
| | |
---
| |
# Thursday, September 10, 2026
---
**Dear Flyover Reader,** Today's partner is [Insurify](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyskDuO4zAQRE9DZTbYTUqWAgYLGM686YYCxW5ZBChRIHv9uf1AE80BJntAVb2g_t3Hu48pbo-_fmUn7zmPxBSDF6Zx41dNLMJlfC0fX7jm1W8fKvHJpdb_RLyNqLE76eEE-scSGnKTpgEadnDpB90Zo7tmcReGeTLWBDtjQDZhaofZhHZAOyEANtEdQj2Ahl6DtWfSPENLLWom49kqq5mi5HKWhYXfvs7pk59cziGvTXKLyF6V-aPwpvC2lywchCnvEvNWj9KRmJtX5gq2bxV24cC-x4MrKHNtiqP9FVOKtbsoqx-rj-nbL7_50dPhVwAAAP__5Uh_Fw), and honestly, this is one of those things that just makes sense to check. Car insurance rates have gone up a lot recently, and it only takes a few minutes to compare quotes and see if you could save money. The process is simple, and there's really no downside to seeing what other options are out there. -Cole, CEO
* * *
[](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyskDuO4zAQRE9DZTbYTUqWAgYLGM686YYCxW5ZBChRIHv9uf1AE80BJntAVb2g_t3Hu48pbo-_fmUn7zmPxBSDF6Zx41dNLMJlfC0fX7jm1W8fKvHJpdb_RLyNqLE76eEE-scSGnKTpgEadnDpB90Zo7tmcReGeTLWBDtjQDZhaofZhHZAOyEANtEdQj2Ahl6DtWfSPENLLWom49kqq5mi5HKWhYXfvs7pk59cziGvTXKLyF6V-aPwpvC2lywchCnvEvNWj9KRmJtX5gq2bxV24cC-x4MrKHNtiqP9FVOKtbsoqx-rj-nbL7_50dPhVwAAAP__5Uh_Fw) **A lot of people have had the same experience lately.** Your car insurance renews, you glance at the number, and somehow it's jumped again. Maybe by $20 a month. Maybe by $50. Maybe more. And yet nothing really changed. No accidents. No tickets. Same car. Same driving habits. It's happening all over the country right now. [Insurance companies have been raising rates aggressively](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyskDuO4zAQRE9DZTbYTUqWAgYLGM686YYCxW5ZBChRIHv9uf1AE80BJntAVb2g_t3Hu48pbo-_fmUn7zmPxBSDF6Zx41dNLMJlfC0fX7jm1W8fKvHJpdb_RLyNqLE76eEE-scSGnKTpgEadnDpB90Zo7tmcReGeTLWBDtjQDZhaofZhHZAOyEANtEdQj2Ahl6DtWfSPENLLWom49kqq5mi5HKWhYXfvs7pk59cziGvTXKLyF6V-aPwpvC2lywchCnvEvNWj9KRmJtX5gq2bxV24cC-x4MrKHNtiqP9FVOKtbsoqx-rj-nbL7_50dPhVwAAAP__5Uh_Fw) over the last few years, and many drivers are simply absorbing the increases because shopping for insurance feels like a hassle. Most people assume comparing rates means filling out endless forms, sitting through sales calls, or spending an entire afternoon jumping between websites. That's exactly why companies like [Insurify](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyskDuO4zAQRE9DZTbYTUqWAgYLGM686YYCxW5ZBChRIHv9uf1AE80BJntAVb2g_t3Hu48pbo-_fmUn7zmPxBSDF6Zx41dNLMJlfC0fX7jm1W8fKvHJpdb_RLyNqLE76eEE-scSGnKTpgEadnDpB90Zo7tmcReGeTLWBDtjQDZhaofZhHZAOyEANtEdQj2Ahl6DtWfSPENLLWom49kqq5mi5HKWhYXfvs7pk59cziGvTXKLyF6V-aPwpvC2lywchCnvEvNWj9KRmJtX5gq2bxV24cC-x4MrKHNtiqP9FVOKtbsoqx-rj-nbL7_50dPhVwAAAP__5Uh_Fw) have taken off. Insurify is a comparison platform that lets you check auto insurance quotes from multiple insurers in one place, side-by-side, in just a few minutes. Instead of manually visiting a dozen insurance websites, you answer a few questions once and quickly see what different companies may charge for similar coverage. [](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyskDuO4zAQRE9DZTbYTUqWAgYLGM686YYCxW5ZBChRIHv9uf1AE80BJntAVb2g_t3Hu48pbo-_fmUn7zmPxBSDF6Zx41dNLMJlfC0fX7jm1W8fKvHJpdb_RLyNqLE76eEE-scSGnKTpgEadnDpB90Zo7tmcReGeTLWBDtjQDZhaofZhHZAOyEANtEdQj2Ahl6DtWfSPENLLWom49kqq5mi5HKWhYXfvs7pk59cziGvTXKLyF6V-aPwpvC2lywchCnvEvNWj9KRmJtX5gq2bxV24cC-x4MrKHNtiqP9FVOKtbsoqx-rj-nbL7_50dPhVwAAAP__5Uh_Fw) And the differences can be surprisingly large. For families with multiple vehicles, teen drivers, long commutes, or recent renewals, [even modest monthly savings can add up fast over the course of a year](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyskDuO4zAQRE9DZTbYTUqWAgYLGM686YYCxW5ZBChRIHv9uf1AE80BJntAVb2g_t3Hu48pbo-_fmUn7zmPxBSDF6Zx41dNLMJlfC0fX7jm1W8fKvHJpdb_RLyNqLE76eEE-scSGnKTpgEadnDpB90Zo7tmcReGeTLWBDtjQDZhaofZhHZAOyEANtEdQj2Ahl6DtWfSPENLLWom49kqq5mi5HKWhYXfvs7pk59cziGvTXKLyF6V-aPwpvC2lywchCnvEvNWj9KRmJtX5gq2bxV24cC-x4MrKHNtiqP9FVOKtbsoqx-rj-nbL7_50dPhVwAAAP__5Uh_Fw). In a time when nearly every household bill seems to be creeping higher, many people are realizing this is one of the easier places to potentially cut costs without changing their lifestyle. The reality is most insurance companies count on inertia. They know many customers will simply renew year after year without checking competitors. But rates can vary dramatically from company to company, even for drivers with nearly identical profiles. That's why comparison shopping matters more today than it did a few years ago. | | | Friend,

Bill Hill is running as an "independent." His own record tells a different story.

**Federal campaign finance records show Hill personally donated to socialists Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, Bernie Sanders, and Kamala Harris.** When Alaskans put their own money behind AOC and Bernie Sanders, that tells you exactly where their politics are, no matter what label they put on the ballot.

And it's not just who Hill supports. It's who's supporting him.
**A Washington, DC-based super PAC has poured more than $2 million into propping up Hill's campaign — more than Hill has raised himself.**

The mailers in your mailbox, the TV ads, the texts on your phone? Paid for by outside, Lower 48 money. And the trail behind that PAC runs through a web of nonprofit organizations that never have to disclose their donors. Alaskans may never know who's really writing the checks to buy this seat.

**He won't even tell voters who he'd caucus with in Congress.**

See the records for yourself — FEC filings, news reports, the full money trail at **[www.TheRealBillHill.com](https://us.list-manage.com/xzOPSeDCl4x?e=6679001ba0&c2id=4b8979688b40abb82eda840804c92b8e)**.

Alaska's seat in Congress should be decided by Alaskans, not by anonymous donors in Washington and California. For Alaska,

Last week,
the House struck down H.J. Resolution 1 — the GOP's calculated attempt to
freeze the Supreme Court at nine seats, locking in their advantage for a
generation.

But make no mistake, the fight isn't over. The 6-3 conservative
supermajority is still on the bench. And it's still working against the
American people. Take a look:

* They gutted the Voting Rights Act, clearing the way for racial
gerrymandering.
* They rubber-stamped partisan maps that lock Republicans into power.
* They handed Trump broad immunity, reinforcing that the law doesn't
apply to a wannabe authoritarian president.

Every one of these rulings was a choice. The Roberts Court chose
billionaires over voters, corporations over workers, and Trump over the
Constitution it swore to defend.

Voters are done pretending this is normal, and the anger is turning into
action. Rep. James Clyburn recently called to expand the Court to a
"Baker's Dozen" — 13 justices who answer to the people, not to corporate
donors or Trump.

Expansion is the only way to break the conservative supermajority's grip
on our democracy and our futures. Right now, six justices hold power over
our rights, our elections, and our government. Adding seats restores real
independence to the highest court in the country.

That's the fight Demand Justice is building. We’re exposing the Supreme
Court’s corruption and organizing the public pressure we need for
structural reform.

body:
It all started in a small town in Aroostook County.
| Hi, it's Susan.I don't get to slow down and share this very often, so today I wanted to take a moment to tell you a bit about how I got here.I grew up in Caribou, Maine - one of six kids raised by my parents, Pat and Don. Both of them served as mayor of Caribou at one point, and my dad, a World War II veteran, went on to serve in the Maine Legislature. Public service just runs in the family - I'm actually the fourth generation of Collins' in public service.Our family also ran a small retail lumber business that's been passed down for six generations, dating back to 1844. Growing up around that kind of hard work taught me a lot about what it means to show up for your community, day after day.My path to Washington wasn't a straight line. I got my start working for a Maine congressman, followed him to the Senate, and eventually found myself championing small businesses - first at the state level, then with the Small Business Administration, and later running a center dedicated to family businesses.Eventually, I ran for the Senate myself, and I've been honored to serve Maine ever since - always trying to work across the aisle and get real results for the people back home.That's my story. clean_body: It all started in a small town in Aroostook County. | Hi, it's Susan.I don't get to slow down and share this very often, so today I wanted to take a moment to tell you a bit about how I got here.I grew up in Caribou, Maine - one of six kids raised by my parents, Pat and Don. Both of them served as mayor of Caribou at one point, and my dad, a World War II veteran, went on to serve in the Maine Legislature. Public service just runs in the family - I'm actually the fourth generation of Collins' in public service.Our family also ran a small retail lumber business that's been passed down for six generations, dating back to 1844. Growing up around that kind of hard work taught me a lot about what it means to show up for your community, day after day.My path to Washington wasn't a straight line. I got my start working for a Maine congressman, followed him to the Senate, and eventually found myself championing small businesses - first at the state level, then with the Small Business Administration, and later running a center dedicated to family businesses.Eventually, I ran for the Senate myself, and I've been honored to serve Maine ever since - always trying to work across the aisle and get real results for the people back home.That's my story. Aroostook County roots, a family that believed in service, and a lot of hard work along the way. | Warmly, Susan | The latest numbers out of Maine show Troy Jackson leading by 2 points.We've seen tight races like this before, and we know exactly what it takes to win them.
