An Iranian woman looks at fruit while shopping in the traditional Grand Bazaar in southern Tehran, Iran, on September 1, 2026, amid rising tensions between Iran and the United States. Photo by Morteza Nikoubazl/NurPhoto via Getty Images.
A video that recently went viral on Iranian social media shows people [eating caviar](https://substack.com/redirect/72fe2ab0-76f3-4ad4-ad09-b5f8703e5f29?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and rare salmon for breakfast in Tehran, a meal costing around 10 million tomans ($50), the monthly wage for many Iranians. Another viral video shows a man wrapping a thick piece of red meat between two layers of bacon, adding additional meat, and then wrapping the concoction in a bun soaked with fat.
Such videos have become increasingly popular in Iran as the country grapples with the rising cost of meat and other food staples.
The head of Iran's Association of Meat and Protein Products Packing Industry said in late May that in response to the high prices, demand for meat products had fallen 50% compared with the previous year. Last summer, one kilogram of mutton cost around 1 million tomans; this summer, the same portion reached 2 million tomans ($10).
The announcement of a new campaign of sanctions targeted against Iran on August 24--dubbed Operation Economic Outcast by the U.S. Treasury Department--and aimed at further turning the screws on the Iranian economy, has been met with a shrug by many ordinary Iranians already exhausted from trying to survive during a rapid collapse of living standards unseen in the country's modern history.
The new campaign, which has so far included the sanctioning of several banks and airlines servicing Iran, comes on top of a blockade of the country's southern ports, which has halted the import of basic resources. As the sanctions campaign continues, the Iranian rial has collapsed, falling Wednesday to a record low of roughly 2.34 million rials to the dollar, making already scarce imports dramatically more expensive.
Iranians have now been forced to navigate a situation in which obtaining the bare necessities of life requires accepting potentially ruinous personal debts, or is simply impossible.
"A packet of tea that used to cost 300,000 to 600,000 tomans [$2-4] now costs one million tomans [$5] after the war. Why should a packet of tea cost one million tomans when a worker's daily wage is not even one million tomans? If you are a day laborer, you have to give up even buying tea," said a construction worker in Tehran, who like others who spoke to Drop Site for this article, requested anonymity to avoid retaliation. "Soap, dental floss, tobacco, and goods like these have become unaffordable for us. Our situation has become embarrassing. To buy the personal hygiene products we actually want, we have to take out loans."
## Food and Medicine
While the Iranian government initially sought to cushion the economic crisis at the start of the year by [providing](https://substack.com/redirect/69dca700-1789-42b5-ae02-283cdec38273?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) approximately 80 million people with monthly electronic food credits for four months, worth 1 million tomans--about $7 when the program was announced--the payments were rapidly eroded by inflation and the rial's continuing collapse.
At the start of the calendar year, the country's minimum wage rose to 10 million tomans per month, equivalent at the time to $100. But with the outbreak of the war and a rise in the dollar exchange rate, the minimum wage by September had once again fallen to the equivalent of $80--even as the price of food rose 3.6% in August alone and stood approximately 128% higher than a year earlier.
According to Consumer Price Index (CPI) reports published by Iran's Statistical Center, which measure the price of a basket of basic items for each household, prices for basic goods are 2.7 times higher than two years ago, while wages have not moved or have even declined.
"Before, even buying small quantities of fruit was a source of embarrassment, and people would feel ashamed, for example, to buy half a kilo of something. But now, even buying fruit one piece at a time is no longer something to be ashamed of. People simply don't have the money to spend, and those who have children or a pregnant wife cannot cut fresh fruit and vegetables from their shopping list," said a 35-year-old resident of Tehran. "I'm not even talking about expenses like entertainment or going to restaurants. Ordinary household shopping alone eats up an average salary. The reason you walk around the city and see everyone angry and arguing with each other is this situation. People see that they are constantly working, but every day they are getting poorer. These things put a lot of pressure on people's nerves."
Even though many people have cut parts of their diets, such as protein, dairy products, or fresh vegetables, because of economic pressures, the financial burden of rising medical prices continues to weigh on them.
Sanctions and the naval blockade, which have prevented raw materials needed for the production of medicines from entering Iran--along with the destruction of a large number of pharmaceutical manufacturing plants during the war--have had a significant impact both on the availability of medicines and on their cost.
"The increase in the price of raw materials, the inability to secure foreign currency, and other economic problems have caused medicine prices to rise and production to decline. On the other hand, because pharmacists cannot adjust their selling prices in line with their costs, it costs them more to produce the medicines than they can sell them for, putting them under even greater pressure, which also affects the market," Dr. Shahram Kalantari, head of the Iranian Pharmacists Association, told the Mehr news agency. "All of this is happening while the government is unable to properly repay its debts to pharmacists and pharmacies, placing them under even greater economic pressure."
The prices of basic painkillers like ibuprofen and antibiotics like amoxicillin have doubled or tripled over the past year, leaving many Iranians in a constant struggle to track down lifesaving medicines which are normally widely available.
"Poverty in Iran has been increasing," said Javad Hoseini, the head of Iran's State Welfare Organization, according to ILNA, the Iranian labor news agency. "And today the population living below the absolute poverty line has risen from 16 million to 34 million people, while people's economic resilience has declined and Iran is facing the widespread nature of poverty."
That estimate came just weeks before the second wave of U.S. attacks, and before the new U.S. blockade and economic sanctions campaign that have raised the level of economic warfare against Iranians to an unprecedented level.
## Buy Now, Pay Later
In the absence of a functional economy where individuals can use their wages to purchase the goods they need, Iran has seen an explosion of short-term personal loan programs, referred to as "Buy Now, Pay Later" services, where individuals can use debt to finance the purchase of clothing, food, and small consumer goods.
An online women's clothing store that operates on Instagram launched its own loan service just two months after the most recent war began, citing what the store itself described as "numerous customer requests."
Yet even this stopgap measure has done little to keep the gears of the economy turning, as low cash liquidity in an economy increasingly running on debt and deferred payments means retailers lack the money to replenish their inventories. This summer, Iran's Purchasing Managers Index, known as the Shamkh, showed [contracting](https://substack.com/redirect/98ffe999-4198-4d56-9106-7e50967cf51f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) net figures for new orders, inventories, sales, and exports for the 16th consecutive month.
"The economic situation has become such that people genuinely need installment plans even to buy ordinary clothes for themselves. But the problem with buy-now-pay-later services is that they make it harder for us to buy and replace our raw materials," said the manager of a clothing store. "On the other hand, if we refuse to offer these services, our sales will decline. Selling the products and hoping that the money comes back is better than keeping the goods in storage and waiting for people's economic situation to improve."
While some U.S. officials initially framed the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran as an effort to liberate Iranians from authoritarian rule, the subsequent sanctions campaign and blockade have been bluntly described as a means of destroying Iranian society by deepening economic deprivation and provoking domestic unrest.
"We have the blockade, and we are going to have the toughest sanctions in history," Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent [said](https://substack.com/redirect/c1cbc358-e3ab-40dc-b59f-8730a027800b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in August, adding: "We are going to collapse this regime." Earlier, Bessent [told](https://substack.com/redirect/eabfa91e-d7ce-4806-b43b-ebcc3f41ec43?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the Senate Banking Committee that Washington had "created a dollar shortage" in Iran, sending its currency into freefall and causing inflation to explode--"and hence we have seen the Iranian people out on the street."
Iran's total trade has fallen by an estimated 25-35%, with imports declining faster than exports, while the workforce has dropped by about 450,000 from a year earlier, according to figures provided by the Iranian government. The International Monetary Fund forecasts that the economy will contract by 6.1% in 2026, as inflation drives up business expenses and consumers cut back their own spending, including on food and basic household goods.
While the U.S. sanctions are succeeding in causing the impoverishment of Iranians, there is little indication that they are set to trigger an uprising that would deliver victory in the U.S. campaign.
Many Iranians who spoke to Drop Site said that their concerns had shifted to merely surviving rather than pursuing political change or confronting a government that has intensified its hold on society amid the war.
"I can see with my own eyes that despite having a steady income--or sometimes even earning more money than I did in some previous months--I am getting poorer every day. When I go to a cafe, I have to go through the entire menu and choose the cheapest thing available. Even that cheapest option gets more expensive every day," said a 27-year-old student living in the city of Karaj. "Our lives weren't like this before. We didn't have to count every penny and calculate every expense. Like many others, I have turned to credit-payment services and installment purchases because I cannot afford the cost of living. A pair of sneakers costs the equivalent of one month's salary for a person in Tehran, and the 'buy now, pay later' services even exist for buying food, which shows just how bad people's economic situation has become. In such circumstances, it is obvious that everyone's focus just shifts toward survival."
## Rising Inequality
At the same time that the Trump administration announced its Economic Outcast program against Iran, Iranian government spokesperson Fatima Mohajerani, [responding](https://substack.com/redirect/f8f8c596-378e-4519-ba86-82de040cafc5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to a question about poverty rates in Iran in late August, told reporters: "The publication of statistics and figures related to the issue of poverty is subject to security restrictions. Although the government has the figures and statistics on this issue, it cannot make the numbers public."
The Iranian government's revenues are also declining day by day under the pressure of sanctions and restrictions on oil exports caused by the blockade.
President Donald Trump has repeatedly [claimed](https://substack.com/redirect/9bcac93d-6f4f-4d2a-8c77-3beacc141208?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that the Iranian government is unable to pay the salaries of its employees and security forces, though no such reports have emerged in Iran, and government employees and soldiers continue reporting for work.
But a recent announcement that the government plans to [increase](https://substack.com/redirect/75a235a3-623d-4d92-82e2-ba5c6b1aba92?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) consumer energy and gasoline prices inside Iran--both normally subsidized by government spending--shows clear signs that the country is under financial strain.
A large share of the expenditure items in Iran's current-year budget have been devoted to the war, even though most of the reconstruction work for war-related damage--estimated at between $20 billion and $40 billion, according to Meysam Zohourian, a conservative member of the Iranian parliament--has not even begun.
Iranian President Massoud Pezeshkian and Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, speaking publicly just days apart late last month, both warned that the costs of running the country must somehow be covered and that the welfare and essential needs of the population cannot be postponed indefinitely.
"No matter how strong we are militarily, if the people are hungry and we do not have financial circulation, economic growth and domestic production, we will not endure," said Ghalibaf on August 21. Days later, Pezeshkian echoed his sentiments with apparent frustration, stating, "Some say sanctions have no effect at all. I really don't know what to say to those people."
Their remarks were directed at domestic hardliners who made demands for major upfront sanctions relief and reparations a condition for negotiations, as well as other segments of the Iranian establishment alleged to be opposed to talks entirely. But the comments have also fueled speculation about the government's concerns over how much economic pressure the population can withstand.
At the same time, amid growing deprivation, the display of excesses such as wrapping red meat in bacon, or cafes serving caviar for breakfast has heightened the sense of inequality in Iran. In the comments section of an Instagram post showing the preparation of a meat dish, one user wrote: "Eating something like this even once has become a dream for me," while another added: "I hold the country's officials responsible for this situation."

This is essential to our mission: to report on what matters most, beholden only to the truth. In that spirit, we made a commitment to ensure that our journalism is free for everyone, not locked behind a paywall. But that means we rely on the voluntary support of our community of readers. Please consider making a. | | ---|---|--- An Iranian woman looks at fruit while shopping in the traditional Grand Bazaar in southern Tehran, Iran, on September 1, 2026, amid rising tensions between Iran and the United States. Photo by Morteza Nikoubazl/NurPhoto via Getty Images. A video that recently went viral on Iranian social media shows people and rare salmon for breakfast in Tehran, a meal costing around 10 million tomans ($50), the monthly wage for many Iranians. Another viral video shows a man wrapping a thick piece of red meat between two layers of bacon, adding additional meat, and then wrapping the concoction in a bun soaked with fat. Such videos have become increasingly popular in Iran as the country grapples with the rising cost of meat and other food staples. The head of Iran's Association of Meat and Protein Products Packing Industry said in late May that in response to the high prices, demand for meat products had fallen 50% compared with the previous year. Last summer, one kilogram of mutton cost around 1 million tomans; this summer, the same portion reached 2 million tomans ($10). The announcement of a new campaign of sanctions targeted against Iran on August 24--dubbed Operation Economic Outcast by the U.S. Treasury Department--and aimed at further turning the screws on the Iranian economy, has been met with a shrug by many ordinary Iranians already exhausted from trying to survive during a rapid collapse of living standards unseen in the country's modern history. The new campaign, which has so far included the sanctioning of several banks and airlines servicing Iran, comes on top of a blockade of the country's southern ports, which has halted the import of basic resources. As the sanctions campaign continues, the Iranian rial has collapsed, falling Wednesday to a record low of roughly 2.34 million rials to the dollar, making already scarce imports dramatically more expensive. Iranians have now been forced to navigate a situation in which obtaining the bare necessities of life requires accepting potentially ruinous personal debts, or is simply impossible. "A packet of tea that used to cost 300,000 to 600,000 tomans [$2-4] now costs one million tomans [$5] after the war. Why should a packet of tea cost one million tomans when a worker's daily wage is not even one million tomans? If you are a day laborer, you have to give up even buying tea," said a construction worker in Tehran, who like others who spoke to Drop Site for this article, requested anonymity to avoid retaliation. "Soap, dental floss, tobacco, and goods like these have become unaffordable for us. Our situation has become embarrassing. To buy the personal hygiene products we actually want, we have to take out loans." Food and Medicine While the Iranian government initially sought to cushion the economic crisis at the start of the year by approximately 80 million people with monthly electronic food credits for four months, worth 1 million tomans--about $7 when the program was announced--the payments were rapidly eroded by inflation and the rial's continuing collapse. At the start of the calendar year, the country's minimum wage rose to 10 million tomans per month, equivalent at the time to $100. But with the outbreak of the war and a rise in the dollar exchange rate, the minimum wage by September had once again fallen to the equivalent of $80--even as the price of food rose 3.6% in August alone and stood approximately 128% higher than a year earlier. According to Consumer Price Index (CPI) reports published by Iran's Statistical Center, which measure the price of a basket of basic items for each household, prices for basic goods are 2.7 times higher than two years ago, while wages have not moved or have even declined. "Before, even buying small quantities of fruit was a source of embarrassment, and people would feel ashamed, for example, to buy half a kilo of something. But now, even buying fruit one piece at a time is no longer something to be ashamed of. People simply don't have the money to spend, and those who have children or a pregnant wife cannot cut fresh fruit and vegetables from their shopping list," said a 35-year-old resident of Tehran. "I'm not even talking about expenses like entertainment or going to restaurants. Ordinary household shopping alone eats up an average salary. The reason you walk around the city and see everyone angry and arguing with each other is this situation. People see that they are constantly working, but every day they are getting poorer. These things put a lot of pressure on people's nerves." Even though many people have cut parts of their diets, such as protein, dairy products, or fresh vegetables, because of economic pressures, the financial burden of rising medical prices continues to weigh on them. Sanctions and the naval blockade, which have prevented raw materials needed for the production of medicines from entering Iran--along with the destruction of a large number of pharmaceutical manufacturing plants during the war--have had a significant impact both on the availability of medicines and on their cost. "The increase in the price of raw materials, the inability to secure foreign currency, and other economic problems have caused medicine prices to rise and production to decline. On the other hand, because pharmacists cannot adjust their selling prices in line with their costs, it costs them more to produce the medicines than they can sell them for, putting them under even greater pressure, which also affects the market," Dr. Shahram Kalantari, head of the Iranian Pharmacists Association, told the Mehr news agency. "All of this is happening while the government is unable to properly repay its debts to pharmacists and pharmacies, placing them under even greater economic pressure." The prices of basic painkillers like ibuprofen and antibiotics like amoxicillin have doubled or tripled over the past year, leaving many Iranians in a constant struggle to track down lifesaving medicines which are normally widely available. "Poverty in Iran has been increasing," said Javad Hoseini, the head of Iran's State Welfare Organization, according to ILNA, the Iranian labor news agency. "And today the population living below the absolute poverty line has risen from 16 million to 34 million people, while people's economic resilience has declined and Iran is facing the widespread nature of poverty." That estimate came just weeks before the second wave of U.S. attacks, and before the new U.S. blockade and economic sanctions campaign that have raised the level of economic warfare against Iranians to an unprecedented level. Buy Now, Pay Later In the absence of a functional economy where individuals can use their wages to purchase the goods they need, Iran has seen an explosion of short-term personal loan programs, referred to as "Buy Now, Pay Later" services, where individuals can use debt to finance the purchase of clothing, food, and small consumer goods. An online women's clothing store that operates on Instagram launched its own loan service just two months after the most recent war began, citing what the store itself described as "numerous customer requests." Yet even this stopgap measure has done little to keep the gears of the economy turning, as low cash liquidity in an economy increasingly running on debt and deferred payments means retailers lack the money to replenish their inventories. This summer, Iran's Purchasing Managers Index, known as the Shamkh, showed net figures for new orders, inventories, sales, and exports for the 16th consecutive month. "The economic situation has become such that people genuinely need installment plans even to buy ordinary clothes for themselves. But the problem with buy-now-pay-later services is that they make it harder for us to buy and replace our raw materials," said the manager of a clothing store. "On the other hand, if we refuse to offer these services, our sales will decline. Selling the products and hoping that the money comes back is better than keeping the goods in storage and waiting for people's economic situation to improve." While some U.S. officials initially framed the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran as an effort to liberate Iranians from authoritarian rule, the subsequent sanctions campaign and blockade have been bluntly described as a means of destroying Iranian society by deepening economic deprivation and provoking domestic unrest. "We have the blockade, and we are going to have the toughest sanctions in history," Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent in August, adding: "We are going to collapse this regime." Earlier, Bessent the Senate Banking Committee that Washington had "created a dollar shortage" in Iran, sending its currency into freefall and causing inflation to explode--"and hence we have seen the Iranian people out on the street." Iran's total trade has fallen by an estimated 25-35%, with imports declining faster than exports, while the workforce has dropped by about 450,000 from a year earlier, according to figures provided by the Iranian government. The International Monetary Fund forecasts that the economy will contract by 6.1% in 2026, as inflation drives up business expenses and consumers cut back their own spending, including on food and basic household goods. While the U.S. sanctions are succeeding in causing the impoverishment of Iranians, there is little indication that they are set to trigger an uprising that would deliver victory in the U.S. campaign. Many Iranians who spoke to Drop Site said that their concerns had shifted to merely surviving rather than pursuing political change or confronting a government that has intensified its hold on society amid the war. "I can see with my own eyes that despite having a steady income--or sometimes even earning more money than I did in some previous months--I am getting poorer every day. When I go to a cafe, I have to go through the entire menu and choose the cheapest thing available. Even that cheapest option gets more expensive every day," said a 27-year-old student living in the city of Karaj. "Our lives weren't like this before. We didn't have to count every penny and calculate every expense. Like many others, I have turned to credit-payment services and installment purchases because I cannot afford the cost of living. A pair of sneakers costs the equivalent of one month's salary for a person in Tehran, and the 'buy now, pay later' services even exist for buying food, which shows just how bad people's economic situation has become. In such circumstances, it is obvious that everyone's focus just shifts toward survival." Rising Inequality At the same time that the Trump administration announced its Economic Outcast program against Iran, Iranian government spokesperson Fatima Mohajerani, to a question about poverty rates in Iran in late August, told reporters: "The publication of statistics and figures related to the issue of poverty is subject to security restrictions. Although the government has the figures and statistics on this issue, it cannot make the numbers public." The Iranian government's revenues are also declining day by day under the pressure of sanctions and restrictions on oil exports caused by the blockade. President Donald Trump has repeatedly that the Iranian government is unable to pay the salaries of its employees and security forces, though no such reports have emerged in Iran, and government employees and soldiers continue reporting for work. But a recent announcement that the government plans to consumer energy and gasoline prices inside Iran--both normally subsidized by government spending--shows clear signs that the country is under financial strain. A large share of the expenditure items in Iran's current-year budget have been devoted to the war, even though most of the reconstruction work for war-related damage--estimated at between $20 billion and $40 billion, according to Meysam Zohourian, a conservative member of the Iranian parliament--has not even begun. Iranian President Massoud Pezeshkian and Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, speaking publicly just days apart late last month, both warned that the costs of running the country must somehow be covered and that the welfare and essential needs of the population cannot be postponed indefinitely. "No matter how strong we are militarily, if the people are hungry and we do not have financial circulation, economic growth and domestic production, we will not endure," said Ghalibaf on August 21. Days later, Pezeshkian echoed his sentiments with apparent frustration, stating, "Some say sanctions have no effect at all. I really don't know what to say to those people." Their remarks were directed at domestic hardliners who made demands for major upfront sanctions relief and reparations a condition for negotiations, as well as other segments of the Iranian establishment alleged to be opposed to talks entirely. But the comments have also fueled speculation about the government's concerns over how much economic pressure the population can withstand. At the same time, amid growing deprivation, the display of excesses such as wrapping red meat in bacon, or cafes serving caviar for breakfast has heightened the sense of inequality in Iran. Peter, **It’s now a full-on sprint to Election Day — just about eight weeks away.** The week after Labor Day (a.k.a. now) traditionally marks the beginning of the final, most consequential period of the general election. | | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138960262/645749710/-1006107969?refcode=MW_ATA_EM_FR_Choices_260910_T1_2_b&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODY1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwYWJmZTMyMi01MGFkLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTkzM2IiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=wIYc0Je7xSDpQEx07kIHzgyJQr3qZrSuVXfx4q-45t8=) _In just eight days, early voting begins in Virginia. This is a long email about why I’m asking voters to re-hire me. But if you’re short on time and want to make sure our message reaches all corners of the Commonwealth, you can chip in here:_

[_**_https://secure.actblue.com/donate/mw-email-260907-road_**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138960263/645749711/-1006107969?refcode=MW_ATA_EM_FR_Choices_260910_T1_2_b&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODY1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwYWJmZTMyMi01MGFkLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTkzM2IiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=wIYc0Je7xSDpQEx07kIHzgyJQr3qZrSuVXfx4q-45t8=) Derek,

I think politics is about choices, and there are a series of choices going on right now in Washington that don’t put America first. That’s wrong – and I’m in this fight to offer a better path forward for Virginia:

**1) I think it is time to end this war of choice with Iran.**

Months in, incredible sacrifice from our service members and their families, and higher costs for all of us... And for what?

We have a regime that's even worse. Iran still has enriched uranium. They still have missiles and drones. And the regime has realized the power it has over the global economy with its ability to close the Strait of Hormuz.

We need to bring this war to an end, and we need to go back to an America that is respected by our allies.

**2) We need to bring down costs and end Donald Trump’s trade wars.**

I have voted repeatedly against Trump’s tariffs, and I’ll keep fighting until we bring down costs and end this stupid cycle of on-again-off-again tariffs that are hurting Virginia small businesses, consumers, and farmers.

**3) We’ve got to expand health care coverage.**

After this election, we're going to see another 300,000 Virginians lose their health care coverage – a direct result of President Trump’s Big Ugly Bill.

We need to restore health care access to Virginians who are losing their coverage because of Republican policies, but we have to go further.

It is time to move to universal health care, so that we don’t only focus on who has coverage, but turn our focus on bringing costs down for everyone.

**4) We need to keep human beings in charge of technology, not the other way around.**

I have introduced a comprehensive AI framework to tackle this issue head on: To protect our communities from giant tech companies building data centers with no guardrails whatsoever, to protect our kids from the dangers these chatbots pose to their health and safety, to protect our national security, and to protect our jobs and help transition our economy.

**The challenges facing our country are big. There’s no doubt about that. But Americans have never been afraid of the future, and we can’t start now. That’s why I’m running for reelection and it’s why I’m humbly asking Virginians to re-hire me.**

[_**And ultimately, our campaign will need more resources so we can keep reaching Virginians, especially as early voting begins next week. If you’re able to, please consider a contribution to my campaign before midnight.**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138960265/645749713/-1006107969?refcode=MW_ATA_EM_FR_Choices_260910_T1_2_b&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODY1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwYWJmZTMyMi01MGFkLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTkzM2IiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=wIYc0Je7xSDpQEx07kIHzgyJQr3qZrSuVXfx4q-45t8=)

Thank you for reading until the end. Whether or not you’re able to donate today, I’m deeply grateful for your ongoing support ahead of this critically important election.

We have just 54 days left before polls close – let’s give them everything we have.

Mark Warner **Before you go:**

We are officially in the final, all-out sprint towards Election Day – and we can’t afford to take our foot off the gas.

Victory in November requires sustained engagement from grassroots supporters like you. Right now, this campaign is recruiting volunteers, getting our ads up on the airwaves, and scaling our Get Out the Vote operation.

clean_body: | | | = In just eight days, early voting begins in Virginia. This is a long email about why I’m asking voters to re-hire me. But if you’re short on time and want to make sure our message reaches all corners of the Commonwealth, you can chip in here: = Derek, I think politics is about choices, and there are a series of choices going on right now in Washington that don’t put America first. That’s wrong – and I’m in this fight to offer a better path forward for Virginia: 1) I think it is time to end this war of choice with Iran. Months in, incredible sacrifice from our service members and their families, and higher costs for all of us... And for what? We have a regime that's even worse. Iran still has enriched uranium. They still have missiles and drones. And the regime has realized the power it has over the global economy with its ability to close the Strait of Hormuz. We need to bring this war to an end, and we need to go back to an America that is respected by our allies. 2) We need to bring down costs and end Donald Trump’s trade wars. I have voted repeatedly against Trump’s tariffs, and I’ll keep fighting until we bring down costs and end this stupid cycle of on-again-off-again tariffs that are hurting Virginia small businesses, consumers, and farmers. 3) We’ve got to expand health care coverage. After this election, we're going to see another 300,000 Virginians lose their health care coverage – a direct result of President Trump’s Big Ugly Bill. We need to restore health care access to Virginians who are losing their coverage because of Republican policies, but we have to go further. It is time to move to universal health care, so that we don’t only focus on who has coverage, but turn our focus on bringing costs down for everyone. 4) We need to keep human beings in charge of technology, not the other way around. I have introduced a comprehensive AI framework to tackle this issue head on: To protect our communities from giant tech companies building data centers with no guardrails whatsoever, to protect our kids from the dangers these chatbots pose to their health and safety, to protect our national security, and to protect our jobs and help transition our economy. The challenges facing our country are big. There’s no doubt about that. But Americans have never been afraid of the future, and we can’t start now. That’s why I’m running for reelection and it’s why I’m humbly asking Virginians to re-hire me. = Thank you for reading until the end. Peter,

If you turn on your TV in the Central Valley right now, there's a good chance you'll see an attack ad running against me. They’re hard to miss, and that's the point.

But here's what you may not know: the ads weren't paid for by David Valadao's campaign. They were paid for by the **Congressional Leadership Fund** \-- House Republicans’ outside spending operation. They've now helped Valadao outspend our campaign by nearly $3 million.

They aren't trying to win an argument. They’re trying to make you angry, distracted, or convinced that nothing you do will matter. They’re relying on muddying the waters for working families in our district, so the billionaires and corporate PACs funding these ads can continue to profit by ripping us off at the grocery store, gas tank, and doctor’s office.

But I've never taken a corporate PAC dollar, and I never will. I don't answer to them - and that's exactly why they're spending against me.

**If we win this race, not only does it mean flipping a House seat, it means proving that this kind of campaign — unifying and powered by real people — is the new winning formula everywhere.**

Peter,

What a week! Thanks to our amazing volunteers, we had two successful volunteer relaunches for our District 8 and Westside communities as we kick into gear for the last 8 weeks of the campaign. We want to build on this momentum as we approach Election Day and have plenty of ways for you to get involved. Talking to voters is our #1 priority, and we are aiming to knock over 200,000 doors by the end of the campaign. Scott supporters knocked over 40,000 doors last week, but we need your help to reach our goal. Election Day is just 55 days away, and ballots hit mailboxes in less than a month.

Making San Francisco affordable will be Scott’s number one priority in Congress. Whether it's fighting to build millions of affordable homes nationwide, organizing with fellow Democrats to push for Medicare For All, or taking his groundbreaking paid family leave law national, I know Scott is up to the challenge.

He is the only candidate in this race with a record of actually getting sh!t done on making life more affordable. We don’t need another do-nothing Democrat in Washington.

Let’s keep pushing for Scott! - Josh

body:
Trump wants to erase Black history Doris Miller was a hero, Peter.

During the attack on Pearl Harbor, Miller — a Black sailor serving in a segregated Navy — stepped beyond the limits of his rank to help wounded sailors and defend his ship.

His courage saved lives and earned him a place in American history. **That's why the Navy named the USS Doris Miller in his honor.** Now, President Trump is considering renaming the ship, _**erasing a powerful tribute to a Black American hero.**_

We don't know what the Navy would rename the carrier yet, but according to reports, **there's been talk of naming it after Trump himself.** That's never been done for a sitting president. And replacing Doris Miller's name to do it? **It's hard to see that as anything but an insult to a real American hero.**

That's why Wesley was proud to join his colleagues in sending a letter urging Navy leadership to protect Doris Miller's name and legacy. Now, he's asking you to stand with him. **[Will you become a citizen co-sponsor of the letter and join Wesley in standing up against this attack on Black history?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138960799/645751174/-1533477001?ms=em26_260909_doris_adv_gq_act___TB_ettx&refcode=em26_260909_doris_adv_gq_act___TB_ettx&source=em26_260909_doris_adv_gq_act___TB_ettx&utm_campaign=em26_260909_doris_adv_gq_act___TB_ettx&utm_medium=email&contactdata=GvtPbEBZrjTxzT1EpD8JHC2p9JQHrbUUHPUHT2OYtWskBcHpgcOcEzfuR1QSpppSlCXgdUcCsBbSE4Ep4QIfVTPGSi+Q6FcdmhrOjk+YYo3EClL68/KPL6Jz7T5D+ixDiJREBXlKER7CKikQsrj/LrWmfOoOVE9KjLFLhBNHW4E=&refcode2=0c189aad-51ad-f111-9b33-0022482a933b&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDYzODkiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMGMxODlhYWQtNTFhZC1mMTExLTliMzMtMDAyMjQ4MmE5MzNiIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=Cin_U3AgpAGwHRMhMurxHffNvcOn-RNO6O2riyLvpcI=&emci=49c03336-7fa8-f111-9b33-0022482a933b&emdi=0c189aad-51ad-f111-9b33-0022482a933b&ceid=1020964)** | [ADD YOUR NAME](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138960800/645751175/-1533477001?ms=em26_260909_doris_adv_gq_act___TB_ettx&refcode=em26_260909_doris_adv_gq_act___TB_ettx&source=em26_260909_doris_adv_gq_act___TB_ettx&utm_campaign=em26_260909_doris_adv_gq_act___TB_ettx&utm_medium=email&contactdata=GvtPbEBZrjTxzT1EpD8JHC2p9JQHrbUUHPUHT2OYtWskBcHpgcOcEzfuR1QSpppSlCXgdUcCsBbSE4Ep4QIfVTPGSi+Q6FcdmhrOjk+YYo3EClL68/KPL6Jz7T5D+ixDiJREBXlKER7CKikQsrj/LrWmfOoOVE9KjLFLhBNHW4E=&refcode2=0c189aad-51ad-f111-9b33-0022482a933b&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDYzODkiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMGMxODlhYWQtNTFhZC1mMTExLTliMzMtMDAyMjQ4MmE5MzNiIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=Cin_U3AgpAGwHRMhMurxHffNvcOn-RNO6O2riyLvpcI=&emci=49c03336-7fa8-f111-9b33-0022482a933b&emdi=0c189aad-51ad-f111-9b33-0022482a933b&ceid=1020964)

In the middle of the worst Cyclosporiasis outbreak on record (with cases up 15-fold compared to last year), a beef recall after it was imported from Argentina and sold to Americans without being inspected at all, and near-constant recalls on lettuce, blueberries, eggs, cheese, mangoes, and more – Donald Trump thinks we should eliminate food inspection regulations entirely.

_Less oversight and no food safety checkpoints are exactly the opposite of what we need right now._

The three main agencies responsible for food safety – the FDA, USDA, and CDC – have already undergone massive federal funding cuts thanks to Donald Trump, Elon Musk, and RFK Jr.

→ The FDA has lost 20% of its workforce, the CDC has lost 25%, and the USDA has lost 27%.

→ The national advisory committee that used to advise our federal agencies on how to prevent food contamination has been completely disbanded.

→ The CDC used to have 11 scientists tracking food parasites; now it has only three.

_Our federal agencies meant to protect public health are already operating with a skeleton crew, and now Trump wants to gut what’s left._

As a doctor, I want to be direct with you: food safety regulations are more than just a bunch of red tape and headaches for producers. They’re why you can go to a grocery store and trust that what you put in your body won’t make you sick. They’re why massive Cyclospora outbreaks like the one from this summer are typically rare and preventable.

We’ve already seen the impact of these federal budget cuts on Americans as thousands more people have gotten sick compared to previous years. Eliminating these programs will cost lives, period.

**This is what happens when you put people in charge of our government and public health who don’t believe in science and who don’t listen to the experts.**

clean_body: and we’re already operating on a skeleton crew| | | | = You cannot make up this level of dysfunction if you tried: = In the middle of the worst Cyclosporiasis outbreak on record (with cases up 15-fold compared to last year), a beef recall after it was imported from Argentina and sold to Americans without being inspected at all, and near-constant recalls on lettuce, blueberries, eggs, cheese, mangoes, and more – Donald Trump thinks we should eliminate food inspection regulations entirely. Less oversight and no food safety checkpoints are exactly the opposite of what we need right now. The three main agencies responsible for food safety – the FDA, USDA, and CDC – have already undergone massive federal funding cuts thanks to Donald Trump, Elon Musk, and RFK Jr. → The FDA has lost 20% of its workforce, the CDC has lost 25%, and the USDA has lost 27%. → The national advisory committee that used to advise our federal agencies on how to prevent food contamination has been completely disbanded. → The CDC used to have 11 scientists tracking food parasites; now it has only three. Our federal agencies meant to protect public health are already operating with a skeleton crew, and now Trump wants to gut what’s left. As a doctor, I want to be direct with you: food safety regulations are more than just a bunch of red tape and headaches for producers. They’re why you can go to a grocery store and trust that what you put in your body won’t make you sick. They’re why massive Cyclospora outbreaks like the one from this summer are typically rare and preventable. We’ve already seen the impact of these federal budget cuts on Americans as thousands more people have gotten sick compared to previous years. Eliminating these programs will cost lives, period. Long before there were highways, there were longhorns moving north through open country, driven by Texans of all stripes who worked hard to feed a growing nation.
The families who settled this land passed their brands down as heirlooms through drought years, blizzards, and market busts.
And the story kept getting bigger.
An industry that once belonged exclusively to men has blossomed into one where the women who worked the pens without credit now run ranches of their own all across Texas, more of them every year.
Whole towns in our district grew up around the feed store and the auction barn.
When America sits down to dinner, there is a decent chance a Texas ranch put the meal on the table, and generations of ranch families take immense pride in that.
This administration has repaid them with three betrayals in a row.
This year, violent ICE raids swept through and emptied ranches and farms of the hired hands and seasonal workers they depend on.
Many Texas operations shut down overnight after nearly their entire workforce disappeared.
Then Trump cut special import deals for cheap Argentine beef, betraying the cattle associations that begged him not to.
Now tens of thousands of pounds of that imported beef are being recalled right here in Texas after it entered the country without proper reinspection.

clean_body: Texas cattle country built this state. Washington is selling it out. | | Peter, Our proud Texas ranchers are under attack from their own government, and I intend to put a stop to it. Long before there were highways, there were longhorns moving north through open country, driven by Texans of all stripes who worked hard to feed a growing nation. The families who settled this land passed their brands down as heirlooms through drought years, blizzards, and market busts. And the story kept getting bigger. An industry that once belonged exclusively to men has blossomed into one where the women who worked the pens without credit now run ranches of their own all across Texas, more of them every year. Whole towns in our district grew up around the feed store and the auction barn. When America sits down to dinner, there is a decent chance a Texas ranch put the meal on the table, and generations of ranch families take immense pride in that. This administration has repaid them with three betrayals in a row. This year, violent ICE raids swept through and emptied ranches and farms of the hired hands and seasonal workers they depend on. Many Texas operations shut down overnight after nearly their entire workforce disappeared. Then Trump cut special import deals for cheap Argentine beef, betraying the cattle associations that begged him not to. Now tens of thousands of pounds of that imported beef are being recalled right here in Texas after it entered the country without proper reinspection. The rigged Republican map that redrew our district swept in a huge stretch of cattle ranches and rural farming communities Keith Self has never represented and hasn't bothered to get to know. Our campaign has boots on the ground out there right now, at the kitchen tables and the co-ops, listening. | These families deserve a congressman who understands what they are up against and how this administration is selling them out one deal at a time. Keith Self is not that man, and out in cattle country they are figuring that out fast. The dignity of a good day's pay for a good day's work was bled and sacrificed for in this country. Protecting it is the whole job of a representative, and this extremist crowd in Washington has abandoned it. ### Announcing the PA Forward Party's First Ever Congressional Endorsement!
###

**The Pennsylvania Forward Party has endorsed Forward Independent Candidate Dennis Mahoney****for the U.S. House of Representatives in Pennsylvania Congressional District 3.** Mahoney brings more than a decade of disaster relief and humanitarian response experience to his campaign, along with a record of building partnerships focused on food insecurity, education, and affordability. Mahoney is the founder of AOI Solutions, a firm focused on disaster relief and humanitarian response. His work has included convening businesses, nonprofits, faith communities, and civic leaders to address complex problems in Philadelphia, across the United States, and around the world. In Philadelphia, he has worked with coalitions supporting children and foster families, helped organize neighborhood food markets, and worked with school districts to support students, teachers, and principals.

| **The Race** Mahoney is running as a Forward Independent candidate for the U.S. House of Representatives in Pennsylvania Congressional District 3. This district includes much of Philadelphia, including the West and Southwest, encompassing Germantown, University City, Mount Airy, Fairmount, and Strawberry Mansion. He entered a previously uncontested race against a candidate nominated by only 12% of eligible voters.
---
**The Takeaways**
Mahoney is running as a Forward Independent candidate for the U.S. House in Pennsylvania District 3. His professional background includes more than a decade of disaster relief and humanitarian response work. This race is one of the best opportunities in the country for an independent candidate in a head-to-head race. Your support can make a huge difference.

I love Ohio with all of my heart.

I was born and raised in Mansfield, a blue-collar city. My dad was a doctor (“Doc Brown” to his patients), and my mom was president of our local YWCA and a leader in the Ohio Hunger Task Force. They both taught me everything I know about hard work, service, and standing up for what’s right.

I was also lucky to learn a lot from the Ohioans who formed the backbone of our community: autoworkers at General Motors, steelworkers at Empire Detroit, machinists at Tappan Stove, and electricians at Westinghouse.

But as time went on, Mansfield – and other Ohio cities and towns like it – took a hit.

I watched as big corporations lobbied for tax breaks and bad trade agreements that shipped Ohio jobs overseas. I saw firsthand how families were devastated by decisions made by Washington politicians hundreds of miles away who didn’t care about the harm they were causing.

The sad thing is, not much has changed since then. The system is rigged against working people and in favor of billionaires and corporate interests, and politicians like Jon Husted are hellbent on keeping it that way. That’s why I’m running to defeat him.

**But I can’t do it without your help, especially today, with the Republicans’ national midterm convention taking place and new attacks sure to come my way. Peter,
House Republicans just cancelled the last two weeks of votes in September. Here’s what I’ve got to say about it:
**In a time where we need it most, Republicans have made zero proposals to actually benefit the American people.**
_Zero_ proposals to lower the cost of gas.
_Zero_ proposals to bring down the price of groceries.
_Zero_ proposals to fight back against rising healthcare costs.
_Zero_ proposals to stop the illegal and unconstitutional war in Iran.
Instead, we just vote on stupid sh*t that Congress shouldn’t be doing: cutting taxes for the rich and doling out favors to billionaires and giant corporations, symbolic votes to “condemn socialism,” and cutting funding for healthcare and food assistance programs that working people rely on.
For years, Republicans have acted against the interests of hardworking Americans.
Now they’re sidestepping real responsibility and canceling votes because they know their popularity is falling—and instead of spending time in Congress to make positive changes, they’d rather do damage control in their districts.
So if they want to cancel votes and spend their time lying to the American people, I’m going back to Seattle to talk about all the things progressive Democrats HAVE done not just in opposition to Republicans, but in PROPOSITION for the future that I believe working families deserve.
**And make no mistake, when we all return to Washington D.C., I will continue fighting for hardworking Americans.**
I will _never_ stop fighting for Medicare For All, paid family and medical leave, just immigration reform, raising the minimum wage to a living wage, and more. But I can’t do it without your support.

clean_body: House Republicans just cancelled the last two weeks of votes this month. Peter, House Republicans just cancelled the last two weeks of votes in September. Here’s what I’ve got to say about it: In a time where we need it most, Republicans have made zero proposals to actually benefit the American people. Zero proposals to lower the cost of gas. Zero proposals to bring down the price of groceries. Zero proposals to fight back against rising healthcare costs. Zero proposals to stop the illegal and unconstitutional war in Iran. Instead, we just vote on stupid sht that Congress shouldn’t be doing: cutting taxes for the rich and doling out favors to billionaires and giant corporations, symbolic votes to “condemn socialism,” and cutting funding for healthcare and food assistance programs that working people rely on. For years, Republicans have acted against the interests of hardworking Americans. Now they’re sidestepping real responsibility and canceling votes because they know their popularity is falling—and instead of spending time in Congress to make positive changes, they’d rather do damage control in their districts. So if they want to cancel votes and spend their time lying to the American people, I’m going back to Seattle to talk about all the things progressive Democrats HAVE done not just in opposition to Republicans, but in PROPOSITION for the future that I believe working families deserve. And make no mistake, when we all return to Washington D.C., I will continue fighting for hardworking Americans. I will never stop fighting for Medicare For All, paid family and medical leave, just immigration reform, raising the minimum wage to a living wage, and more. But I can’t do it without your support. In solidarity, Pramila Jayapal | | Email us: info@pramilaforcongress.com

The Democrats and their allies in the media are doing everything in their power to expand that edge in order to flip a Senate seat. They will pour in outside money. They will flood the airwaves. subject: Officially the nominee

body:
# [](https://act.katieporter.com/go/9?t=1&akid=41568%2E3422442%2E8xN9lk)
Peter, Cait Conley here.
I am the Democratic nominee for New York’s 17th Congressional District and will officially face off against Mike Lawler this November.
This is one of only three districts nationwide that split their ticket in 2024 for Kamala Harris and a Republican. There is no path for Democrats to take back the House without winning this seat.
**[If you are ready for the work ahead, I’m asking you to split a donation to my campaign and Truth to Power right now. The general election has begun, it’s critical that we hit the ground running.](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21531?c0=em_ms_ttp_20260910_1_ak.ZSLpcx&refcode=em20260910-41568&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=2&akid=41568%2E3422442%2E8xN9lk)**
[Donate ›››](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21531?c0=em_ms_ttp_20260910_1_ak.ZSLpcx&refcode=em20260910-41568&t=21&akid=41568%2E3422442%2E8xN9lk)
I’m running for Congress not because this was ever part of some big life plan. But because the country I was willing to die for, the one I’ve lost countless friends defending, is becoming something I barely recognize.
We cannot let this happen. Not on our watch.
My opponent, Republican Mike Lawler, has a massive fundraising advantage over us. That means that we are the underdogs heading into the general election. From here on out, we can expect the attacks and mudslinging to only increase.
It’s going to be an uphill battle. But I’ve never shied away from a tough fight.
In the special operations community, we have a saying: “Run to the sound of the guns.”
That’s what I’ve done my entire life. I joined the Army after 9/11. I deployed six times overseas, serving in combat zones like Iraq and Afghanistan, hunting down brutal terrorists to keep America and the world safe.
Part of taking on tough fights means knowing when to ask for help.
And today, I need to ask for your help.
**[Please, make a split $5 donation to my campaign in NY-17 and Truth to Power today. Anything you can give will be put right to work, building an operation to beat Mike Lawler.](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21531?c0=em_ms_ttp_20260910_1_ak.ZSLpcx&refcode=em20260910-41568&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=22&akid=41568%2E3422442%2E8xN9lk)**

Let’s take back the House.
With gratitude and fire,
Cait Conley

Hi friends!

_A NOTE BEFORE TODAY'S HEADLINES_ 💔

_One year ago today, Charlie Kirk was killed. In a personal
reflection, RMV's own Tori Ganahl, a former student he mentored in
Oregon, recalls how his death briefly quieted the noise of division,
sending people back to church, family, and each other, and asks
whether that unity has faded as the news cycle moved on. She shares
that Charlie's influence continues in her own life: she married in
October and is expecting a son due in January, a legacy she says
carries forward his call to build strong families, mentor the next
generation, and show up for others rather than retreat into cynicism.
As she puts it: the fire he lit is still burning, and it's now up to
the rest of us to keep it going. READ THE FULL COMMENTARY HERE.

This is your Mountain Minute for Thursday, September 10, 2026.

– Team RMV

TODAY'S TOP STORIES

XCEL’S LARGE LOAD TARIFF FIGHT: WHO WILL PAY FOR COLORADO’S DATA
CENTERS?
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

BY SHAINA COLE, ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

One of the biggest open questions about who pays for Colorado’s data
center boom is being decided this fall at the Public Utilities
Commission, and the answer testimony that frames the fight is already
filed. By Aug. 19, intervenors had filed a stack of answer testimony
in Proceeding No. 26AL-0137E,

Xcel Energy’s proposed Large Load Tariff. The case has drawn a
crowd. Google is in it. So is Walmart. So is the City and County of
Denver, the City of Boulder, the electric cooperative United Power,
the state’s own energy office, and the commission’s trial staff.

The evidentiary hearing is set for 5 days across late October, Oct.
21, 22, 26, 27 and 28. A second public comment hearing is set for Oct.
20. The hearing wraps 6 days before Colorado’s Nov. 3 general
election, and the commission has not set a date to decide the question
of whether ordinary Xcel customers help pay for data center power.

READ MORE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

ADAMS COUNTY’S ELECTION-WORKER SHORTAGE NEEDS A PLAN, NOT MORE FEAR
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

BY KAREN HOOPES, ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

_With Adams County roughly 200 election workers short, the clerk's
fear-based explanation is getting a pass it hasn't earned._

*
A MANAGEMENT PROBLEM, NOT A MYSTERY: The author argues Clerk Josh
Zygielbaum's claim that fear is keeping workers away needs actual
evidence — how many former workers were contacted, and how many
cited fear versus pay, hours, or a slow hiring process.

*
A PATTERN OF ALARMING RHETORIC: The piece points to the clerk's 2022
talk of body armor and an alarm raised over a powdery ballot substance
later found harmless, arguing repeated worst-case messaging risks
discouraging workers and conditioning voters to expect delays.

*
A CONCRETE FIX, NOT EXCUSES: The author, who is running for Adams
County Clerk and Recorder, proposes a rapid "200 Workers in Seven
Days" recruiting push, competitive pay comparisons, and daily public
staffing updates.

BY C. J. GARBO | COMMENTARY | SEPTEMBER 8

_Douglas County voters will soon be asked to make a consequential
decision about the structure of their county government. A
citizen-initiated ballot measure proposes expanding the Board of
County Commissioners from three members to five, with the expanded
board composed either of five commissioners elected by district or
three elected by district and two elected at large._

__

DENVER ICE WALKOUT TURNS VIOLENT, AND THE JOURNALISTS FILMING IT SAY
THEY WERE ATTACKED
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.

BY SHAINA COLE | LOCAL | SEPTEMBER 8

_The flyer set the time at noon, Friday, September 4, at La
Alma-Lincoln Park. No work. No school. No shopping. ICE out. There was
a DJ. There were food trucks. Kids danced. Then the water bottles
started flying, and by the time the crowd cleared, three people had
gone to the hospital and at least one woman had been beaten until one
eye was swollen nearly shut._
__
__

__

__

THE SENSITIVITY WEAPON: LITTLE MISS MUFFET
[https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.
BY DRAKE HUNTER | COMMENTARY | SEPTEMBER 6

_Last week, we dove into Jesus’ command to “Ask, Seek, and
Knock,” highlighting the vital role of resourcefulness—what I like
to call source management! Remember Poor Little Bo-Peep? Instead of
seeking her lost sheep, she just hoped they would find their way home.
This week, we journey with poor Little Miss Muffet as Jesus guides us
to persistently ask, seek, and knock until we uncover the truths
waiting for us._

name: Mark Kelly
subject: The stakes in NH are high
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Chris Pappas for Senate
body:
Recent polling shows Chris’s opponent ahead of him for the first time in this entire campaign.
Team, it's Mark Kelly.
**I was in New Hampshire with my friend Chris Pappas, and I can tell you firsthand: The energy is electric, but the stakes couldn't be higher.**
As a Navy pilot and astronaut, I learned early on that when a mission plan changes, you don't panic -- you look at the data, adjust your strategy, and execute.
So I'm going to be straight with you about where things stand in New Hampshire: This week marks the official launch of the general election against Chris’s Republican opponent. **And recent polling shows him ahead of Chris for the first time in this entire campaign.**
**[Will you help us flip the Senate by chipping in $5 or whatever you can to Chris’s campaign right now? The path to the majority runs through New Hampshire, and your support matters now more than ever.](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260910_3.HPcg45&refcode=em20260910-3&t=1&akid=8842%2E582294%2Excn7I5)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260910_3.HPcg45&amount=5&refcode=em20260910-3&t=20&akid=8842%2E582294%2Excn7I5)**
The flood of out-of-state corporate money pouring into New Hampshire is having an impact. National Republican groups know there is no path for Democrats to retake the Senate majority without holding this open seat. That’s why they’re spending whatever it takes to boost Chris’s opponent, lock in their Senate majority, and push an extreme agenda.
**We need to turn the tide right now -- and we cannot let them buy this seat.**
Chris Pappas is the kind of leader New Hampshire needs -- pragmatic, grounded, and focused on delivering real results for working families. He’s fighting to lower everyday costs, protect reproductive freedom, and defend our democracy. He doesn't rely on corporate PACs; he relies on folks like you.
Chris has proven he can win tough fights, but winning this race takes all of us stepping up right now.
**[Will you join me today by chipping in $5, $15, or whatever you can afford to help Chris Pappas fight back and take back the Senate?](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260910_3.HPcg45&refcode=em20260910-3&t=21&akid=8842%2E582294%2Excn7I5)**
**[Donate »](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260910_3.HPcg45&refcode=em20260910-3&t=22&akid=8842%2E582294%2Excn7I5)**
We have zero margin for error in this race. Thank you for standing with Chris when it counts most.
Mark Kelly
**New Hampshire is poised to be one of the closest Senate races in the country. Will you chip in today to help Chris stop the Republicans from flipping the Granite State red and expanding their Senate majority?**
**[Donate »](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_cp_footer?refcode=em20260910-3&t=23&refcode2=8842_582294_xcn7I5&akid=8842%2E582294%2Excn7I5)**

| | | Fellow American, I'm walking onto the stage soon at the first-ever Republican Midterm Convention -- right here in Texas. **Before I do, I want to know you're standing with me, Friend.** CNN already sent a host down here trying to pick this convention apart before we've even started. They'd rather talk about anything except what Republicans have actually delivered -- lower taxes, a secured border, real energy production, an economy climbing back from the mess Biden left behind. **That's the choice in this election.** Republican results, or the direction Democrats like James Talarico want to drag this country -- higher taxes, an open border, and law enforcement treated like subject: Let’s hit the ground running
body:
It’s official: I am the Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate here in New Hampshire.
---
Derek, this is an email from the Democratic National Committee about our work to take back control of Congress this November. If you'd prefer to [receive fewer emails](https://ak.democrats.org/signup/receive-less-email/?t=1&akid=9059%2E22930333%2EZFlyww) or [stop receiving our emails](https://ak.democrats.org/cms/unsubscribe/unsubscribe/?t=2&akid=9059%2E22930333%2EZFlyww), you can click [here](https://ak.democrats.org/signup/receive-less-email/?t=3&akid=9059%2E22930333%2EZFlyww). | [](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-pappas-split?amount=20&refcode=em_20260910_9059_fr&refcode2=9059_22930333_ZFlyww&akid=9059%2E22930333%2EZFlyww)
---
Hi Derek, it’s Chris Pappas.
**It’s official: I am the Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate here in New Hampshire.**
I’m so grateful to every Granite Stater who put their trust in me and helped build this campaign together.
Growing up in Manchester and working alongside my family at our restaurant, I learned that you don’t get ahead just by making promises. You have to be accountable. You listen to people, work hard, and deliver.
That’s the same approach I’ve brought to Congress, and it’s why I’m running for the Senate.
I’m running to make New Hampshire more affordable for working families; protect Social Security, Medicare, and Medicaid; safeguard reproductive freedom; and stand up for the small businesses that are the backbone of our communities.
**And now our general election fight against John Sununu officially begins.**
Political experts just changed this race to a Toss-up, Derek. The fact is: New Hampshire is a fiercely independent state, and this election could go either way. The country is watching, and the outcome here in New Hampshire will help determine control of the U.S. Senate and what the next two years look like for millions of families across the country.
[**Derek, we are running a grassroots-powered campaign fueled by people like you. We need all hands on deck in order to keep New Hampshire blue and flip the Senate. Will you step up with $20 or whatever you can spare – split between me and the DNC – to boost our campaign and the Democrats as we enter the general election?**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-pappas-split?refcode=em_20260910_9059_fr&amount=20&refcode2=9059_22930333_ZFlyww&akid=9059%2E22930333%2EZFlyww)
**[CHIP IN TO KEEP NH BLUE >>](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-pappas-split?refcode=em_20260910_9059_fr&refcode2=9059_22930333_ZFlyww&akid=9059%2E22930333%2EZFlyww)**
John Sununu has spent his career putting Washington and corporate special interests ahead of Granite Staters. While he was in Congress, he voted to give tax breaks to Big Pharma and Big Oil, and now he’s profiting off of investments in those same industries.
As we speak, national Republicans and dark-money groups are spending millions to put him back in the Senate because they know he’ll do the bidding of Trump and corporate interests, not look out for the people of New Hampshire.
**This race is a toss-up, so we need to join together right now and stay focused over the next eight weeks.**
[**Will you chip in a $20 contribution split between my campaign and the DNC right now to help us hit the ground running to keep this seat blue and take back the Senate?**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-pappas-split?refcode=em_20260910_9059_fr&amount=20&refcode2=9059_22930333_ZFlyww&akid=9059%2E22930333%2EZFlyww)

* **Kept Trump's illegal war in Iran alive** , voting again and again against ending it — and even after three Republican senators voted to stop it, he was the lone Democrat still fighting to continue it.4
* **Cast the deciding vote for Trump's Republican budget bill** , stripping health care from millions of Americans — including 400,000 Pennsylvanians — and driving ACA premiums up 114%.
* **Became the first Senate Democrat to back Republicans' Laken Riley Act,** stripping due process from immigrants accused of certain crimes.5
* **Responded to ICE's killing of Renée Good in Minnesota by using the moment to demand more deportations** , telling Fox News**:** "Round up all the criminals. Deport them. They shouldn't have ever been here, and they definitely have to go."
* **Defended the ongoing genocide in Gaza** for over three years, refusing to support even a two-state solution — and even asking Israel to pardon Netanyahu on corruption charges.6

**Whatever party he claims, Fetterman's record tells the real story — nominee by nominee, vote by vote, he's given the Republican Party exactly what it needed.** His support has helped Republicans rip away health care, gut food assistance for seniors and veterans, and pour billions into ICE, all while bankrolling another round of tax breaks for billionaires. **Last night, Peter, John Fetterman thanked them for it.** Pennsylvania deserves a senator who fights for working people, not one auditioning for Republican approval. clean_body: | | | Peter, Last night, Pennsylvania Senator John Fetterman appeared in a video at the Republican Party's convention — praising Donald Trump and Republican Senator Dave McCormick for "helping" America's steel industry. 1 Let that sink in. A sitting Democratic senator, thanking Republicans, at their own convention. Meanwhile, here's who he's thanking: the party that's slashing taxes for the rich and ballooning the military budget, while gutting Medicaid, veterans' benefits, SNAP, and environmental protections to pay for it. The party coming after pensions, coming after Social Security, coming after the right to vote. The party supercharging ICE, re-opening private detention camps, and shredding due process for immigrants. That'swho Fetterman was thanking last night. We know 2028 feels far away. We know the midterms are the fight in front of us right now. But strong challengers don't appear overnight — they take years to recruit, build support, and raise the resources to win. So let's start. Right now. Here's the fuller picture, Peter — because last night’s convention video isn't a one-off. It's a pattern, and the pattern is betrayal. Since taking office in 2024, Fetterman has: Confirmed more Trump nominees than any other Senate Democrat — including standing alone as the only Democrat to support Pam Bondi, an election denier, for Attorney General.2 Voted against his own party more than any other senator in the Senate — Democrat or Republican.3 Kept Trump's illegal war in Iran alive , voting again and again against ending it — and even after three Republican senators voted to stop it, he was the lone Democrat still fighting to continue it.4 Cast the deciding vote for Trump's Republican budget bill , stripping health care from millions of Americans — including 400,000 Pennsylvanians — and driving ACA premiums up 114%. Became the first Senate Democrat to back Republicans' Laken Riley Act, stripping due process from immigrants accused of certain crimes.5 Responded to ICE's killing of Renée Good in Minnesota by using the moment to demand more deportations , telling Fox News: "Round up all the criminals. Deport them. They shouldn't have ever been here, and they definitely have to go." Defended the ongoing genocide in Gaza for over three years, refusing to support even a two-state solution — and even asking Israel to pardon Netanyahu on corruption charges.6 Whatever party he claims, Fetterman's record tells the real story — nominee by nominee, vote by vote, he's given the Republican Party exactly what it needed. His support has helped Republicans rip away health care, gut food assistance for seniors and veterans, and pour billions into ICE, all while bankrolling another round of tax breaks for billionaires. Last night, Peter, John Fetterman thanked them for it. Pennsylvania deserves a senator who fights for working people, not one auditioning for Republican approval. We've already launched We'll be hosting events across the state in the coming months to find and train the people who'll actually stand up for working Pennsylvanians. But we can't do it without you. clean_body: Let’s clear the air.| | | | | Peter , I flew above battlefields, passing burning husks of armored vehicles, and in Iraq I poured enough sand out of my boots to fill a desert. You would think that after flying an Apache helicopter through an active war zone, and having God knows how many stray bullets shot my direction, there’s not a thing on this planet that could scare me. I thought so too, until my team reminded me about what’s coming in the next few days. Let me explain. This campaign’s bigger than anything I’ve done in Iraq. Rather than covering for a team on the ground, the fate of more than 10 million people will be decided in November. Campaigning isn’t easy, and sometimes it feels like the weight of the world is on my shoulders. Just before I typed this email, my team reminded me about our upcoming End-of-Quarter fundraising deadline. This isn’t just an arbitrary deadline; this is one of our last BIG goals before the November election. I’m not going to ask you to dig deep into your pockets. All I’m asking is a $1 or more donation, which will go right into my campaign's war chest and help me and President Trump take down the Democrat machine come November. As a combat veteran and a patriot - I give you my word that every dollar matters, and I’m eternally thankful for ANY gift you can make. Time is running out. Thank you for listening, and I hope I can count on your help. | | — John James Republican Nominee for Governor | | Paid for by John James for MI | | 35744 Van Dyke Avenue, Sterling Heights, MI 48312 The use of John James' military images, uniforms, or personnel does not imply endorsement by the Department of War or any branch of the U.S. military. |

# How Washington State Democrats Keep Winning
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/cXjGrQbttxZ?e=d6c5c7d7ec&c2id=d01ae369e8fbc8d507a43d27c2d1769e)
| | In the 2024 general election, every state had major shifts towards Republicans – but not Washington. For five election cycles in a row, Washington State Democrats have increased or maintained their majorities in the state legislature, and have acheived an 8-2 Democratic majority in their U.S. House of Representatives delegation.
So how do Washington State Democrats keep winning?__ To find out, we asked one of the best organizers around - **DNC Vice Chair and Washington State Democratic Party Chair Shasti Conrad.**
Shasti has made history time and time again as the first woman of color and youngest ever Chair of Washington State Democrats as well as the first ever woman of South Asian descent to chair any state party in America. Under her leadership, Washington State Democrats has continued to grow and thrive, but she’s not done making history.
If you want to know the secrets behind Washington State Democrats’ success and how she plans to win big this November, we encourage you to read [her story](https://us.list-manage.com/62V1Hb63LUL?e=d6c5c7d7ec&c2id=d01ae369e8fbc8d507a43d27c2d1769e) below.

We can flip this seat, but only if we hit every single fundraising target – like the one we set for today.

Peter, we’ll start with the bad news.
Frankly, the odds are stacked against us: President Trump has never lost a race in North Carolina, and NC hasn’t sent a Democrat to the U.S. Senate since 2008 – _almost two decades ago._
However, the tides are turning: **Roy Cooper is undefeated 6-0 in statewide elections, and with him as our nominee, experts say North Carolina is the best pickup opportunity Democrats have on the map this cycle.**
_The only problem?_ Our progress has the GOP panicking.
Stephen Miller, JD Vance and President Trump himself have all gone out of their way to attack Roy personally.
Far-right super PACs are spending nearly $100 million so far to erase his razor-thin lead – and with a recent poll showing the race has slimmed down to a statistical tie, we know it’s working.
So with less than eight weeks left to win this race, we need your help to fight back immediately.
[**_We can flip this seat, but only if we hit every single fundraising target from here on out. A donation of $5 from you before midnight would go a long way toward closing the gap to our daily goal, so please, Peter, will you chip in that much (or _anything_) right away?_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1306&amount=5&t=8&akid=3373%2E124072%2EIwrk1t)
