She introduced herself. Told the woman she was volunteering to protect preborn babies. Asked politely if she could count on her vote.

The woman said "no, thank you." Grace said have a good day and turned to leave.

**That 's when someone screamed from inside the house. A second woman ran out the door - she chased Grace down the driveway, shoved her, and hit her in the head with both fists.**

As Grace tried to run away and reached the end of the driveway, the woman threw a dinner roll that hit her in the face - **and kept following her down the street, screaming that she hoped Grace would be run over by a car.**

Grace filed a police report. The woman was arrested and charged.

My name is Kristan Hawkins, and I'm the President of Students for Life Action. You can think of us as the grassroots arm of the Pro-Life Movement.

Friend, this is just one story from one of Students for Life Action's door-to-door canvassers during the last midterm election.

I've told every one of our canvassers to prepare for anything over the next two months.

I wish I could tell you Grace's story was a one-off. It isn't. Doors get slammed. Voices get raised. Sometimes it gets violent.

And yet our canvassers keep walking up the next driveway because they know if the Abortion Lobby seizes power in November, it will be a death sentence to millions more innocent preborn babies.

**_[Friend, will you please prayerfully consider sending a Care Package to one of our door-to-door canvassers heading into the field this fall](http://links.freedomfirstalert.com/u/click?_t=9ca143e971904d26a973d002cb0ae7f7&_m=dee1252727324b588d5970dcaf955e25&_e=d2IFf4hYUP6VvRc7DO9M8w8zdPz-85MmYZi0daefwRshqzLQ_tazxSeWwT6bpbXznJwAwuHpuv8hm7JPGPy3Ix8jMvOuFTUDuiUjYmQqPUQUSSS8hz2fugOZd50Jt-NCoxfYAlJ4aZgmAcnxjCT9lGLU-1VpHXN8fv-cA2-6XCiRRyhS9-cgHP1JKfTFaIOQwAwPPiaVLl1orVhDoFGpi3ey6QPnNQnUJIYysFm5KfNMOSJfhbvQ4muiTzpqAH-XNs2nX6OtCDFUCCmJPZpbm5QaoGrgucHOCzks-pGQppHcT8aVfTito3SGa9rcnF7y23Dp0YK5e8YHuOPYMEN5fMOzIXOCoUIpCiCPnRyYKbz3LeD6q6dLRyJmwCVETBZmKkvtGZQm2QeHU91qUBz3wJxkCS00WnPB-5PcdgcYH2BVeYFonOOKjxBk2nRD3Na9kg4zTf47f7TrVwCbewWdgDWkYGwLTMflLmN1umvc9ZTdrV2lMHS8RsKEMDGNnkmSv3X3oreYxnWpHjHl0ID3zCCB4E_mj2QXW4aoogMQHIaKUW8u2ZV80lPzS7Eijv5iail9cZuqGbMfZmxjibMX9JRSkHiyiFJTAoHZTDpLsamUVkrggZO45s7ScR6AoqAs6XooYVpUwcwLK0GUQjBzBA%3D%3D)_**?

These young women and men will be walking for hours in scorching heat. Knowing pro-lifers like you have their backs will help keep them going.

Of course, I could tell our door-knockers to go home.

I could focus on running expensive TV ads instead.

But studies show that face-to-face conversations move voters more than any TV ad, mailer, or text ever could - and the effect doesn't disappear after one election.

**Voters who talk to one of our students in person are more likely to show up and vote pro-life again in the _next_ election cycle, too.**

_And, it only costs us about $3 for every door we knock._

Not only that, but we'll be deploying teams of pro-life activists to blanket church parking lots with flyers exposing the records of pro-abortion politicians in key districts every Sunday in September and October.

This is the on-the-ground grassroots campaigning that's needed to turn out every pro-life voter.

Last cycle, this approach worked.

***** In Oklahoma,** our student canvassers knocked 633 doors, made 26,931 phone calls, and sent 26,078 texts exposing two pro-abortion senators who killed our Chemical Abortion Pill Trafficking Bill - and voters threw them out.

***** In South Carolina,** we knocked 2,572 doors and made 51,371 calls exposing three pro-abortion Republican senators who protected the _Life at Conception Act 's_ enemies - and they lost too.

***** In North Carolina,** 1,052 doors and 52,554 texts helped four pro-life candidates win their primaries outright.

That's just a small sample of what our door-to-door canvassing team has done over the years. The Abortion Lobby would love nothing more than for our students to stay home this fall.

Right now, we're already deployed and expanding over the next two months, where this election gets decided door by door. Our target map for the 2026 Midterms is the most ambitious we've run:

**> >> Idaho and Missouri** - ballot referendum battles where the Abortion Lobby is trying to buy a win at the ballot box.

**> >> Georgia, Iowa, Michigan, North Carolina, Ohio, Texas** - U.S. Senate races that could decide who controls the chamber.

**> >> Georgia, Iowa, Michigan, Ohio, North Carolina, Pennsylvania** - Gubernatorial and state legislative races that will shape abortion law for years.

**> >> California's 13th, Iowa's 3rd, Michigan's 10th, Pennsylvania's 10th, North Carolina's 1st, Ohio's 9th, and Texas's 34th** - U.S. House battlegrounds where a few thousand doors could flip a seat and determine control of Congress.

We'll be active in at least ten states in races up and down the ballots. And every single one of them needs boots on the ground before Tuesday, November 3rd.

Friend, the Abortion Lobby has the money, the media, and the institutions. What they don't have is thousands of young pro-lifers willing to knock on a stranger's door, get yelled at, sometimes get hit with worse than words - and go knock on the next door anyway.

Kristan Hawkins

She introduced herself. Told the woman she was volunteering to protect preborn babies. Asked politely if she could count on her vote.

The woman said "no, thank you." Grace said have a good day and turned to leave.

**That 's when someone screamed from inside the house. A second woman ran out the door - she chased Grace down the driveway, shoved her, and hit her in the head with both fists.**

As Grace tried to run away and reached the end of the driveway, the woman threw a dinner roll that hit her in the face - **and kept following her down the street, screaming that she hoped Grace would be run over by a car.**

Grace filed a police report. The woman was arrested and charged.

My name is Kristan Hawkins, and I'm the President of Students for Life Action. You can think of us as the grassroots arm of the Pro-Life Movement.

Peter, this is just one story from one of Students for Life Action's door-to-door canvassers during the last midterm election.

I've told every one of our canvassers to prepare for anything over the next two months.

I wish I could tell you Grace's story was a one-off. It isn't. Doors get slammed. Voices get raised. Sometimes it gets violent.

And yet our canvassers keep walking up the next driveway because they know if the Abortion Lobby seizes power in November, it will be a death sentence to millions more innocent preborn babies.

**_[Peter, will you please prayerfully consider sending a Care Package to one of our door-to-door canvassers heading into the field this fall](http://links.bestamericanow.com/u/click?_t=f6e78b69acbb4291bd75bc93fae35a62&_m=817540f8f56a43bfb3101ff64420a7d9&_e=DNw9PUBJG0UDAr2jyTdExwMI0zNWIqLHNg6e8lD49oLvxcXDwYsybUsIuCHaUKB5GZaUoNO4niaanC9iJxy0Ep69YlS0hHMUDA8YS8tE3Up4EM8XdQE9wWoasZ8ZiJ7qUVlO7mYB0L4v21tyLf96ruZ9mpHK09OKGOeeL0tMmfwgf1sTmg4cz7lwbuDOt7YVgIKdk1kdwOHk1r4_FriBtUvHbv-Sd3geH8-wqjj1SOqlhW0Jp5yxy-AKFHdj_MeatFxp-JzzJ-rCaMzsv2Mb_6WvfEnTiUC0Dbjbj1x02anwS8ZxOshRhszlqArrcqVMvoUo77IR4IXwZkOjhhwMh6OX5YpyD9Rd8eggqsTz1rFUT18Y3lmYtamP47JdYtEpR803g7Y9xsz7UtkQgTKqBW50FwZF9fnGbtmnibivk02EqJdUpipbvA1ltwqE2GJSO8YeMFaC3dKSp3Mlul66DgFeSoHD63077rAbt22sfYfQ6JPcyLgvpMrRrBEGcjq74HRbaHhjOXN2YNiKxMYSG2-e7YsfAfLfdtlecZxZxlA5qv2l0pXf6Q6Izs2W037tikigKi6gsaiP7BYXgu3z_s9lDPjQJaCKDjdeTr-Zb26uWXsJqa1gL-FXuZ_r7G0tGsSjJ70CcXaDFwTv1F6JNQ%3D%3D)_**?

_And, it only costs us about $3 for every door we knock._

Not only that, but we'll be deploying teams of pro-life activists to blanket church parking lots with flyers exposing the records of pro-abortion politicians in key districts every Sunday in September and October.

clean_body: Dear Peter, " I rang the doorbell, and a lady answered." That's how Grace's story starts. She introduced herself. Told the woman she was volunteering to protect preborn babies. Asked politely if she could count on her vote. The woman said "no, thank you." Grace said have a good day and turned to leave. That 's when someone screamed from inside the house. A second woman ran out the door - she chased Grace down the driveway, shoved her, and hit her in the head with both fists. As Grace tried to run away and reached the end of the driveway, the woman threw a dinner roll that hit her in the face - and kept following her down the street, screaming that she hoped Grace would be run over by a car. Grace filed a police report. The woman was arrested and charged. My name is Kristan Hawkins, and I'm the President of Students for Life Action. You can think of us as the grassroots arm of the Pro-Life Movement. Peter, this is just one story from one of Students for Life Action's door-to-door canvassers during the last midterm election. I've told every one of our canvassers to prepare for anything over the next two months. I wish I could tell you Grace's story was a one-off. It isn't. Doors get slammed. Voices get raised. Sometimes it gets violent. And yet our canvassers keep walking up the next driveway because they know if the Abortion Lobby seizes power in November, it will be a death sentence to millions more innocent preborn babies. ? These young women and men will be walking for hours in scorching heat. Knowing pro-lifers like you have their backs will help keep them going. Of course, I could tell our door-knockers to go home. I could focus on running expensive TV ads instead. But studies show that face-to-face conversations move voters more than any TV ad, mailer, or text ever could - and the effect doesn't disappear after one election. Voters who talk to one of our students in person are more likely to show up and vote pro-life again in the next election cycle, too. And, it only costs us about $3 for every door we knock. Not only that, but we'll be deploying teams of pro-life activists to blanket church parking lots with flyers exposing the records of pro-abortion politicians in key districts every Sunday in September and October. This is the on-the-ground grassroots campaigning that's needed to turn out every pro-life voter. Last cycle, this approach worked. *** In Oklahoma, our student canvassers knocked 633 doors, made 26,931 phone calls, and sent 26,078 texts exposing two pro-abortion senators who killed our Chemical Abortion Pill Trafficking Bill - and voters threw them out. *** In South Carolina, we knocked 2,572 doors and made 51,371 calls exposing three pro-abortion Republican senators who protected the Life at Conception Act 's enemies - and they lost too. *** In North Carolina, 1,052 doors and 52,554 texts helped four pro-life candidates win their primaries outright. That's just a small sample of what our door-to-door canvassing team has done over the years. The Abortion Lobby would love nothing more than for our students to stay home this fall. Right now, we're already deployed and expanding over the next two months, where this election gets decided door by door. We'll be active in at least ten states in races up and down the ballots. And every single one of them needs boots on the ground before Tuesday, November 3rd. Peter, the Abortion Lobby has the money, the media, and the institutions. What they don't have is thousands of young pro-lifers willing to knock on a stranger's door, get yelled at, sometimes get hit with worse than words - and go knock on the next door anyway. ## I. The Institutional Failure: The Crucible of State Care
At the start of their tenure inside a state mental hospital, a newly hired therapist is mandated to go through exhaustive training courses and instructional videos preaching that dignity and respect are paramount qualities that must be cultivated. Inspired by a deep reverence for the work, the dedicated staff, and the residents--who are not there by choice, but forced into state care under the Baker Act--the therapist approaches the ward with a firm belief that a real difference can be made. In the classroom, the therapist throws away the "teacher's desk," opting for a roundtable, rectangular in shape, where everyone sits as equals to talk, learn, and serve one another. But the institutional reality quickly shatters the illusion. Beneath the mandated corporate training lies a nightmare of systemic maltreatment: basic necessities like toilet paper are denied, food is withheld, rats literally fall through the ceilings, and residents are subjected to severe over-medication and brutal beatings. Even religious dignity is weaponized, as Jewish individuals are enticed with non-kosher foods or denied kosher meals entirely.
When the horrified therapist begins to confide in colleagues, they are met with a chilling wall of indifference, leading to the devastating realization that all the supervisors and managers know exactly what is happening and actively permit it. Seeking justice outside the hospital walls, the individual turns to the regulatory machinery itself--the state's Department of Children and Families--only to be bombarded with endless paper warfare. In an act of systemic collusion, the whistleblower's recorded statements are handed directly back to the very co-workers they accused, forcing the insider to endlessly answer for, and defend, their own accusations against their attackers. Escalating the fight to the state Inspector General and Senators yields nothing but referrals back to the department's own internal investigators. Letters and calls to the federal Department of Justice, the Department of Health and Human Services, and the Agency for Health Care Administration generate thousands of pages of documentation, unceasing tears, and immediate, terrifying professional retaliation. Terrified but refusing to be silenced, the isolated whistleblower has only one desperate recourse: to breach the fortress by bringing the truth to non-profit agencies like Disability Rights Florida and to the free press. By serving as a vital source to investigative journalist Leonora LaPeter at the Tampa Bay Times, the wall of secrecy was finally shattered in great part, culminating in the historic, Pulitzer Prize-winning series, _Insane. Invisible. In Danger._

## II. The Conceptual Framework: Beyond the Fourth Branch
This harrowing trajectory is not an isolated instance of institutional failure, nor is it merely a dark chapter in state history. It is the real-world, visceral manifestation of a far more formidable structure that dominates modern governance: the Iron Triangle. In standard civics textbooks, students are taught that American governance is defined by three distinct, constitutional branches: the Legislative, the Executive, and the Judicial. In modern political discourse, commentators often point to a "Fourth Branch of Government"--the sprawling, unelected administrative state--as the source of systemic dysfunction. However, framing this institutional machine merely as a "branch" grants it a veneer of constitutional legitimacy it does not deserve. To understand the true, lived reality of modern power, one must look past textbook labels and confront the Iron Triangle. Reimagined for the modern era, this machine is an impenetrable, self-sustaining stronghold formed by the collision of three interlocking vertices: the Bureaucracy, the Establishment, and Special Interests. It is an overwhelming fortress where each vertex fortifies the other, creating a closed loop that extracts from the public and thrives on the erosion of human liberty.
## III. The Bureaucracy: The Extractive Enforcer
To fully understand how this machine sustained the horrors at the state hospital, one must isolate its first vertex: the unchecked Bureaucracy. This Bureaucracy represents the formal, official machinery of government. It is comprised of sprawling regulatory agencies, unelected administrators, and a permanent civil service that operates far outside the ballot box. While it justifies its existence through promises of safety, order, and expertise, its practical output is the manufacturing of a staggering web of administrative rules and endless paper trails. These rules are not merely bureaucratic red tape; they are instruments of extraction. When the Bureaucracy expands its regulatory reach, it extracts directly from the People. The hidden cost of this unchecked rule-making is paid in the most precious currencies a free society possesses: lost liberty, lost property, and the systematic erosion of the consent of the governed.
## IV. The Establishment: The Protective Gatekeeper
The Bureaucracy, however, could not sustain its extractive power without the protective shield of the second vertex: the Establishment. Unlike the formal structure of government agencies, the Establishment is an informal, deeply entrenched network of power. It spans across political parties, Wall Street executives, legacy media empires, and elite cultural institutions. Bound together by shared economic interests and a fierce commitment to the status quo, the Establishment acts as the supreme gatekeeper of public life. Its primary role in the triangle is to maintain and defend the very governmental system that allows the Bureaucracy to flourish. By using the media to shape acceptable public narratives, bury inconvenient truths, and box out populist, anti-establishment outsiders, this elite class ensures that the underlying machinery of the state remains untouched, protecting the loop from internal exposure and external disruption.

In the context of state-run institutions, this capture is where the abstract becomes visceral. When low-bid food contractors and pharmaceutical interests prioritize profit margins over patient dignity, "care" is redefined as "warehousing." The withheld meals and the systemic over-medication are not mere managerial failures; they are the logical results of a system that views human beings as overhead costs to be minimized.
## V. The Special Interests: The Captive Engine
Yet, even an entrenched Establishment requires an economic engine to fuel its dominance, and this engine is found in the third vertex: Special Interests. Special Interest groups--the heavily funded corporate lobbies, trade associations, and financial conglomerates--operate as the financial lifeblood of the machine. They do not seek to govern openly; instead, they operate behind closed doors, using immense capital, campaign contributions, and insider lobbying to influence and direct the raw power of the Establishment. This relationship represents a profound semantic shift in how we view political influence. Over time, these elite Special Interests have successfully captured the Establishment, transforming it into a vehicle that protects monopolies, secures targeted subsidies, and guarantees favorable legislation. In the context of state-run institutions, these interests ensure that budgets are slashed and oversight is sanitized, transforming places of healing into warehouses of profitable neglect.
## VI. The Ironclad Alliance: The Closed Loop of Power
When these three forces align, they form an ironclad alliance that is greater than the sum of its parts. This is not a formal cabal meeting at an annual summit, nor a roundtable of representatives coordinating a plot. The reality is far more banal and far more dangerous; it is a decentralized alignment that occurs piecemeal, through a handshake here or a directive there, driven by a shared set of incentives. Special Interests direct the power of the Establishment; the Establishment protects the system that empowers the Bureaucracy; and the Bureaucracy enforces the rules that protect Special Interests from disruption, while extracting wealth, dignity, and freedom from the populace. It is a closed loop of mutual benefit, completely insulated from the democratic will of the people.
## VII. The Eyewitness Verdict: The Cost of Autonomy
Ultimately, choosing to call this machine the Iron Triangle is not a matter of mere semantics--it is an acknowledgment of a harsh, unyielding reality. Anyone who has ever attempted to challenge a regulatory ruling, disrupt an entrenched industry, or shine a light on internal systemic rot has run headfirst into the overwhelming, impenetrable power of this structure. It does not bend, it does not compromise, and it does not reform itself. The sheer strength of this modern Iron Triangle is so vast, and its capacity to quietly dismantle freedom is so complete, that regular politics is no longer enough to contain it. This is not an abstract exercise in political theory, nor is it a detached academic observation. I know the unyielding weight of this fortress because I am the therapist who lived this nightmare from 2013 to 2016. While the calendar has turned, the machinery of the Iron Triangle has not. I witnessed these horrors a decade ago, yet the structural loops of the Bureaucracy, the Establishment, and Special Interests remain as intact and impenetrable today as they were then. The faces in the offices may change, but the machine is permanent. I have stood at its center, felt its crushing pressure, and watched each piece support the other to protect itself. I know its power firsthand--and I know that only permanent, unyielding vigilance can ever stand against it.

**Strike the root. Secure the table.**

The Institutional Failure: The Crucible of State Care At the start of their tenure inside a state mental hospital, a newly hired therapist is mandated to go through exhaustive training courses and instructional videos preaching that dignity and respect are paramount qualities that must be cultivated. Inspired by a deep reverence for the work, the dedicated staff, and the residents--who are not there by choice, but forced into state care under the Baker Act--the therapist approaches the ward with a firm belief that a real difference can be made. In the classroom, the therapist throws away the "teacher's desk," opting for a roundtable, rectangular in shape, where everyone sits as equals to talk, learn, and serve one another. But the institutional reality quickly shatters the illusion. Beneath the mandated corporate training lies a nightmare of systemic maltreatment: basic necessities like toilet paper are denied, food is withheld, rats literally fall through the ceilings, and residents are subjected to severe over-medication and brutal beatings. Even religious dignity is weaponized, as Jewish individuals are enticed with non-kosher foods or denied kosher meals entirely. When the horrified therapist begins to confide in colleagues, they are met with a chilling wall of indifference, leading to the devastating realization that all the supervisors and managers know exactly what is happening and actively permit it. Seeking justice outside the hospital walls, the individual turns to the regulatory machinery itself--the state's Department of Children and Families--only to be bombarded with endless paper warfare. In an act of systemic collusion, the whistleblower's recorded statements are handed directly back to the very co-workers they accused, forcing the insider to endlessly answer for, and defend, their own accusations against their attackers. Escalating the fight to the state Inspector General and Senators yields nothing but referrals back to the department's own internal investigators. Letters and calls to the federal Department of Justice, the Department of Health and Human Services, and the Agency for Health Care Administration generate thousands of pages of documentation, unceasing tears, and immediate, terrifying professional retaliation. Terrified but refusing to be silenced, the isolated whistleblower has only one desperate recourse: to breach the fortress by bringing the truth to non-profit agencies like Disability Rights Florida and to the free press. Taking back state-level power in Iowa.
#
Hi there,
For the first time since 2006, Iowa’s governor’s seat is open, giving Democrats the best opportunity in years to break almost a decade of unchecked Republican rule.
With Iowa's local economy reeling from federal tariffs and years of extreme policies, Democratic State Auditor **Rob Sand** is leading in the polls to become Iowa’s next Governor.
**Flipping the Governor's mansion would be a game-changer, but protecting the power of a Democratic governor’s veto requires blocking Republican supermajorities in the State Senate and State House.**
Last year, Iowa Democrats flipped two State Senate seats in special elections to break the Republican supermajority in the upper chamber, and we need to make sure it stays that way.
This year, we have an equally big opportunity in the State House, where Republicans hold 67 of 100 seats—meaning flipping just one single seat will break the GOP supermajority in this chamber, too.
[](https://act.swingleft.org/go/27?c0=sl-states-ia-2026.pSaoxF&refcode=em20260910-2736&t=1&akid=2736%2E1562180%2ERrtrlf)
Denying Republicans a veto-proof supermajority ensures that when Rob Sand takes office, his veto power will actually hold. It guarantees Democrats can block legislation that doesn’t serve Iowans and rebuild after years of one-party control.
There’s a real and clear path to victory, but with only 54 days left until Election Day, we can’t afford to leave key state races underfunded in these final weeks.

---
Peter, When Mike Lawler announced he would speak at Trump’s midterm convention in Dallas, a lot of people were probably wondering: _“Doesn’t he represent a Clinton-Biden-Harris district? body:
Me! Peter,

Look, I know you're probably no stranger to political fundraising emails. And if you're getting this email, chances are you're pretty familiar with mine, too.

You've probably seen "Kim Schrier (personal)" pop up in your inbox before—just like it did today. And I wouldn't blame you if, at some point, you thought to yourself: _**Come on. She didn't actually write this.**_

But I have some news for you: **I did!**

When you get an email addressed directly from me, I really did sit down and write it. I have a wonderful team who helps me edit, refine, and make sure everything is ready before we hit send, but I am behind every single "Kim-signed" email that goes out from this campaign.

And when it says "Kim Schrier (personal)," the words started with me. I know that's not how every political campaign operates. But it has always mattered to me that you actually hear from me—especially when I'm asking you to contribute your hard-earned money. **You deserve to know who is asking, you deserve to know why, and you deserve more than some generic fundraising pitch with my name slapped on the bottom.**

So, since I really am the one writing to you, I'll tell you directly why I'm asking today. We have a tough election ahead of us. Republicans have targeted this district cycle after cycle, and I need to be ready for them to spend whatever it takes to try and hold onto their slim majority. I don't take a single election—or a single vote—for granted. I'm running a serious campaign, even in a year when others may become complacent.

We know this is a 48-48 district, with a very small sliver that's truly "independent." I need to win over every Democrat, and at least half of those independents to win again, and that's a tall order. We all know just how partisan this country has become. That's why I'm asking personally:

**Will you chip in $10, or whatever feels right to you today, to help me defend this seat and keep me, the first and only pediatrician in the House, standing up to RFK Jr. and Donald Trump, and fighting for the people of WA-08 in Congress? >> [**https://secure.actblue.com/donate/schrier-q3-email-26 &refcode2=dpwillis67@gmail.com**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138966005/645767332/-2042773732?refcode=em26_260909_write_fndd_gq_act___KSP_ettx&utm_campaign=em26_260909_write_fndd_gq_act___KSP_ettx&utm_medium=email&refcode2=3d8a5c47-5dad-f111-9b33-0022482a933b&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS85MTExMyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzZDhhNWM0Ny01ZGFkLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTkzM2IiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=XnhuMmuLX7PUCs_4kDM84tdE2mTW37IBwD2dyF8DDss=)**

Hi, we don’t have much time left.
Early voting here in Ohio starts in just 26 days. That’s 26 days to fight back against the GOP’s baseless attacks before Ohioans start voting in person. That’s 26 days to reach millions of voters with our message and get them to the polls.
Then, before you know it, we’ll be watching the results come in on election night.
We’ve done what nobody thought possible by putting Ohio and the Senate in play this year – but if you’re looking at the neck-and-neck polls and rosy expert predictions and thinking we’ve got this in the bag, **you’re wrong.**

Hey folks,
Andrew and Tristan Tate just got hit with two major developments: the UK has formally submitted its extradition request, and there's a renewed push in Congress to investigate Barron Trump's reported ties to the brothers.
And after losing their bail fight, the Tates and their allies are melting down publicly. There's a lot happening here--and a lot of questions that still need answers.
* [**00:01:14**] The UK formally files its extradition request, and we break down the serious charges Andrew and Tristan Tate are accused of facing.
* [**00:03:01**] The focus shifts to Barron Trump as Rep. Yassamin Ansari renews calls to investigate his reported relationship with the Tate brothers.
* [**00:06:13**] Why the Tates appear to be turning on Trump-world figures--and what they're threatening to reveal if nobody comes to their rescue.
* [**00:09:05**] Joe McBride invokes Jesus after the Tates lose their bail fight, leading to a deeply personal conversation about faith, accountability, and hypocrisy.
* [**00:12:01**] We unpack what happens next in the extradition process, why the brothers remain behind bars, and why their own public rhetoric could hurt their case.

This episode is about more than Andrew and Tristan Tate. It's about power, proximity, accountability, and whether political connections can--or should--shield anyone from scrutiny. We dig into the extradition fight, the unanswered questions surrounding Trump-world connections, and the public campaign to portray the Tates as victims. Peter — For nearly 30 years, LCV Victory Fund's Dirty Dozen https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/L6b_sLX~AmF- has named the candidates for federal office whose records most consistently side
against the environment. This year, the list carries an added, urgent
throughline: the skyrocketing energy costs that will be a major deciding factor
for a crucial set of swing voters. Every candidate on this year's Dirty Dozen
has a record, a vote, a lobbying history, or a policy position, that is helping
drive up the electricity and heating bills their own constituents pay, whether
through blocking or repealing clean energy projects, providing handouts to
dirtier and more expensive fuels like oil, coal and gas, or embracing costly
data center buildouts without protecting ratepayers from the bill or the
pollution. LCV Victory Fund calls this rising force the Energy Bill Voter: the parent,
retiree, or small business owner in a battleground community watching their
electricity and heating bills climb, and increasingly ready to vote on it. As we
detailed in June https://links.messages.lcv., 42% of swing voters say they are "very concerned" about rising electricity
costs, and new polling found that 35% of all voters, and 51% of undecided
voters, now rank the cost of utilities like electricity and heating as the
single most important issue in deciding their vote in Congressional elections.
Energy costs have risen 18% nationwide since Trump took office, with electricity
prices near data centers rising as much as 267% in some areas. The politics have
moved just as fast: Congressional Republicans, who voters credited by a 7-point
margin at the start of 2025 with making energy prices better, are now underwater
by 37 points on the same question, while Trump has swung from +15 to -41. The 2026 Dirty Dozen includes five Senate candidates and seven U.S. House
incumbents running in competitive races. Nearly all of them voted in 2025 for
the Republican Tax Law also known as the Big Ugly Bill, which eliminated tens of
billions of dollars in clean energy tax credits. Independent economic modeling
from the Rhodium Group and Energy Innovation projects that law's energy
provisions alone will raise average U.S. household energy costs by roughly $80
to nearly $200 a year by 2035 — with the steepest increases concentrated in
states these candidates represent — even as data center electricity demand adds
further pressure to utility bills nationwide. This is part of LCV Victory Fund's broader effort this cycle: an at-least-$50-million investment in the 2026 midterms https://links.messages.lcv., announced in July 2026, funding paid media, field, mail and content-creator
programs to reach Energy Bill Voters and hold Dirty Dozen candidates accountable

| | In recent weeks, I've held a series of health care hearings across Oregon. I wanted to give real patients and health care providers the opportunity to share how the Republican health care cuts have left them sicker, poorer, and worse off than ever before. Overwhelmingly, the message from these hearings was one that you yourself have probably experienced trying to access care, no matter where you live: health care is hard to come by, and it's expensive when you do. Months of trying to find a provider that will see you, followed by even more time spent battling over the phone with your insurance company that's finding any reason it can to delay and deny your care. Republicans took a health care system that was already failing parents and made it worse. They defunded federal health programs in order to give tax breaks to the billionaires and private health insurance companies that profit at the expense of denying you and your loved ones health care. This corrupt system demands a bold plan that meets the moment, and that plan is Medicare for all. These are extraordinary times, and they call for bold solutions. A quarter of a million Oregonians stand to lose their health insurance next year, and the story is similar in other states — much of it thanks to the cruel cuts in the Big Ugly Bill that Trump and his GOP allies in Congress rammed through last year. **We need a government that's actually willing to establish health care for all and lower costs.** I know this won't happen overnight. But in less than eight weeks, we have a chance to flip the Senate — and that's the first step toward making Medicare for All a reality. If Democrats win in November and retake a trifecta of power in 2028, as chairman of the Senate Finance Committee, I will have control over rebuilding America's health care system. And I'm building the comprehensive plan to get our country to Medicare for All. In the meantime, I'm fighting to elect Democrats in key Senate races who are serious about putting working families first, and aren't afraid to take on health insurance giants and Big Pharma. **These races will be too close to call all the way to Election Day.** [**Can I count on your help? clean_body: My vision? Medicare for All. | | | | In recent weeks, I've held a series of health care hearings across Oregon. I wanted to give real patients and health care providers the opportunity to share how the Republican health care cuts have left them sicker, poorer, and worse off than ever before. Overwhelmingly, the message from these hearings was one that you yourself have probably experienced trying to access care, no matter where you live: health care is hard to come by, and it's expensive when you do. Months of trying to find a provider that will see you, followed by even more time spent battling over the phone with your insurance company that's finding any reason it can to delay and deny your care. Republicans took a health care system that was already failing parents and made it worse. They defunded federal health programs in order to give tax breaks to the billionaires and private health insurance companies that profit at the expense of denying you and your loved ones health care. This corrupt system demands a bold plan that meets the moment, and that plan is Medicare for all. These are extraordinary times, and they call for bold solutions. A quarter of a million Oregonians stand to lose their health insurance next year, and the story is similar in other states — much of it thanks to the cruel cuts in the Big Ugly Bill that Trump and his GOP allies in Congress rammed through last year. We need a government that's actually willing to establish health care for all and lower costs. I know this won't happen overnight. But in less than eight weeks, we have a chance to flip the Senate — and that's the first step toward making Medicare for All a reality. If Democrats win in November and retake a trifecta of power in 2028, as chairman of the Senate Finance Committee, I will have control over rebuilding America's health care system. And I'm building the comprehensive plan to get our country to Medicare for All. In the meantime, I'm fighting to elect Democrats in key Senate races who are serious about putting working families first, and aren't afraid to take on health insurance giants and Big Pharma. name: True the Vote
subject: The truth is worth standing for
body:
One year later, the question isn't whether we remember. It's what we do now.
| | | September 10, 2026 | [**Read Online**](https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/lmu2rmld6efmhnpn9k5h6h8dqgkk7tgh4dogv/08hwh9h2l3w75ohlh5/aHR0cHM6Ly9ja2FyY2hpdmUuY29tL2IvMzh1cGhraDI4MmxkNmgzN3h4bDc1ZjQ1ZTBxcXdjN2h6eGczbQ==) |
---

Hi Friend —
One year ago today, Charlie Kirk was murdered in front of a crowd of students who had come to hear him speak and take questions. He was 31.
I have thought about that a great deal this year. About his family. About the loss. And about what happens to a country when people become afraid to say what they believe.
We can grieve Charlie and pray for those who loved him while being absolutely clear about this: his murder cannot become a warning that convinces the rest of us to retreat from public life. Violence cannot be allowed to decide who gets to speak.
This morning, I was in Dallas, alongside the RNC gathering, with more than 200 pastors who had come from all over the country. Small towns and big cities. Different congregations, different communities, but a shared concern for our country and the people they serve.
I did not have to talk them into caring. They already cared deeply. What they wanted to know was practical: What do we do? What can a church legally do? How can we help people understand what is happening in their own communities? How do we turn concern into something useful?
Those are the right questions. And there are real answers.
But we have to be willing to move beyond talking about everything that is wrong and take responsibility for what we can do.
Jesus tells us in John 8:32, “You shall know the truth, and the truth shall set you free.”
That promise is rooted in Him. And for me, it carries a responsibility: seek the truth, tell the truth, and live by it. Even when it is uncomfortable. Even when it costs something. Especially when looking the other way would be easier.
In our work at True the Vote, that means helping people move from wondering to knowing. Not assuming a headline tells the whole story. Not assuming someone else has checked. Learning what we can verify, documenting what we find, and following through.
A place to begin is your own voter record.
Go to [**ScanCheckProtect.org**](https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/lmu2rmld6efmhnpn9k5h6h8dqgkk7tgh4dogv/8ghqhohormp5v2ckh9/aHR0cHM6Ly9zY2FuY2hlY2twcm90ZWN0Lm9yZy8=)**** and check your registration and voting history. Help the other voters in your household check theirs. And if you have moved, check your previous addresses to make sure an old registration is not still active.
If something does not look right, Scan.Check.Protect. equips you to document and report it, and take the appropriate next steps.
Then share it. Help a family member. Send it to a friend. Introduce it to your church. You do not need a national platform to do something that matters to the person standing right beside you.
That is what encouraged me about this morning. These pastors were asking how to help their congregations become informed, prepared, and useful in their own communities. That is work worth doing, and True the Vote is here to help.
To get involved, reply to this email and tell us your city and state. Whether you are a pastor, a volunteer, or someone ready to serve for the first time, we will help you get connected.
And through all of it, we need to remember where our strength comes from.
Ephesians 6 tells us to put on the whole armor of God: truth, righteousness, the gospel of peace, faith, salvation, and the Word of God. It calls us to pray and, having done all, to stand.
We are not going to meet this moment through outrage alone. We need discernment. We need courage. We need the humility to keep learning and the endurance to keep serving.
We need God.
Today, please pray for Charlie’s family. Pray for these pastors and the communities they serve. And ask God to show each of us where we can be useful, right where we are.
We cannot undo the heartbreak of a year ago. But we can refuse to let fear have the final word in our own lives.
Put on the armor. Stand in the truth. Help your family and friends do the same. Working together, we can true the vote — and we can save the republic.
Keep the faith. Never quit. Ephesians 6 FTW!
Ever Onward,
| |

Fellow Conservative: In 1991, the mob came for Clarence Thomas. They smeared him. They tried to destroy his name, his reputation, and his honor. As Justice Thomas himself has put it, critics in Washington _"don't bomb you, necessarily, but they bomb your reputation or your good name or your honor."_ **He refused to cave.** And because he did, he became one of the four giants of the modern Supreme Court — alongside Justices Scalia, Alito, and Rehnquist. Senator Ted Cruz has just released a remarkable new book: _**Going Further: The Incomparable Clarence Thomas**_ , built on exclusive interviews with the Justice himself.

---
|
---
[](http://links.conservativesfordjt.com/u/click?_t=05b03ef2209247bcbdad7fd5099cd670&_m=b54ae8dd92344a04833c3a0f8b201cba&_e=KFHY72Vv9ng-20N2g1PwgtbzFfCtxts_4hdcEyXo0PKB52FrBtBbs6Ily-M4hQ0mZpBYtwatBmHkPBpVhutUZDaXfJBwOjhVQgjya25fc7zW2Z6VR_mWavoPJCrGfu5XYcUMZ3cGz6yTsEm-yvjnCgsiNLOBresYzlM3x4ydCuIwiIvbPeGdVhhKce1-eKUeoICA8wteYct0gHXWoFLTaAMrTYnZ_tY-H9JlkX7CSv7xOEOpArGIGDFIg1hxutctXRiOFxGGUv0dLLsYX4MDo3-QGPiN972XZboHbl5FJ4YV_3PXpPkYUz7x1i7zsYERUh4G4mdjxaUq0FWRO18kHevVRQZS9aPQXCHhRaRcRq6Xpb7FarMcjfGs7DjY1cbhVjDGAdAsltiWjrkTK72y4g%3D%3D)
---

It tells the story of a man who rose from grinding poverty in Pin Point, Georgia — raised by a grandfather he calls _"the single greatest human being I've ever met"_ — to become, in Cruz's words, the justice _"more willing to go back to the original Constitution... and to overturn precedent" than any other in history._

There's a moment in the book that says everything. When Justice Scalia told Thomas he was _"tilting at windmills"_ by trying to overturn bad precedent, Thomas shot back: _"Nino, windmills are dangerous."_

That is the kind of courage we need on the federal bench. And here is the part every conservative must understand:

**Clarence Thomas only reached the Supreme Court because the Senate confirmed him by just two votes.**

Presidents nominate judges. But the Senate confirms them. Every originalist on the bench, and every one we hope to see there, depends on having conservative senators willing to fight. When we lose the Senate, we lose the courts. It's that simple.

That's the mission of the Senate Conservatives Fund: electing principled conservatives to the U.S. Senate so we can confirm the next generation of Clarence Thomases, and stop the Left from ever again turning a confirmation hearing into a character assassination.

So today, we want to put Senator Cruz's book in your hands.

**When you contribute $50 or more to the Senate Conservatives Fund, we'll send you a copy of _Going Further: The Incomparable Clarence Thomas_ as our thank-you.** [**Please join us in the effort to build a conservative Senate by making a contribution today.**](http://links.conservativesfordjt.com/u/click?_t=05b03ef2209247bcbdad7fd5099cd670&_m=b54ae8dd92344a04833c3a0f8b201cba&_e=KFHY72Vv9ng-20N2g1PwgtbzFfCtxts_4hdcEyXo0PKB52FrBtBbs6Ily-M4hQ0mZpBYtwatBmHkPBpVhutUZDaXfJBwOjhVQgjya25fc7wF1AULuNzmu2UzlUV8pQWdNxHMFJKds9ZNAHwZfTUbxQQSbvtgIlf9Lz-ldIwXFv-Im3D7Zdx2dI4_ALaA2989D_HkdHPt2NYLoaw8yZXehr7UHlNX3_OPw3UXHYJPhWtJbT7_nUzFeuc6H-k6sN4_k17-ImUz3VbbHNwARdgesk863eKxLP3aNG-m6Cglmzqi8085-HudJZEwmlrvapW1tDkkq7B-OaVuH-QsnW5PB2PzVzUuKbAYpTM8mpV53Izj-y7GwoYN2QvrcMT0uPS8Fa4pXx7uJqucOSF1JiA3xA%3D%3D) Your support will help elect the conservative senators who will confirm judges like Justice Thomas — and will help make sure the next conservative nominee who refuses to bow to the woke mob has the votes to win. NYPD Commissioner Jessica Tisch **[created quite an awkward moment](https://substack.com/redirect/ee408749-72b4-4b17-8931-e7ed3cb893ef?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** during an NYPD event, Wednesday, by demanding "moral clarity" on 9/11, proclaiming that "terrorists" were to blame for the horrific attacks on America while she was standing right next to Mayor Zohran Mamdani, who was sitting motionless and starring blankly.
"Preserving that history also means preserving its moral clarity," Tisch said. "The men who attacked this city were terrorists. The men and women who ran into the towers to save innocent lives were heroes. Twenty-five years cannot be allowed to blur that distinction and shame on those who do."

# **Trump headlines GOP 's first midterm convention, urges "pretend I'm on the ballot"**
President Donald Trump **[kicked off the GOP's first-ever midterm convention](https://substack.com/redirect/b6727423-8825-45f5-a0b0-975937fc83e0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** in Dallas, urging supporters to "pretend" he's on the ballot to help finish his agenda, while unveiling new policy pledges including ending surprise medical billing, national voter ID, and death penalty provisions for major drug dealers.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/b6727423-8825-45f5-a0b0-975937fc83e0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

* **The event featured surprises including[a video from Sen. John Fetterman](https://substack.com/redirect/4f0fad66-f75c-40da-b59a-949dd17749bf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) criticizing "socialism"** and praising GOP Sen. Dave McCormick amid party-switch speculation, plus jumbotron images mocking communist streamer Hasan Piker, an ally of Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed who is closely linked to the DSA. Rising GOP figures, including Reps. Monica and Carlos De La Cruz, also took the stage.

# **TPUSA plans Charlie Kirk memorial as left-wing student group protests at UVU**

| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4a41ee78-6465-4c5e-805e-60c577bc3c6a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

All quotations below are from the September 1 post unless otherwise noted.
**The core claim**
Sheets opens with his signature theme: the devil's most effective weapon isn't force but cunning. He contrasts Genesis 3:1 with 1 Peter 5:8 -- Satan is "far more dangerous as the serpent -- through his craftiness -- than he is as the roaring lion... which speaks of his power. He operates as a hidden foe, camouflaging his efforts with seasoned skill."
Then comes the revelation claim at the heart of the piece:
"Roughly 30 years ago, Holy Spirit spoke to me that the 'strong man' over America was headquartered at the Supreme Court (See Matthew 12:29). I acknowledge the fact that this statement cannot be proven, but I stand by it."
The "strong man" language is the classic spiritual-warfare motif of Matthew 12:29 and Mark 3:27 -- the idea that a territorial evil power must first be "bound" before its domain can be plundered. In Sheets' telling, the Court is that strong man's address, and his bill of particulars is blunt: the Court "opened the door to more evil into our nation" than any government entity -- abortion, the redefinition of marriage, and the removal of God's influence from schools. "Numerous Justices," he writes, "have allowed demons to reshape and defile America," and the damage is "literally incalculable."
[Join Heartland Journal ®'s subscriber chatAvailable in the Substack app and on webJoin chat
---](https://open.substack.com/pub/heartlandjournal/chat?utm_source=chat_embed)
**Why the Court, of all places?**
Sheets' answer is institutional, and it's the most analytically interesting section of the post. Satan chose the Court because it is "unelected... with lifetime appointments, extreme and unchecked power, and the least amount of exposure." He then reaches for a founding-era authority:
"Thomas Jefferson was right to warn that the power of this unchecked Supreme Court would result in despotism. He insisted that it would place the United States 'under the despotism of an oligarchy'... Turns out Mr. Jefferson was pretty smart!"
That's a genuine Jefferson argument -- the 1820 letter to William Jarvis warning that judicial construction would make the Constitution "a mere thing of wax... the Judiciary... under the despotism of an oligarchy." Sheets' footnote cites the line in the post itself.
He also takes aim at the famous umpire analogy -- the framing John Roberts offered at his 2005 confirmation hearings, when he said judges don't make the rules, they call balls and strikes. Sheets agrees with the analogy but accuses many justices of breaking it: "many can't help but join the rules committee, twisting the words of the Constitution to fit their preferences." And then the escalation:
"When a Justice on the Court feels they have the Constitutional authority to redefine marriage... or to decree the right to kill babies in the womb, they are officially a despot. And I would add, under the influence of Baal and his underling, Molech."
That last sentence -- invoking ancient deities associated in Scripture with child sacrifice -- is the post's sharpest theological edge, and the moment readers will quote or screenshot.
**The hard part: making Americans care**
Sheets concedes the practical problem he's faced for three decades: "the White House and Congress typically remain at the top of everyone's governmental prayer list." The Court is obscure, and obscurity is camouflage. But he reports a shift "over the past 2-3 decades" as prayer ministries have targeted the Court, and he says "the Court is slowly changing" -- a notable admission of movement in the post-Dobbs era.
**The mobilization: "Consecrate the Court"**
The post is ultimately an invitation. Sheets spotlights Phillip Jauregui, the attorney who leads the Judicial Action Group, credited with work on "hundreds of judicial nominations over the past 20 years, including eight of the nine current United States Supreme Court justices" -- arithmetically, that means every current justice except Clarence Thomas, the only one seated before 1991. Jauregui is also the author of 'The Parable of the Prodigal Court'.
Each year, Jauregui hosts a prayer gathering timed to the Court's first day of its new session under the phrase the Lord gave him: "Consecrate the Court." This year's edition:
\- When: October 4-5, 2026 (the new term opens Monday, October 5 -- the first Monday in October, per tradition)
\- Where: The Museum of the Bible, Washington, D.C.
\- Who: Sheets will keynote the Monday-night dinner; prophetic leader Chuck Pierce and other ministry heads will participate
\- Tickets/info: JAGF.org -> EVENTS (tickets required)
Sheets is candid that this is not a rally: "an event like this is not as exciting as one with tens of thousands of people on the Washington Mall. But I assure you, it is just as important." His urgency is demographic: "Some of the Justices on the Bench are in their 70s. Resignations and replacements will no doubt take place soon. This is a very critical season!" (Thomas, Alito, and Sotomayor are all in their 70s, as is Chief Justice Roberts by 2026.)
His ask is specific: churches should "send a delegate," prayer ministries "send an intercessor," and everyone should pray -- even from home.
**The prayer and the decree**
The post closes in the standard Give Him 15 format. The prayer is a national repentance -- for rejecting God "through this institution," for the "loss of tens of millions of Americans," and for "powerful curses on our land" -- followed by a petition that the Court be brought "back under YOUR plans, purposes, precepts, and laws," that God "oversee the timing and decisions of all resignations and replacements," and that He "fill this branch of government and its building with Your presence once again." It ends "in the holy and all-powerful name of Yeshua."
The daily decree: "We decree that the Supreme Court of the United States is being reconsecrated and rededicated to Almighty God, Creator and Owner of all the earth."
**Context notes for readers**
\- Who is Dutch Sheets? A charismatic teacher with 45+ years in ministry and more than 20 books, founder of Dutch Sheets Ministries. 'Give Him 15' launched in 2020 as a daily 15-minute "Appeal to Heaven" intercession broadcast and has become one of the largest mobilizers of conservative prayer in America, sitting at the intersection of charismatic Christianity and constitutional politics.
\- The historical docket behind the rhetoric. The decisions Sheets alludes to are the familiar targets of religious conservatives: Engel v. Vitale (1962) and Abington v. Schempp (1963) on school prayer and Bible reading; Roe v. Wade (1973); and Obergefell v. Hodges (2015) on marriage. Since Dobbs (2022) overturned Roe, the campaign's attention has pivoted to the Court's remaining casualties on that list -- which is exactly why the prospect of new vacancies matters to this coalition.
\- The umpire line. Roberts' 2005 "balls and strikes" formulation is the most famous analogy in modern confirmation history. Sheets accepts it as the standard and indicts the Court by its own measure -- a rhetorically effective move even for readers who reject the demonology.
\- Timing is the tell. The event's dates are keyed to the first day of the Court's new term, and the post's urgency is keyed to the ages of sitting justices and the coming midterm season. This is a vacancy-and-confirmation strategy dressed in intercessory language -- or, from Sheets' side, intercession that happens to align with a vacancy strategy. Both readings are accurate to the text.
\- An honest caveat from the author himself. Sheets concedes his central revelation "cannot be proven." Critics will say that's the point -- an unfalsifiable claim anchoring a political campaign. Supporters will say prophecy has never submitted to peer review, and that the Court's decades of rulings are the evidence that matters. Substack readers should decide which burden of proof they accept.
**What to watch**
1\. The October 4-5 gathering itself -- turnout, which ministry networks show up, and whether any justices or congressional allies make quiet appearances.
2\. Retirement signals -- any justice in their 70s announcing plans; Sheets' network will treat timing as providence and will have been praying for it by name.
3\. The midterm tie-in. Sheets' September posts are building toward November -- the September 3 follow-up was titled "The Magnitude of the Upcoming Midterm Elections." The Court campaign and the midterm campaign are one integrated push.
Whatever one makes of the theology, the September 1 post is a window into how a major segment of the American church now engages the judiciary: not primarily through litigation or legislation, but through what Sheets calls a "prayer siege" -- sustained, targeted, organized intercession aimed at a single building at One First Street, in the conviction that the nation turns when its court does.
\---
Sources: Dutch Sheets, "Exposing the 'Strong Man,'" Give Him 15, September 1, 2026 (givehim15.com/post/september-1-2026); Give Him 15 archive; Jefferson letter to William C. Jarvis (1820); Roberts confirmation testimony (2005).

clean_body: The administration’s attack on state policies is pricing working-class students out of higher education. We're not going away quietly. | | | Peter, school is back in session. And the administration is once again targeting students in its mass delegalization campaign. In a coordinated effort to push higher education out of reach for low-income and working students, the Department of Justice has sued to strip in-state tuition from students in 21 states that let students qualify for in-state tuition regardless of immigration status. More than 120,000 students have already lost in-state tuition. Another 218,000 are at risk. 1 Immigrant youth have organized for years to win these laws. In states like California, the Dream Act has stood for over two decades.2We're not handing any of it back quietly. At the University of Houston, a senior watched her bill go from about $6,000 a semester to $14,000 — she worked on campus, took freelance jobs, borrowed from her mother, and graduated on time anyway.1 In South Texas, a 21-year-old who wanted to be a nurse gave up premed and transferred to a community college.1 In Florida, immigrant students are facing tuition spikes of over 300%.2 This is deliberate: keep working students underpaid, buried in debt, and far from a degree and the job that follows — then point them toward a handful of scholarships and call it opportunity. 2 Working people everywhere are being squeezed on rent, groceries, and healthcare while the wealthiest few consolidate more. The system is built to protect billionaire interests: their power, their wealth, their gain. Not ours. But together, we have the power — the billionaire class needs us more than we need them. Just a few months ago, immigration agents were showing up at our K-12 schools — children sat in class wondering whether federal agents were waiting for a classmate, a teacher, a parent. Our communities organized because students belong in classrooms. That resilience guides us now. Friends,

Working people are the backbone of the Hudson Valley. That is why I am deeply proud to have earned the endorsement of the NY AFL-CIO, as well as CSEA, NY State United Teachers, 1199 SEIU, Communications Workers of America, Retail, Wholesale and Department Store Union, and Theatrical Stage Employees Local One.

**It is an honor to stand with organized labor every day of this campaign.** I come from a working-class family. My grandfather and great-grandfather worked at the Montrose brickyard, my dad from Hopewell Junction worked construction, and my mom spent 48 years as a postal worker — raising three girls here in the Hudson Valley. I know what it’s like for families to struggle — I lived it. And it’s getting even worse as a direct result of Mike Lawler, who has voted with Trump 100% of the time. Nowhere is this clearer than in Lawler’s deciding vote for Trump’s One Big Ugly Bill — slashing healthcare, food assistance, and the crucial job-creating investments in the Inflation Reduction Act — all so Trump and his administration can fund tax breaks for billionaires. In Congress, I will fight every day for working people:

* Investing in infrastructure and clean energy projects that create good-paying jobs
* Enforcing prevailing wage laws so workers are paid what they deserve
* Expanding BOCES and trade skills programs so the next generation can thrive here without leaving
* Creating an American Public Service Home Loan Program so our teachers, nurses, law enforcement and first responders can afford to live in the communities they serve

Doing right by working families is why I’m in this fight. In the Army, failure was never an option — and I promise to bring that same mentality to Congress. With gratitude and fire, Cait Conley

clean_body: | | | | Friends, Working people are the backbone of the Hudson Valley. That is why I am deeply proud to have earned the endorsement of the NY AFL-CIO, as well as CSEA, NY State United Teachers, 1199 SEIU, Communications Workers of America, Retail, Wholesale and Department Store Union, and Theatrical Stage Employees Local One. It is an honor to stand with organized labor every day of this campaign. I come from a working-class family. My grandfather and great-grandfather worked at the Montrose brickyard, my dad from Hopewell Junction worked construction, and my mom spent 48 years as a postal worker — raising three girls here in the Hudson Valley. I know what it’s like for families to struggle — I lived it. And it’s getting even worse as a direct result of Mike Lawler, who has voted with Trump 100% of the time. Nowhere is this clearer than in Lawler’s deciding vote for Trump’s One Big Ugly Bill — slashing healthcare, food assistance, and the crucial job-creating investments in the Inflation Reduction Act — all so Trump and his administration can fund tax breaks for billionaires. In Congress, I will fight every day for working people: Investing in infrastructure and clean energy projects that create good-paying jobs Enforcing prevailing wage laws so workers are paid what they deserve Expanding BOCES and trade skills programs so the next generation can thrive here without leaving Creating an American Public Service Home Loan Program so our teachers, nurses, law enforcement and first responders can afford to live in the communities they serve Doing right by working families is why I’m in this fight. In the Army, failure was never an option — and I promise to bring that same mentality to Congress. subject: 💥Get Out and Get Inspired💥
body:
In September of 2017, my Command Chief and I...
---
| | | | | |
---
| | 💥Get Out and Get Inspired💥
---
In September of 2017, my Command Chief (Nate Perry) and I made an early morning drive down to Richmond, Virginia (I was the commander of Joint Base Andrews at the time). We arrived at our designated parking spot, unloaded our heavy bags of equipment, and made our way to the lobby of the Sun Trust Center in the middle of the city.
There we rendezvoused with our party, a small group of Airmen from the base. They were firefighters, security forces members, and paramedics. Alongside these first responders, we had one intimidating purpose – complete the 9/11 Memorial Stair Climb to honor those who paid the ultimate sacrifice in service to our communities as they ran towards danger on that fateful day in 2001.
Collectively we donned our full complement of firefighter gear and started the long and grueling climb up 110 stories, the height of the Twin Towers in lower Manhattan. The Sun Trust Center is not that tall, so we were forced to make four laps of the building (taking the elevator down to the bottom each time after reaching the top).
We were hotter, sweatier, and more tired than we had ever been – at least I was. But we made it!
There were some notable differences between our experience on that day and the experience faced by those heroic first responders twenty-five years ago:
* The Sun Trust Center’s air conditioning was working well in the stairway
* We didn’t experience a smoke-filled environment and there was no falling debris
* As we climbed up, there weren’t panicked people running in the opposite direction.

But the biggest difference was this – We were walking towards a finish line while the first responders on September 11, 2001 were running towards imminent danger.
Much like my evening ride-along with a Los Angeles County Sheriff gang unit in 2006, this experience was eye opening and life-changing. It allowed me to more thoroughly appreciate the heroism of first responders in communities throughout our nation who run towards danger in the most difficult of circumstances.
It was a lesson that would last a lifetime – I was permanently inspired by them!
This experience highlights an important leadership truth.
There are several reasons why a leader should regularly walk out of their office, dive into the trenches of their organization, and get their hands dirty. They should diligently schedule frequent times to do so.
What are the benefits?
* They will get to know the members of their team and allow the members of their team to get to know them.
* They will better understand the mission.
* They will more thoroughly be able to contextualize their decisions.
* They will gain first-hand experiences that will reveal challenges, barriers, and successes throughout the organization.
* They will be able to inspire the members of their team.

Yet, the best reason may be the least apparent! The leader will be inspired by the members of their team!
Along these lines, General Dwight D. Eisenhower said the following: “A commander meets to talk to his men to inspire them. With me it’s the other way around. I get inspired by you.”
This solemn anniversary for our nation is the perfect time to reflect upon our rightful appreciation of first responders. While the rest of us run away from danger, they run towards it. We should all be inspired by them!
In the meanwhile, leaders should commit to the simple principle described above. When you get out of your office to experience the efforts of the members of your team, they will be inspired. Please know, you will also be inspired by them.
Get Out and Get Inspired. Doing so will allow you the LEAD WELL!

* John

The clean energy sector is growing quickly across North Carolina, six times faster than the statewide economy.Brad Knott voted to repeal clean energy tax credits used by 89,000 North Carolina households, a move projected to raise average household energy costs by $215 in 2026. | | Dear Folks,

Ohio is suddenly at the center of a national fight over data centers and **The Wall Street Journal put it on the front page!**

A decade ago, Ohio created generous tax incentives to attract data centers. The industry we subsidized then barely resembles the one operating today.

These are now some of the largest and wealthiest corporations on EARTH, building enormous facilities, threatening our air quality and water supplies, and consuming staggering amounts of electricity while Ohio taxpayers continue picking up part of the tab.

As I told the Wall Street Journal:

_“They seem to have more money than God, and they’re able to build without the need for these types of incentives.”_

Ohio’s incentives helped give data centers an effective tax rate of just 1.2% in 2025, the lowest among 15 states analyzed by EY.

---
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138968228/645774966/745496376?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjMvMS8xMjcxMTkiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMjcwY2U5YWItNjVhZC1mMTExLTliMzMtMDAyMjQ4MmE5MzNiIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=6XWWQcJiTov-dM7dbrqhdR4noaTTFjQlsRfFsTYvyec=&emci=dadbc541-64ad-f111-9b33-0022482a933b&emdi=270ce9ab-65ad-f111-9b33-0022482a933b&ceid=2017840)
---
Meanwhile, private data-center construction spending reached roughly $4.4 BILLION in a single month this summer.

Read that again: **$4.4 billion. In one month.**

This industry does not need a taxpayer handout to keep building.

clean_body: | | | = | | Dear Folks, Ohio is suddenly at the center of a national fight over data centers and The Wall Street Journal put it on the front page! A decade ago, Ohio created generous tax incentives to attract data centers. The industry we subsidized then barely resembles the one operating today. These are now some of the largest and wealthiest corporations on EARTH, building enormous facilities, threatening our air quality and water supplies, and consuming staggering amounts of electricity while Ohio taxpayers continue picking up part of the tab. As I told the Wall Street Journal: “They seem to have more money than God, and they’re able to build without the need for these types of incentives.” Ohio’s incentives helped give data centers an effective tax rate of just 1.2% in 2025, the lowest among 15 states analyzed by EY. Building makeshift shelters in Jabal Zaid displaced persons camp, Wednesday, September 9, 2026. Photo: Khalid Al-Banna.
TAIZ, Yemen*--This week, as Ansarallah forces advanced by the hour to seize the port city of Mokha and secure access to the strategic Bab al-Mandab strait off the coast of Yemen, residents of Taiz braced for more fighting.
Over the past week, some of the fiercest battles between Ansarallah (also known as the Houthis) and Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces took place in the hills surrounding Taiz--a crucial trade hub in southwestern Yemen, situated between Ibb, Mokha, Hodeidah, and Aden.
On Wednesday, Saudi Arabia bombed five Yemeni governorates more than 50 times in a single 12-hour span. On Sunday, powerful explosions shook Taiz and several residential areas were shelled. The Yemeni government attributed the explosions to Ansarallah. Ansarallah neither claimed the bombings nor denied them, but the fighting proved decisive ahead of Ansarallah's capture of Mokha later in the week.
Thousands of households from across the Taiz governorate have been displaced since September 3, when a new round of intensified fighting began. Across Yemen, nearly 20,000 have fled their homes, according to the International Organization for Migration. Over the past week, at least 500 have been killed, according to the AFP, most of them combatants. Among the dead and wounded are civilians, including numerous children.

Many of the displaced are from Jabal Habashi, a district in the Taiz governorate characterized by greenery, agriculture, and terraced hills. Jabal Habashi has seen the majority of the violence in the area--and its families have experienced among the highest rates of displacement. Because of its strategic position, wedged between Taiz and Mokha, it is a crucial passageway for securing Yemen's west coast.
Yet, as Ansarallah has been increasingly taking hold of the districts surrounding the provincial capital, which is thus far still under the control of the Saudi-backed Yemeni government, has attempted to retain a sense of normalcy: Its markets are bustling and people walk the streets, despite the presence of military convoys bringing in injured fighters to its hospitals.
"When I heard the explosions I remembered the difficult days of the beginning of the war in 2015," said Taiz city resident Mohammed Abdulmalik, "and felt with the suffering of the population who witness it nowadays in west Taiz."
## **Civilian Targeting**
Drop Site News visited several hospitals in the city of Taiz, including Al Thawra and Al Safwah, speaking with local patients hospitalized with injuries incurred in the ongoing fighting. The aisles of these hospitals were overflowing with patients; the majority of them were injured fighters, although the hospital is treating civilians as well. Ashraf, a 47-year-old construction worker from the Jabal Habashi district, was injured while attempting to flee his village on Saturday with his family, a day after heavy fighting with shelling broke out around him. (Ashraf is a pseudonym used for his safety.)
"We were moving in small separate groups to reduce the risk of being targeted, and an explosion went off. I lost consciousness and fainted, and was later evacuated to Taiz."
Ashraf woke up in a hospital surrounded by other wounded civilians, including children. Still sitting in a hospital bed, he told Drop Site, "It is always us civilians who suffer the brunt of this war."
At a private hospital also in Taiz, four injured children were in hospital beds, staying in the same room: three boys and one girl, who was the eldest. The girl and two of the boys were siblings, while the fourth boy was their neighbor.
The children's guardian, their uncle, told Drop Site he had brought them from the Jabal Habashi district to Taiz city after their home was shelled.
"On Friday, we all stayed home because the fighting was fierce," he told us. "But by the afternoon, things had calmed down, and the children went out to play in front of the house as usual. Then we heard an explosion nearby and the screams of other children. We ran out and found the four of them on the floor, bleeding." He was uncertain whether Ansarallah or the Saudi-backed government forces had caused the explosion, as both had been firing at each other.
The uncle said they normally could not afford hospital costs, but an international NGO operating locally funded their stay at the private facility."I just hope they recover and can return home. Their parents are stuck in the village, as leaving is too dangerous right now. So I am taking care of them for the time being."
## **Families Torn Apart**
The Jabal Zaid camp for Internally Displaced People (IDP), nestled between the green valleys of Taiz governorate, is one of several camps that have absorbed at least 5,600 households displaced across the Taiz and Hodeidah governorates in the past week, according to the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA). Residents here live in makeshift tents built from scant, hard-to-source materials.
Rahma, a displaced woman at Jabal Zaid who asked to go only by her first name, told Drop Site News that her family--who was already displaced by fighting a decade ago and living in a different IDP camp--had not only been displaced again, but divided. "When fighting broke out near our [first] camp on Friday, we took our children and fled the area," she said. "Later that same day, my husband returned to bring our belongings. We waited for him until the next day, but he didn't come back. We were terrified he might have been killed or injured."
Rahma later learned from neighbors that he was stuck in the middle of the fighting and no one was allowed to leave the area. Five days later, Rahma's husband was still trapped in the middle of the fighting.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9fbfb244-69bf-4fe6-a555-56687c962b99?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Nujud Mohammed and her children at Jabal Zaid camp on Wednesday, September 9, 2026. Photo: Khalid Al-Banna.
Nujud Mohammed, 28, a mother of six also displaced at Jabal Zaid, described a similar rupture. She is originally from Al Barah, a site that has seen heavy clashes due to its position on the supply route connecting Taiz and Mokha, and has been increasingly targeted by Yemeni government forces and allied warplanes attempting to repel Ansarallah's advance.
"I tried to return to retrieve our belongings," she said, "but the road was blocked. We weren't allowed to reach our old camp to take anything. Our area is now encircled by fighting, and no one can enter or leave. So I returned with nothing. I praise Allah that we are safe, and I trust that He will compensate us for everything we lost."
For many at Jabal Zaid, the past week is not a first displacement but a second, or third. Nujud's family fled to Jabal Habashi nine years ago, at the start of Yemen's civil war, and had lived there ever since.
"Nine years ago we fled because of the fighting in our area. We spent nine years in Jabal Habashi, but on Friday, sudden fighting reached our camp. I immediately took my children and walked from the afternoon until sunset, when we finally found a car that brought us to this camp."
Surrounded by her children, the youngest of whom is still a toddler, she cooked flatbread over a fire using plastic basins and a makeshift fire. "It isn't easy to start over in a new camp, but we have been forced to do so because we have no alternative."
## **Camp Without Aid**
Nujud and her children now share a single tent with three other families, relying on the goodwill oftheir new neighbors for food, mattresses, and other basic goods. "No humanitarian organizations have arrived yet," she said. "Only two representatives from a relief agency came to take our names and ask questions, but no aid has been delivered. We are in dire need of shelter and food."
Looking at the temporary tent housing her, she said: "All I want at this moment is for the war to end so I can return."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/eadf6d63-229d-4e89-b9d8-592a27ca3386?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Mohammed Ahmed and his family in Jabal Zaid camp, Wednesday, September 9, 2026. Photo: Khalid al-Banna.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/7d39a08f-7f14-4f54-b2bc-fa466dbc632e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Mohammed Ahmed and his family in Jabal Zaid camp, Wednesday, September 9, 2026. Photo: Khalid al-Banna.
Mohammed Ahmed, 35, a father in the camp, said his family had expected help to be awaiting them once they reached safety: "We assumed that as soon as we reached a safe area, we would receive support from humanitarian organizations, since we know they cannot reach dangerous frontlines," where their home is. Indeed, many families chose Jabal Zaid precisely because it is considered a safe area, yet no agency has provided aid there so far.
"If this situation continues, our children could starve to death, as there are no job opportunities here and no one to help us."
Fawzi Al-Habashi, Director of the Better Life Association for Coexistence and Development, a local humanitarian organization that provides food, shelter, and hygiene assistance, said NGOs "have monitored and documented the displacement movement, conducted initial needs assessments, and coordinated with local authorities, providing limited emergency aid to the most vulnerable families based on priority."
However, as explained by Baraa Shaiban, a Yemeni political analyst who spoke to Drop Site, the suddenness of the displacement, combined with severe funding shortages that have characterized many areas of Yemen (particularly areas controlled by Ansarallah where international aid access has been restricted for years), has hindered the delivery of emergency assistance.
The Saudi-led war against Ansarallah that began in 2015 after the group took over Sana'a spawned one of the world's worst humanitarian crises and left over 150,000 dead until an uneasy truce was reached in 2022. Many Yemeni civilians are experiencing the clashes as a return to heightened instability, as they see their lives starting over once again, in yet another displacement camp.
As Shaiban put it: "Whatever normality people were hoping to get, it is quickly fading away."
_* A journalist in Yemen contributed reporting._
