If our work matters to you, | | ---|---|--- Building makeshift shelters in Jabal Zaid displaced persons camp, Wednesday, September 9, 2026. Photo: Khalid Al-Banna. TAIZ, Yemen--This week, as Ansarallah forces advanced by the hour to seize the port city of Mokha and secure access to the strategic Bab al-Mandab strait off the coast of Yemen, residents of Taiz braced for more fighting. Over the past week, some of the fiercest battles between Ansarallah (also known as the Houthis) and Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces took place in the hills surrounding Taiz--a crucial trade hub in southwestern Yemen, situated between Ibb, Mokha, Hodeidah, and Aden. On Wednesday, Saudi Arabia bombed five Yemeni governorates more than 50 times in a single 12-hour span. On Sunday, powerful explosions shook Taiz and several residential areas were shelled. The Yemeni government attributed the explosions to Ansarallah. Ansarallah neither claimed the bombings nor denied them, but the fighting proved decisive ahead of Ansarallah's capture of Mokha later in the week. Thousands of households from across the Taiz governorate have been displaced since September 3, when a new round of intensified fighting began. Across Yemen, nearly 20,000 have fled their homes, according to the International Organization for Migration. Over the past week, at least 500 have been killed, according to the AFP, most of them combatants. Among the dead and wounded are civilians, including numerous children. Drop Site is always free to read. Subscribe today: Many of the displaced are from Jabal Habashi, a district in the Taiz governorate characterized by greenery, agriculture, and terraced hills. Jabal Habashi has seen the majority of the violence in the area--and its families have experienced among the highest rates of displacement. Because of its strategic position, wedged between Taiz and Mokha, it is a crucial passageway for securing Yemen's west coast. Yet, as Ansarallah has been increasingly taking hold of the districts surrounding the provincial capital, which is thus far still under the control of the Saudi-backed Yemeni government, has attempted to retain a sense of normalcy: Its markets are bustling and people walk the streets, despite the presence of military convoys bringing in injured fighters to its hospitals. "When I heard the explosions I remembered the difficult days of the beginning of the war in 2015," said Taiz city resident Mohammed Abdulmalik, "and felt with the suffering of the population who witness it nowadays in west Taiz." Civilian Targeting Drop Site News visited several hospitals in the city of Taiz, including Al Thawra and Al Safwah, speaking with local patients hospitalized with injuries incurred in the ongoing fighting. The aisles of these hospitals were overflowing with patients; the majority of them were injured fighters, although the hospital is treating civilians as well. Ashraf, a 47-year-old construction worker from the Jabal Habashi district, was injured while attempting to flee his village on Saturday with his family, a day after heavy fighting with shelling broke out around him. (Ashraf is a pseudonym used for his safety.) "We were moving in small separate groups to reduce the risk of being targeted, and an explosion went off. I lost consciousness and fainted, and was later evacuated to Taiz." Ashraf woke up in a hospital surrounded by other wounded civilians, including children. Still sitting in a hospital bed, he told Drop Site, "It is always us civilians who suffer the brunt of this war." At a private hospital also in Taiz, four injured children were in hospital beds, staying in the same room: three boys and one girl, who was the eldest. The girl and two of the boys were siblings, while the fourth boy was their neighbor. The children's guardian, their uncle, told Drop Site he had brought them from the Jabal Habashi district to Taiz city after their home was shelled. "On Friday, we all stayed home because the fighting was fierce," he told us. "But by the afternoon, things had calmed down, and the children went out to play in front of the house as usual. Then we heard an explosion nearby and the screams of other children. We ran out and found the four of them on the floor, bleeding." He was uncertain whether Ansarallah or the Saudi-backed government forces had caused the explosion, as both had been firing at each other. The uncle said they normally could not afford hospital costs, but an international NGO operating locally funded their stay at the private facility."I just hope they recover and can return home. Their parents are stuck in the village, as leaving is too dangerous right now. So I am taking care of them for the time being." Families Torn Apart The Jabal Zaid camp for Internally Displaced People (IDP), nestled between the green valleys of Taiz governorate, is one of several camps that have absorbed at least 5,600 households displaced across the Taiz and Hodeidah governorates in the past week, according to the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA). Residents here live in makeshift tents built from scant, hard-to-source materials. Rahma, a displaced woman at Jabal Zaid who asked to go only by her first name, told Drop Site News that her family--who was already displaced by fighting a decade ago and living in a different IDP camp--had not only been displaced again, but divided. "When fighting broke out near our [first] camp on Friday, we took our children and fled the area," she said. "Later that same day, my husband returned to bring our belongings. We waited for him until the next day, but he didn't come back. We were terrified he might have been killed or injured." Rahma later learned from neighbors that he was stuck in the middle of the fighting and no one was allowed to leave the area. Five days later, Rahma's husband was still trapped in the middle of the fighting. | | ---|---|--- Nujud Mohammed and her children at Jabal Zaid camp on Wednesday, September 9, 2026. Photo: Khalid Al-Banna. Nujud Mohammed, 28, a mother of six also displaced at Jabal Zaid, described a similar rupture. She is originally from Al Barah, a site that has seen heavy clashes due to its position on the supply route connecting Taiz and Mokha, and has been increasingly targeted by Yemeni government forces and allied warplanes attempting to repel Ansarallah's advance. "I tried to return to retrieve our belongings," she said, "but the road was blocked. We weren't allowed to reach our old camp to take anything. Our area is now encircled by fighting, and no one can enter or leave. So I returned with nothing. I praise Allah that we are safe, and I trust that He will compensate us for everything we lost." For many at Jabal Zaid, the past week is not a first displacement but a second, or third. Nujud's family fled to Jabal Habashi nine years ago, at the start of Yemen's civil war, and had lived there ever since. "Nine years ago we fled because of the fighting in our area. We spent nine years in Jabal Habashi, but on Friday, sudden fighting reached our camp. I immediately took my children and walked from the afternoon until sunset, when we finally found a car that brought us to this camp." Surrounded by her children, the youngest of whom is still a toddler, she cooked flatbread over a fire using plastic basins and a makeshift fire. "It isn't easy to start over in a new camp, but we have been forced to do so because we have no alternative." Camp Without Aid Nujud and her children now share a single tent with three other families, relying on the goodwill oftheir new neighbors for food, mattresses, and other basic goods. "No humanitarian organizations have arrived yet," she said. "Only two representatives from a relief agency came to take our names and ask questions, but no aid has been delivered. We are in dire need of shelter and food." Looking at the temporary tent housing her, she said: "All I want at this moment is for the war to end so I can return." | | ---|---|--- Mohammed Ahmed and his family in Jabal Zaid camp, Wednesday, September 9, 2026. Photo: Khalid al-Banna. | | ---|---|--- Mohammed Ahmed and his family in Jabal Zaid camp, Wednesday, September 9, 2026. Photo: Khalid al-Banna. Mohammed Ahmed, 35, a father in the camp, said his family had expected help to be awaiting them once they reached safety: "We assumed that as soon as we reached a safe area, we would receive support from humanitarian organizations, since we know they cannot reach dangerous frontlines," where their home is. Indeed, many families chose Jabal Zaid precisely because it is considered a safe area, yet no agency has provided aid there so far. "If this situation continues, our children could starve to death, as there are no job opportunities here and no one to help us." Fawzi Al-Habashi, Director of the Better Life Association for Coexistence and Development, a local humanitarian organization that provides food, shelter, and hygiene assistance, said NGOs "have monitored and documented the displacement movement, conducted initial needs assessments, and coordinated with local authorities, providing limited emergency aid to the most vulnerable families based on priority." However, as explained by Baraa Shaiban, a Yemeni political analyst who spoke to Drop Site, the suddenness of the displacement, combined with severe funding shortages that have characterized many areas of Yemen (particularly areas controlled by Ansarallah where international aid access has been restricted for years), has hindered the delivery of emergency assistance. The Saudi-led war against Ansarallah that began in 2015 after the group took over Sana'a spawned one of the world's worst humanitarian crises and left over 150,000 dead until an uneasy truce was reached in 2022. Many Yemeni civilians are experiencing the clashes as a return to heightened instability, as they see their lives starting over once again, in yet another displacement camp. As Shaiban put it: "Whatever normality people were hoping to get, it is quickly fading away." Unless we stop them, _these California-style rules are headed your way_. 1.2 million registered voters in Texas are on something called a suspense list. That's six percent of all registered voters in the entire state.
Three hundred thousand of those people are in Harris County. Houston. One of the most diverse counties in the country.
Standing Our Ground is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..HhKchu40rQh63hC1wB6v8WMpG0HtxWpsaaSzgDaq5pE?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=214814326)
Most of them have no idea.
Here's how it worked. The state tried to verify addresses by mail. People didn't respond. Maybe they moved. Maybe they never got the letter. Maybe life happened. And the state just quietly moved them to this list. You can still vote if you're on it, but your registration can be cancelled. And the deadline to fix it is October 5th.
October 5th.
Texas has no online voter registration. No same-day registration. So if you miss that window, you might show up in November and find out you can't vote.
Now. I don't think this is unrelated to the fact that Trump called Greg Abbott personally to push redistricting that drew people like Jasmine Crockett out of her district. Think about who's on that suspense list. Think about where Harris County is. Think about who lives there.
I'm not speculating. I'm connecting dots that are right in front of us.
Before I move on, I want to drop some good news because I don't want you walking away feeling like everything is doom. Maryland's state Supreme Court just handed us a win. There is now a question going on the ballot to redraw congressional districts, which would draw out Andy Harris and his insurrection-loving self. Don't mess with us, Maryland. That's real. That matters.

Hi, Peter — this is Katie Hobbs, governor of Arizona. It’s because of folks like you that we beat MAGA extremist Kari Lake by just 17,117 votes in 2022. And it will be thanks to folks like you that we beat far-right election-denier Andy Biggs this November. For the sake of our state’s future, _we must_. **Our work to keep moving Arizona forward has only just begun, and the stakes in this race are sky-high.[_Before I share more of my story with you, will you split a donation of $10 or more to my re-election campaign and Yassamin Ansari?_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138969199/645778039/1476462686?amount=10&refcode=LOC_EM_FR_2026.09.10_Katie-Hobbs-Split-Bio_B1_F1_S1_C1_60OP_N-T0&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS83OTA5NyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2OTFhMTI0Yi02OWFkLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTkzM2IiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=EEJkva_JLTz6oYE2SyxR5plQmEQfrI7Y15MwFi6k7rA=)** I’m running for re-election as Arizona’s governor because the work we started almost four years ago must be continued by someone who understands what it means to struggle. I don’t have the story of a typical politician, Peter. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138969200/645778040/1476462686?amount=10&refcode=LOC_EM_FR_2026.09.10_Katie-Hobbs-Split-Bio_B1_F1_S1_C1_60OP_N-T0&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS83OTA5NyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2OTFhMTI0Yi02OWFkLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTkzM2IiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=EEJkva_JLTz6oYE2SyxR5plQmEQfrI7Y15MwFi6k7rA=) I’m a born and raised Arizonan from a working-class family in Tempe that often relied on food stamps and church support to make ends meet. I worked at fast food restaurants like Burger King and Pizza Hut to pay my way through school. My husband and I raised our kids through the Great Recession, experienced a home foreclosure, and we’re still paying off our student loans. I went on to become a social worker to treat the root problems facing our most vulnerable communities. It was because of my background in social work that I decided to run for office in the first place. I realized: _if you can’t change the policy, you have to change the people making it._ So I ran for office — and I won. But after that, I still had to take a second job driving for Uber to make sure my kids had Christmas presents. When I say this work is personal to me, I mean it. **As governor, I’ve always pledged to fight just as hard every day for your family as I fought for mine — and that’s what I promise to keep doing when re-elected this November.** Together, we’ve cut $1.4 billion in taxes for working-class Arizonans, announced $3 million in childcare grants to give families breathing room, wiped out medical debt for nearly 700,000 Arizonans, paused tax giveaways to data centers for three years, and successfully fought to repeal the total abortion ban and defend reproductive rights. But all of that progress is on the line come November. **My Republican opponent, Andy Biggs, is as extreme as they come:** he pushed election conspiracy theories, voted against certifying the 2020 presidential election results, helped organize the events that led to the January 6th insurrection, and to this day, he won’t admit that Donald Trump lost in 2020 or that I won in 2022. If this man becomes governor, _he will be the one responsible for certifying the 2028 presidential election results in Arizona._ Plus, he cheered when the Supreme Court overturned _Roe v. Wade_ and supports a total abortion ban; he voted to gut Arizonans’ healthcare and other services to give tax breaks to billionaires; and he supported Trump’s disastrous tariffs that have cost Arizona families and small businesses. He also has a history of protecting predators over women and girls. **Biggs isn’t right for Arizona, but he has the full backing of Donald Trump, JD Vance, and national Republicans** — who have collectively named this seat as one of their top targets to flip red in 2026, and they’re prepared to spend _whatever it takes_ to do it. My opponent may have Trump’s network, his MAGA megadonors, and far-right super PACs in his corner, but I have something far better: **you.** **[_So please, Peter: Chip in any amount now to Yassamin Ansari and my campaign to help us win this critical race on November 3rd. We won by less than 1% in 2022, so if we’re going to win one of the most competitive races in the country and keep moving Arizona forward, it’s going to take all of us._](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138969201/645778041/1476462686?amount=10&refcode=LOC_EM_FR_2026.09.10_Katie-Hobbs-Split-Bio_B1_F1_S1_C1_60OP_N-T0&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS83OTA5NyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2OTFhMTI0Yi02OWFkLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTkzM2IiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=EEJkva_JLTz6oYE2SyxR5plQmEQfrI7Y15MwFi6k7rA=)** | _If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your split donation to Katie Hobbs and Yassamin Ansari will go through immediately:_

That’s right. There are three big ways we can put a strong check on his administration. Here's my plan: 1. Once we have that power, we can block any far-right, extremist judge that Trump nominates to the Supreme Court. 3. This is our chance to actually put a stop to Trump as soon as possible — and I’m not taking this chance for granted. clean_body: I'm proud to stand with Darline Graham, and I'm asking you to do the same. | Fellow Patriot, Darline Graham is a principled conservative leader and a strong advocate for South Carolina families. And I am proud to give her my full support. Darline’s brother and my dear friend, Lindsey Graham, served South Carolina with distinction. Darline carries that same sense of duty into this fight in her own way. Fellow Patriot, she is not a career politician. She spent nearly thirty years serving South Carolina before she ever ran for anything, and she stepped into this race the same way she has approached everything else in her life: because it was needed, not because she wanted the title. Her Democrat opponent, with the help of the National Democrats, has raised nearly $11 million to try to flip this seat. Hollywood donors and DC insiders think that if they can pour enough money into this race, they can elect the most radical Democrat ever nominated for statewide office in South Carolina. Every attack ad between now and November is designed to convince South Carolina that her Democrat opponent isn’t a radical, paid gun control advocate or a leader of “White Women for Kamala Harris.” Darline’s Democrat opponent opposed South Carolina's law keeping girls' sports for girls. If she’s elected, she’ll back expanding the U.S. Supreme Court. We know better, but right now, Darline doesn’t have the same resources to set the record straight. Darline has already proved she can lead in just a few short months in the Senate, and I know she will continue representing South Carolina with the same purpose and commitment her brother did. South Carolina deserves a senator who has already spent a lifetime proving she will fight for it. clean_body: I think you should hear it | | | | | Peter , I flew above battlefields, passing burning husks of armored vehicles, and in Iraq I poured enough sand out of my boots to fill a desert. You would think that after flying an Apache helicopter through an active war zone, and having God knows how many stray bullets shot my direction, there’s not a thing on this planet that could scare me. I thought so too, until my team reminded me about what’s coming in the next few days. Let me explain. This campaign’s bigger than anything I’ve done in Iraq. Rather than covering for a team on the ground, the fate of more than 10 million people will be decided in November. Campaigning isn’t easy, and sometimes it feels like the weight of the world is on my shoulders. Just before I typed this email, my team reminded me about our upcoming End-of-Quarter fundraising deadline. This isn’t just an arbitrary deadline; this is one of our last BIG goals before the November election. I’m not going to ask you to dig deep into your pockets. All I’m asking is a $1 or more donation, which will go right into my campaign's war chest and help me and President Trump take down the Democrat machine come November. As a combat veteran and a patriot - I give you my word that every dollar matters, and I’m eternally thankful for ANY gift you can make. Time is running out. Thank you for listening, and I hope I can count on your help. | | — John James Republican Nominee for Governor | | Paid for by John James for MI | | 35744 Van Dyke Avenue, Sterling Heights, MI 48312 The use of John James' military images, uniforms, or personnel does not imply endorsement by the Department of War or any branch of the U.S. military. |

**It’s official: I am the Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate here in New Hampshire.**

I’m so grateful to every Granite Stater who put their trust in me and helped build this campaign together.

Growing up in Manchester and working alongside my family at our restaurant, I learned that you don’t get ahead just by making promises. You have to be accountable. You listen to people, work hard, and deliver.

That’s the same approach I’ve brought to Congress, and it’s why I’m running for U.S. Senate.

I’m running to make New Hampshire more affordable for working families; protect Social Security, Medicare, and Medicaid; safeguard reproductive freedom; and stand up for the small businesses that are the backbone of our communities.

**And now our general election fight against John Sununu officially begins.**

Political experts just changed this race to a Toss-up, Peter. The fact is: New Hampshire is a fiercely independent state, and this election could go either way. The country is watching, and the outcome here in New Hampshire will determine control of the U.S. Senate and what the next two years look like for millions of families across the country.

Supreme Court blocks new gerrymandered map Peter, between all the news alerts and different court rulings, you may have some questions about what’s actually happening with Missouri’s map — and we’ve got answers. Here’s the bottom line: Because Missourians kept fighting back for fairness, Republicans’ new gerrymandered map will NOT take effect this November. This outcome was far from a given. It only happened because the fair maps movement refused to back down. (Hint: That’s our plan in every state where Republicans try to rig the rules —= So what just happened? The Supreme Court ruled that Missouri Republicans’ new gerrymander cannot be used in the midterm election. This is the map lawmakers drew to try to squeeze out (read: steal) an extra U.S. House seat for themselves by splitting up Kansas City and diluting the voting power of Black Missourians. Which map will be in effect for November? The map that was passed in 2022! Not the new GOP gerrymander. Donald Trump and Republicans failed to eliminate a Democratic member of the state’s congressional delegation. They even tried to ignore the Missouri Supreme Court ruling last week that stopped the map from taking effect — but the U.S. Supreme Court shut that down earlier today. Wasn’t there also going to be a referendum about the new gerrymander? What’s happening with that now? The referendum will be on the ballot in November, despite Republicans’ attempts to sabotage it. Voters will have a chance to reject the new gerrymander and keep it from taking effect in future years. What does this mean beyond November? It puts Republican map manipulators on notice: their gerrymanders will not go unanswered. Our movement will keep challenging this cynical Republican power grab, state by state. Peter,

balance of power. Our movement has become the dominant force in the
Democratic Party, now let’s do the same at the ballot box.

co-chair, on the history of our movement and the role grassroots
organizing plays in building political power.

a decade of organizing around policy and how we’re transforming the
Democratic Party from the inside out.

Board of Aldermen, on building progressive political infrastructure at the
local level and developing candidates who move from activism to local,
state and federal office.

name: Eric Burlison
subject: One year without Charlie Kirk
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Eric Burlison for Congress
body:
Reflecting on the legacy of a true champion for America’s youth and conservative values| | |
---
One year ago today, our nation lost a fearless fighter, a devoted husband and father, and a deeply cherished friend to so many of us in the conservative movement: Charlie Kirk. It’s still difficult to process that a full year has passed since Charlie was taken from us. **In the days and months following that terrible day, we felt the profound weight of his absence – not just on college campuses or in political debates, but in the heart of our conservative family.** Charlie possessed a rare, generational courage. At a time when so many were content to stay silent, Charlie stepped directly into the fire. **He poured his life into empowering young Americans, defending our constitutional liberties, and unapologetically proclaiming his faith in God.** He believed with every fiber of his being that America’s best days were still ahead if we simply had the fortitude to stand up for the truth. As I reflect on his life today, I am reminded that Charlie didn’t fight out of anger – he fought out of love. Love for his family, love for our country, and love for the principles that make America the greatest nation on earth. While he is no longer with us, the torch he lit in the hearts of millions of young patriots burns brighter than ever. **His voice may be silent, but his life’s work continues to echo across high school and college campuses in every corner of our country.** Today, I ask you to join my family in honoring Charlie’s memory. Please keep his wife, Erika, their sweet children, and the entire Kirk family in your prayers as they navigate this painful anniversary. **May we honor Charlie’s legacy not just with our words, but by carrying forward his unwavering commitment to faith, family, and freedom.** God bless you, and God bless the memory of Charlie Kirk. _Rep. Eric Burlison_

name: Mark Ronchetti
subject: An AI Insider Just Issued a Terrifying Warning
body:
Plus, New Ads, AI Politics & Remembering 9/11| New episode for dpwillis67@gmail.com

| | | | | |
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/N6m6Pr8z0lt?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
| | | | | | An AI Insider Just Issued a Terrifying Warning!We use AI. You probably do too.
But when the people actually BUILDING this technology start publicly warning that they’re worried about where it’s headed, we think it’s worth paying attention.And one former Anthropic researcher just issued a warning that stopped us in our tracks.
🔥 THE PEOPLE BUILDING AI ARE SOUNDING THE ALARMJacob Coxon, who worked on AI research at Anthropic and previously at OpenAI, publicly quit and warned about the race toward increasingly powerful artificial intelligence. His concern? The companies developing this technology are racing toward super-intelligence without knowing for certain that humans will remain in control.
And he isn't alone.
Another Anthropic researcher publicly backed Coxon's concerns and said he believes there is a greater than 10% chance AI could cause catastrophic harm to humanity within the next decade. We break down what they're saying — and why this conversation suddenly feels a lot less like science fiction.
Spoiler alert: Remember when The Terminator seemed completely ridiculous? It hits a little differently now.
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/2dJNwx4Nzgl?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
| |

🚨 AI IS ALREADY CHANGING OUR ELECTIONS
We don't even have to wait for super-intelligence to see a problem. The Paxton campaign in Texas has released an ad featuring an AI-generated James Talarico. The statements in the ad are based on positions and comments attributed to Talarico — but that's not actually Talarico standing there delivering those lines.
That's where we have a problem.
If campaigns normalize realistic AI versions of candidates, how long before voters can't tell what's real? And once voters stop believing their own eyes and ears, that's a much bigger problem than one political ad.
🌶️ TRUMP WANTS TO RENAME NEW MEXICO?!
Yes, this happened. President Trump floated the idea of changing New Mexico to “New America,” and New Mexico's political leaders quickly responded.
We have a slightly different reaction: Guys. He's trolling you.
Nobody is actually renaming New Mexico. Meanwhile, our state has plenty of REAL problems that deserve the attention of our elected officials.We break down the reaction — and why politicians continue taking the bait.
---
| [STREAM NOW](https://us.list-manage.com/rinMrlzOOnK?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
---
| |

📺 HAALAND AND HULL HAVE NEW ADS
We finally have new campaign ads from both Deb Haaland and Gregg Hull in the New Mexico governor's race. And we're critiquing both of them.Haaland's ad surprised us with an incredibly dark portrayal of life in New Mexico: stretching meals, battling for homes and struggling to get by.
Gregg Hull takes a much more optimistic approach — but his ad is only 15 seconds long. Our take? He has a compelling story. Give voters enough time to hear it.
And yes, we're conservatives. But we're not going to tell you a Republican ad is great when we don't think it is. That's not what this show is.
---
| [STREAM NOW](https://us.list-manage.com/ve76sRlUb9v?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
---
| |

🇺🇸 WE WILL NEVER FORGET
Friday marks another anniversary of September 11, 2001.
Mark and Krysty share their memories of that morning — where they were, who they called and the moment they realized America was under attack. Mark also remembers something almost unimaginable today: flying home the NIGHT BEFORE 9/11 with the cockpit door open.
Then we share an incredible story from actor James Woods.A month before the attacks, Woods was on a flight when four men caught his attention. Their behavior concerned him enough that he alerted the flight crew and said he believed they might be preparing to hijack the plane. After September 11, he called the FBI. What happened next is remarkable.
For those of us who remember that day, we have a responsibility to make sure our children understand it too. We can remember the evil that occurred without living in fear — and remember something else that happened afterward:For a brief moment, America came together.
We'd love to see some of that again.

And this is how the President of the United States chose to talk about it. I am beyond horrified to say the least. Whatever disagreements we have about foreign policy, there should be nothing partisan about recognizing the enormous weight of sending Americans into harm’s way or honoring the lives of those who do not come home. [_**And if you’re as horrified as I am, I’m asking you to help me do something about it. Chip in $10, $25, or whatever you can today to help us take back the House and restore an actual check on this administration.**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138970940/645783606/1043545852?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTM0MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwZmIxOWQ5Mi02ZmFkLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTkzM2IiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=msAuFxo5uoPZ2RWES1FdqXgYlEgNADLn9cMhHRHxku0=) Americans are already feeling the consequences of this conflict. I was 28 years old when Susan Collins first became my senator. Now I’m 58 years old, and Susan is still my senator.
#
Peter, I was 28 years old when Susan Collins first became my senator.
Now I’m 58 years old, _and Susan is still my senator._
After 30 years in Washington, she’s become a corporate puppet who does the bidding of her billionaire donors and Donald Trump – she’s voted with him 96% of the time.
Mainers are sick and tired of her broken promises and her fake concern. But being in the Senate for half of my entire life means every single voter is gonna know who she is when they see her name on the ballot this November.
On the other hand, I’m a logger from Allagash who started this campaign just over a month ago.
Mainers already know they don’t like Susan Collins, but they also need to know that they can get the government they deserve by voting for our campaign.
My team and I are criss-crossing this state to talk to as many folks as we can, but the fastest way to reach every Mainer between now and November is our ads.
Peter, we need these ads running on TVs across Maine if we want any shot at winning on Election Day.

Elect Max Engling ****INDIANAPOLIS, Ind.** -- Gov. Mike Braun announced a $1 million statewide media campaign in support of Max Engling's campaign for Indiana secretary of state. The investment unites the governor and the Indiana Republican Party behind a major statewide effort, with each contributing $500,000 to the campaign. The investment reflects Braun's strong support for Engling and is part of a statewide effort to make clear the choice facing Hoosier voters in the secretary of state race and highlight what's at stake this November. "Max Engling is exactly who Indiana needs running our elections, someone who will protect the integrity of every vote and put Hoosiers first, not politics first. I'm proud to put my full support behind him, and this campaign is about making sure voters across our state know what's at stake in this race," Braun said. The statewide campaign will draw clear distinctions in the race and set the record straight for Hoosier voters ahead of Election Day. "The secretary of state's office is too important to leave to chance, and Max Engling has the experience and integrity to earn Hoosiers' trust. The Indiana Republican Party is proud to stand with Gov. Braun in this effort and make sure Hoosiers understand the choice before them," Indiana Republican Party Chairwoman Lana Keesing said.### [](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-l-ftkjijd-hhlljjcji-r/)[](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-l-ftkjijd-hhlljjcji-y/)[](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-l-ftkjijd-hhlljjcji-j/)[](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-l-ftkjijd-hhlljjcji-t/)[](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-l-ftkjijd-hhlljjcji-i/)[](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-l-ftkjijd-hhlljjcji-d/) ** PAID FOR BY THE INDIANA REPUBLICAN STATE COMMITTEE. ****NOT AUTHORIZED BY ANY CANDIDATE OR CANDIDATE'S COMMITTEE. ****WWW.INDIANA.GOP.** | Indiana Republican State Committee 101 W.
